project.name: proposal_orchestrator
project.description: A DAG-driven orchestration engine that transforms programme rules, call-specific constraints, and project data into evaluator-oriented Horizon Europe proposal deliverables. It enforces an eight-phase workflow with mandatory quality gates, constitutional compliance checks, and full traceability from source documents to final proposal text.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package root for the out-of-band evaluation and integrity harness; re-exports the E1 substrate (verdict, provenance, routing, judge, report, calibration, gold set) and documents the enforced one-way dependency boundary in which harness may import runner but never the reverse.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel using an explicit __all__ re-export surface; the module docstring is the architectural contract that keeps the harness out of the runtime DAG.

nodes.name: blind_assessment.py
nodes.summary: Candidate-bound blind pre-evaluation lane: materialises a candidate from section artifacts or a dev-graph document, enforces a leakage guard, grades each criterion cell with the pinned non-drafter assessor, and writes a report bound to the candidate hash, profile version and assessor pin.

nodes.name: calibration.py
nodes.summary: Judge-reliability calibration (E1.5): measures the pinned judge's precision and recall against a human-labeled faithfulness gold set and turns the result into a graduation decision that keeps every harness metric advisory until a fresh, applicable, above-threshold calibration exists.

nodes.name: claim_ledger.py
nodes.summary: Escaped-claim detector (E3): decomposes section prose into atomic assertions with an independent judge, filters them through the materiality classifier, and matches the material remainder by meaning against the section's claim ledger to surface facts asserted without any claim_id.

nodes.name: _common.py
nodes.summary: Shared bootstrap for the harness module commands: resolves the repo root anchored on this file and loads .env.harness from main() rather than at import, so importing a command never mutates os.environ.

nodes.name: resolve_document
nodes.summary: Resolves a user-supplied document reference to a dev-graph node id, accepting either a node id or a document id that has exactly one current version.

nodes.name: assert_no_leakage
nodes.summary: Leakage guard over a built blind package: raises LeakageError naming the offending items when any evidence item carries a tag the blind view policy forbids.

nodes.name: materialise_candidate
nodes.summary: Writes a blind evidence package out as a candidate directory of section artifacts under the output root, so the assessor is only ever constructed against materialised, leakage-checked content.

nodes.name: build_blind_evidence
nodes.summary: Builds the blind evidence for a dev-graph document under the blind pre-evaluation view policy and runs the leakage guard before anything is written.

nodes.name: load_candidate
nodes.summary: Loads a candidate directory into a Candidate object, parsing each section artifact and computing the formatting-invariant content hash that binds every downstream verdict.

nodes.name: _check_intake
nodes.summary: Validates an ESR intake record's purpose and availability, refusing an intake declared for anything other than a blind assessment.

nodes.name: assess_candidate
nodes.summary: Core assessment loop: grades every criterion-to-section cell of the profile with the pinned assessor, labels the report SCOPE_PARTIAL when profile-required sections are missing, and refuses a candidate holding none of them.

nodes.name: write_report
nodes.summary: Serializes a blind assessment report to the next free numbered path under the report directory.

nodes.name: load_report
nodes.summary: Rehydrates a persisted report and re-binds it to the candidate on disk, raising CandidateHashMismatch naming both hashes when the candidate has changed.

nodes.name: render_report
nodes.summary: Renders a blind assessment report as an ASCII-safe human-readable text block with the per-cell verdicts and scope labelling.

nodes.name: ReviewTask
nodes.summary: Describes one review task and whether it is blind, validating in __post_init__ that a blind task carries a coherent view policy.

nodes.name: BlindCell
nodes.summary: One graded (criterion, section) cell of a blind assessment, carrying the verdict plus the candidate hash, profile version and assessor pin that bind it.

nodes.name: BlindAssessmentReport
nodes.summary: The bound blind assessment report: cells, scope label, missing sections and the binding triple, with a summary view and a serializable form.

nodes.name: confusion_from_labels
nodes.summary: Builds a confusion matrix from paired human gold labels and judge predictions, taking supported as the positive class.

nodes.name: calibrate
nodes.summary: Computes a calibration report from already-collected judge predictions over a gold set, recording the judge pin alongside precision and recall.

nodes.name: calibrate_with_judge
nodes.summary: Runs the pinned judge over every gold pair and calibrates on the results, pairing each prediction with its human label.

nodes.name: graduation_for
nodes.summary: Decides whether a metric may graduate from advisory to gating: returns advisory unless a fresh calibration exists for the exact judge pin and clears the threshold, treating an uncomputable score as a failure.

nodes.name: ConfusionMatrix
nodes.summary: Immutable confusion matrix with derived precision, recall, F1, accuracy and gap-detection recall, each returning None rather than a pass when undefined.

nodes.name: GraduationThreshold
nodes.summary: The precision/recall bar a calibration must clear before a metric may gate, validated on construction.

nodes.name: CalibrationReport
nodes.summary: A calibration result bound to the judge pin and gold-set hash it was measured on, with applies_to and meets predicates.

nodes.name: CalibrationLog
nodes.summary: Append-only JSONL log of calibration runs with a latest_for lookup by judge pin.

nodes.name: load_section_prose
nodes.summary: Loads a Tier-5 section's sub-section prose from disk into the typed prose surface the decomposer consumes.

nodes.name: chunk_prose
nodes.summary: Chunks section prose deterministically on whole-paragraph boundaries so the decomposition is reproducible and no sentence is split across chunks.

nodes.name: parse_assertions_payload
nodes.summary: Parses the judge's decomposition response into atomic assertions, failing rather than repairing a malformed payload.

nodes.name: decompose_chunk
nodes.summary: Asks the independent judge to decompose one prose chunk exhaustively into atomic assertions, with no importance filtering.

nodes.name: dedup_assertions
nodes.summary: Deduplicates decomposed assertions by normalized text so repeated prose does not inflate the escaped-claim count.

nodes.name: dedup_ledger_claims
nodes.summary: Deduplicates ledger claim records by meaning rather than claim_id, because real ledgers repeat ids across drafting blocks.

nodes.name: lexical_shortlist
nodes.summary: Builds a token-overlap shortlist of candidate ledger claims for an assertion, bounding how many pairs reach the judge.

nodes.name: build_coverage_prompt
nodes.summary: Renders the prompt asking the judge which shortlisted ledger claim, if any, covers an assertion by meaning.

nodes.name: extract_covered_by
nodes.summary: Extracts the covering claim reference from the judge's coverage response, treating an unparseable answer as unjudgeable.

nodes.name: judge_assertion_covered_by
nodes.summary: Runs one assertion against its shortlist through the judge and returns the coverage outcome.

nodes.name: match_assertion
nodes.summary: Matches one material assertion against the section's ledger: shortlist, judge, and classify the result as covered, escaped or unjudgeable.

nodes.name: evaluate_ledger_completeness
nodes.summary: End-to-end E3 evaluation: chunk and decompose the prose, classify materiality, match every material assertion against the ledger, and assemble the completeness result with escaped, covered, non-material and unjudgeable partitions.

nodes.name: AssertionFinding
nodes.summary: One assertion's outcome against the ledger, exposing whether it is a hard finding and the flag that surfaces it to a human.

nodes.name: LedgerCompletenessResult
nodes.summary: Aggregate E3 result partitioning assertions into escaped, covered, non-material and unjudgeable sets, with outcome counts, a materiality note and a report builder.

nodes.name: load_harness_env
nodes.summary: Loads .env.harness into os.environ from a command's main(), anchored on the repo root so the commands work from any working directory.

nodes.name: blind_assessment.py
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point for the blind assessment lane: assesses one candidate directory or dev-graph document against a pre-evaluation profile, or re-binds a persisted report to the candidate on disk and rejects it when the candidate changed.

nodes.name: faithfulness_calibration.py
nodes.summary: Turnkey, resumable runner for the E1.5 faithfulness calibration: judges every gold-set pair through a paced/retrying backend, checkpoints predictions per pair, salvages verdicts from malformed judge JSON, and writes a decision-log draft with the graduation outcome.

nodes.name: freeze_grounding_baselines.py
nodes.summary: Freezes the judge half of the E4 regression golden set section by section, injecting a single paced and retrying backend choke point so a rate-limited judge (TPM/RPM caps, 429s) cannot abort the run; already frozen sections are skipped on re-run.

nodes.name: rubric_grading_run.py
nodes.summary: Drives the E5 rubric grid over the committed Part B sections under an explicit judge budget: computes and records the full call/token plan before the first judge call, checkpoints every grid cell for multi-day resume, and freezes both the grid report and the E4 rubric-lane baseline.

nodes.name: evidence_pack.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic evidence-pack builder that keeps each rubric judge call inside the token budget: selects the prose spans and claim-ledger entries bearing on an expectation by versioned term matching and anchor sub-section bonuses, then records every excluded item and the reason it was dropped.

nodes.name: _parser
nodes.summary: Builds the argparse parser for the assess and verify sub-commands and their candidate, document, profile and output options.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command entry point: resolves the candidate (directory or dev-graph document), constructs the pinned assessor, writes or verifies a bound report, and maps the outcome onto distinct exit codes.

nodes.name: _run
nodes.summary: Judges the outstanding gold pairs with per-pair checkpointing, salvaging a verdict from malformed judge JSON and excluding an unrecoverable pair rather than aborting the run.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Calibration run entry point: loads the gold set and checkpoint, paces the judge calls, computes precision and recall, applies the graduation threshold and writes the decision-log draft.

nodes.name: build_paced_judge
nodes.summary: Constructs the pinned judge wrapped in the paced, retrying backend so every judge call in the freeze passes through one rate-limiting choke point.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Freeze entry point: iterates the committed sections, skips any already frozen under the current judge pin, and writes one grounding baseline per section with resume on interruption.

nodes.name: PacedRetryingBackend
nodes.summary: Backend wrapper that paces every judge call under a TPM/RPM budget using the backend's real token usage and retries the provider's own retryable errors with exponential backoff, honouring a try-again hint.

nodes.name: compute_budget_plan
nodes.summary: Computes the full offline call and token plan for the grid (expectations by mapped sections by N>=3, coverage plus grounding, cross-pack claim dedup) and records it before the first judge call, making a multi-day resume explicit rather than silently shrinking the panel.

nodes.name: run_meta
nodes.summary: Assembles the run metadata block (judge pin, profile version, rubric fingerprint, timestamps) stamped onto every artifact the run writes.

nodes.name: load_checkpoint
nodes.summary: Loads the per-cell checkpoint and verdict cache, validating it against the current run plan so a stale checkpoint cannot be silently resumed.

nodes.name: run_grading
nodes.summary: Grades the grid cell by cell within the recorded budget, persisting the checkpoint after each cell and stopping cleanly with BudgetStop when the plan's allowance is exhausted.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Run entry point: loads the profile bundle, writes the budget plan, optionally stops at plan-only, grades with resume, then freezes the grid report and the E4 rubric-lane baseline.

nodes.name: _load_sub_sections
nodes.summary: Reads a Tier-5 section artifact's sub-sections into the ordered prose surface the pack builder selects spans from.

nodes.name: _fill_budget
nodes.summary: Greedily fills the pack to the token ceiling in score order and records every item it had to leave out together with the reason.

nodes.name: build_evidence_pack
nodes.summary: Builds the deterministic evidence pack for one (expectation, section) pair: term-matches and anchor-bonuses candidate prose spans and claims, fills the token budget, and attaches the full exclusion record.

nodes.name: ProseSpan
nodes.summary: One selectable paragraph of section prose with its matched terms, render form and token estimate.

nodes.name: PackClaim
nodes.summary: One selectable claim-ledger entry with its matched terms, render form and token estimate.

nodes.name: ExcludedItem
nodes.summary: A record of one item the budget fill dropped and why, so a capped pack never reads as an empty section.

nodes.name: EvidencePack
nodes.summary: The assembled, budget-bounded evidence pack handed to one judge call, with its render, token estimate and serializable form.

nodes.name: expectation_coverage.py
nodes.summary: Coverage-axis grader (E5c): asks the judge, over one evidence pack, whether the section substantively addresses a profile evaluator expectation, routing the property through the deterministic-first router and requiring an N>=3 majority panel with mandatory provenance.

nodes.name: expectation_grounding.py
nodes.summary: Grounding-axis grader (E5d): aggregates the status-aware faithfulness verdicts for the claims in an evidence pack into a per-expectation grounding rate and weakest-link claim, contributing no faithfulness judgment of its own and reusing existing verdicts under a fail-closed consistency check.

nodes.name: expectations.py
nodes.summary: Expectation substrate loader (E5a): derives the applicable evaluator expectation set from the Tier-2A registry by parsing [OPTION for ...] applicability tags under the profile's grammar, then requires the result to reproduce the profile scorecard exactly and fails closed on any divergence.

nodes.name: faithfulness.py
nodes.summary: The atomic faithfulness primitive: renders the bounded prompt asking whether a cited source supports one claim and reads back a boolean verdict, so calibration and the E2 metric ask the judge exactly the question the gold set is labeled against.

nodes.name: gold_set.py
nodes.summary: Human-labeled faithfulness gold set: the (claim, source_ref, supported?) data model, a fail-closed loader that refuses unlabeled pairs, a content hash, and a deterministic seeder that emits unlabeled templates from a Phase-8 section's claim statuses without ever fabricating the human label.

nodes.name: grade_coverage
nodes.summary: Grades the coverage axis for one expectation and pack: routes the property through the deterministic-first router, runs an N>=3 majority panel, and refuses a judge without an attached provenance log.

nodes.name: grade_expectation
nodes.summary: Thin orchestration that builds the expectation's evidence pack and grades coverage over it, the single call every grid cell goes through.

nodes.name: CoverageGrade
nodes.summary: The coverage-axis result for one (expectation, section) cell, keeping the judge's raw majority alongside the clean pass bit and the routing decision.

nodes.name: _check_reused_finding
nodes.summary: Fail-closed consistency check on a reused faithfulness verdict, refusing a stale result that would silently re-attribute a verdict to a different claim.

nodes.name: derive_grounding
nodes.summary: Derives the grounding grade for one expectation by aggregating per-claim faithfulness verdicts over the pack's claims, reusing supplied verdicts where valid and delegating any remaining claim to the E2 evaluator.

nodes.name: derive_expectation_grounding
nodes.summary: Builds the expectation's evidence pack and derives its grounding grade, the grounding-axis counterpart of grade_expectation.

nodes.name: ClaimGroundingRow
nodes.summary: One claim's contribution to an expectation's grounding grade, carrying its status, severity and whether it is grounded.

nodes.name: GroundingGrade
nodes.summary: The grounding-axis result for one cell: per-status row partitions, the confirmed grounding rate, the weakest-link claim and the integrity failures.

nodes.name: parse_option_tag
nodes.summary: Parses an [OPTION for ...] applicability tag under the profile's tag grammar into a structured option tag, rejecting an unrecognised prefix or variant.

nodes.name: _scorecard_text_matches
nodes.summary: Compares a registry row's expectation text against a scorecard aspect's verbatim text under the normalization the reproduction check allows.

nodes.name: _registry_rows
nodes.summary: Reads the Tier-2A evaluator expectation registry rows for the profile's instrument type.

nodes.name: _scorecard_entries
nodes.summary: Parses the profile's scorecard file into the binding, human-verified aspect entries that the applicability filter must reproduce.

nodes.name: _resolve_tag
nodes.summary: Resolves a registry row's applicability tag to applicable, excluded or absent for the profile's instrument variant.

nodes.name: load_expectation_substrate
nodes.summary: Loads the E5a substrate: filters the registry by applicability tag, requires the result to reproduce the scorecard exactly, maps every expectation to its criterion and sections, and raises rather than grading a silent subset.

nodes.name: ExpectationSubstrate
nodes.summary: The loaded expectation set with lookups by stable expectation key and by criterion.

nodes.name: build_claim_user_prompt
nodes.summary: Renders the user half of the faithfulness prompt for one (claim, source) pair.

nodes.name: build_faithfulness_prompt
nodes.summary: Renders the full (system, user) faithfulness prompt pair that asks the single bounded question whether the source supports the claim.

nodes.name: resolve_source_text
nodes.summary: Resolves a pair's source_ref to the source text the judge is shown, failing when the reference cannot be resolved.

nodes.name: judge_pair_supported
nodes.summary: Asks the judge the atomic faithfulness question about one pair and returns the boolean verdict plus its provenance.

nodes.name: _iter_raw_pairs
nodes.summary: Iterates the raw pair objects out of a gold-set file, tolerating both the list and keyed container shapes.

nodes.name: load_gold_set
nodes.summary: Fail-closed gold-set loader that refuses an unlabeled pair, because a judge cannot be characterized against labels that do not exist.

nodes.name: gold_set_hash
nodes.summary: Content hash over the gold set, so a calibration is provably bound to the exact label set it was measured on.

nodes.name: seed_pairs_from_claim_statuses
nodes.summary: Deterministically draws candidate pairs from a Phase-8 section's claim statuses and emits unlabeled templates, never fabricating the human label.

nodes.name: _allocate
nodes.summary: Allocates the seed quota across status classes with even spacing so the template is not skewed toward one status.

nodes.name: GoldPair
nodes.summary: One (claim, source_ref, human label) gold triple, validated on construction, with labeled/unlabeled predicates and round-trip serialization.

nodes.name: GoldSet
nodes.summary: An iterable collection of gold pairs with labeled/unlabeled partitions and a require_fully_labeled guard for calibration use.

nodes.name: jsonl_log.py
nodes.summary: Shared append-only JSONL log base: seeds from any pre-existing file, mirrors records in memory, and atomically re-serializes the whole file on every append so a reader never sees a torn line.

nodes.name: judge.py
nodes.summary: The independent judge: a pinned, temperature-zero, non-drafter model over the OpenAI-compatible transport that enforces grader/generator independence, refuses to silently repair a malformed response, and logs provenance for every verdict before returning it.
nodes.languageNotes: Dependency injection by backend callable keeps the judge testable with no network; the drafter-model blocklist and transport check are enforced in JudgeConfig construction rather than at call time.

nodes.name: ledger_granularity.py
nodes.summary: Offline, judge-free measurement of the claim-ledger granularity gap between the graph-sourced sections and the drafter-era ledgers preserved in the E4 golden baselines, verifying the prose is byte-identical so the cardinality deficit is exact rather than confounded by content drift.

nodes.name: materiality.py
nodes.summary: The CLAUDE.md section 10.5 materiality classifier and its ledger-anchored calibration: separates a material, attributable claim from framing and definitional prose, seeding positives from the engine's own claim ledger and leaving negative candidates unlabeled for a human.

nodes.name: profile.py
nodes.summary: Pre-evaluation profile parser: turns the versioned configuration bundle (instrument type, option-tag grammar, criterion-to-section map, scorecard and rubric-set pins) into typed objects fail-closed, and owns the version arithmetic that hashes the profile over its bundled component pins.

nodes.name: JsonlLog
nodes.summary: Append-only JSONL log base that seeds from an existing file, mirrors records in memory, and atomically rewrites the file on every append so a reader never sees a torn line.

nodes.name: resolve_judge_config
nodes.summary: Resolves the judge configuration from the environment, rejecting any drafter model and the claude_cli transport so grader/generator independence holds structurally.

nodes.name: _verdict_from_payload
nodes.summary: Turns a parsed judge response into a typed Inferred verdict, raising a JudgeResponseError rather than repairing a malformed payload.

nodes.name: JudgeConfig
nodes.summary: The pinned judge configuration (model, version, transport, temperature) validated on construction to exclude drafter models.

nodes.name: Judge
nodes.summary: The injectable judge: invokes the pinned non-drafter model over the configured backend, returns typed Inferred verdicts, runs N>=3 majority panels, and logs provenance before returning.

nodes.name: measure_section
nodes.summary: Measures one section's ledger granularity against its drafter-era baseline, verifying the prose is byte-identical per sub-section before reporting the claim-cardinality deficit.

nodes.name: run_e4_regression
nodes.summary: Runs the deterministic E4 golden-set comparison over the measured sections to supply the baseline side of the granularity measurement.

nodes.name: build_report
nodes.summary: Assembles the LG-1 measurement report from the per-section measurements and the regression comparison.

nodes.name: _print_summary
nodes.summary: Prints the LG-1 measurement summary to the console for the human reading the result.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point for the offline, judge-free LG-1 measurement run.

nodes.name: seed_materiality_positives
nodes.summary: Turns real claim_summary values from the engine's own ledger into auto-labeled positive materiality examples, using the engine's enumeration rather than a fabricated gold label.

nodes.name: seed_negative_candidates
nodes.summary: Seeds framing, transition and definitional prose spans as unlabeled negative candidates for a human to label.

nodes.name: load_materiality_set
nodes.summary: Fail-closed loader for the materiality example set used to calibrate the classifier.

nodes.name: classify_materiality
nodes.summary: Runs the section 10.5 materiality classifier over one assertion, quoting the constitutional text verbatim in the prompt and returning an Inferred verdict.

nodes.name: calibrate_materiality
nodes.summary: Measures the materiality classifier's precision and recall against the labeled example set and records the result bound to the judge pin.

nodes.name: MaterialityExample
nodes.summary: One materiality example (text plus optional human label) with labeled predicate and round-trip serialization.

nodes.name: MaterialityCalibration
nodes.summary: A materiality calibration result bound to the judge pin and example set, exposing whether it had negatives to measure against.

nodes.name: _parse_grammar
nodes.summary: Parses the profile's option-tag grammar (applicable variant, known variants, prefix vocabulary) fail-closed.

nodes.name: _parse_criteria
nodes.summary: Parses the profile's criterion specs and their criterion-to-section mapping.

nodes.name: parse_profile
nodes.summary: Parses a pre-evaluation profile document into typed objects, cross-checking that the declared scorecard and rubric-set IDs and versions match the files actually loaded.

nodes.name: parse_scoring
nodes.summary: Parses the profile's scoring block (scale, weights, thresholds) with numeric validation.

nodes.name: PreEvaluationProfile
nodes.summary: The versioned configuration bundle the harness grades under: instrument spec, tag grammar, criterion-to-section map, scorecard and rubric-set pins, with criterion and section lookups.

nodes.name: provenance.py
nodes.summary: Judge-verdict provenance: a stable content hash over the (system, user) prompt pair, an immutable record carrying judge model, version, prompt hash, score and rationale that cannot be built with a non-Inferred evidence type, and an append-only JSONL sink.

nodes.name: regression.py
nodes.summary: Regression golden set (E4): freezes each Tier-5 section's claim ledger, per-sub-section prose hashes and canonical artifact hash as a baseline, then diffs a current artifact against it and classifies lost claims, status weakenings and source-ref swaps as breaking regressions; also owns the grounding and rubric baselines.

nodes.name: report.py
nodes.summary: The harness's terminal artifact: aggregates a metric's verdicts and routing decisions into one serializable report that is advisory by construction, with no method that could yield a gate pass/fail for the scheduler.

nodes.name: routing.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic-first routing authority: refuses to judge any property whose key names a deterministic predicate the runtime actually dispatches, while deliberately treating the in-run semantic registry as non-deterministic so the independent judge may legitimately re-check it.

nodes.name: rubric.py
nodes.summary: Contradiction detector and rubric grid report (E5e): deterministically combines the coverage and grounding axes into a 2x2 grid whose headline cell is high coverage with weak grounding, carrying no blended score anywhere so that cell can never be averaged away; also renders the report and owns the grading CLI.

nodes.name: ProvenanceRecord
nodes.summary: The immutable five-field provenance record for a judge verdict, which cannot be constructed with a non-Inferred evidence type, plus construction from a verdict.

nodes.name: ProvenanceLog
nodes.summary: Append-only JSONL sink for provenance records, written atomically so Python owns every write.

nodes.name: freeze_section_fingerprint
nodes.summary: Snapshots a section's claim ledger matched by meaning, its per-sub-section prose hashes and a canonical whole-artifact hash as the deterministic E4 baseline.

nodes.name: load_golden_set
nodes.summary: Loads the frozen golden-set fingerprints for every baselined section.

nodes.name: _diff_ledger
nodes.summary: Diffs a current claim ledger against a frozen one by meaning, classifying removed claims, status weakenings and source-ref swaps as breaking and additions as advisory.

nodes.name: _diff_prose
nodes.summary: Diffs per-sub-section prose hashes and calls out prose that changed while the ledger did not, the escaped-claim risk zone.

nodes.name: compare_section
nodes.summary: Compares one current section artifact against its frozen fingerprint and returns the classified regression result.

nodes.name: compare_to_golden_set
nodes.summary: Compares every section in the golden set against the current artifacts and aggregates the per-section results into one regression report.

nodes.name: _judge_section
nodes.summary: Runs the status-aware faithfulness evaluation over one section to produce the judge-lane input for a grounding baseline.

nodes.name: freeze_section_grounding
nodes.summary: Freezes a section's judge-lane grounding baseline under the current judge pin.

nodes.name: compare_section_grounding
nodes.summary: Compares a section's current grounding verdicts against its frozen baseline and reports the invariance violations.

nodes.name: _require_report
nodes.summary: Validates that a rubric report has the shape the baseline freeze requires, failing rather than freezing a partial grid.

nodes.name: freeze_rubric_baseline
nodes.summary: Freezes an E5 rubric grid report as the E4 rubric-lane baseline, embedding the run's budget accounting.

nodes.name: compare_rubric_baseline
nodes.summary: Diffs a current rubric grid against the frozen baseline cell by cell, classifying axis-value and contradiction-kind changes.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Regression CLI entry point for the deterministic lane: freeze or check the section golden set and the rubric baseline.

nodes.name: LedgerEntry
nodes.summary: One frozen ledger claim identified by meaning - summary, status and source_ref - never by bare claim_id, with round-trip serialization.

nodes.name: SubSectionFingerprint
nodes.summary: The frozen prose hash for one sub-section, built from its prose and serializable both ways.

nodes.name: SectionFingerprint
nodes.summary: A section's complete frozen baseline: ledger entries, sub-section prose hashes, status counts, confirmed share and canonical artifact hash.

nodes.name: RegressionFinding
nodes.summary: One classified regression finding with its breaking flag.

nodes.name: SectionRegressionResult
nodes.summary: Per-section regression outcome exposing whether the section regressed and which findings are breaking.

nodes.name: RegressionReport
nodes.summary: The aggregate E4 regression report across sections, with a regressed predicate and a human summary.

nodes.name: build_report
nodes.summary: Builds the advisory harness report from a metric's verdicts and routing decisions.

nodes.name: HarnessReport
nodes.summary: The harness's terminal report object, advisory by construction - always advisory, never blocking, with no gate pass/fail accessor the scheduler could consume.

nodes.name: route
nodes.summary: Routes a named property: refuses to judge it when the key names a deterministic predicate the runtime dispatches, otherwise returns a decision permitting the judge in the semantic gap.

nodes.name: RoutingDecision
nodes.summary: The recorded routing decision for one property, attached to every grade so the deterministic-first rule is auditable.

nodes.name: load_spine_registry
nodes.summary: Loads the spine-fact registry (researcher, host, call and related facts) used to annotate a grid cell with the unconfirmed facts its claims rest on.

nodes.name: _weak_grounding_explanation
nodes.summary: Builds the human-readable explanation of why a cell's grounding is weak, naming the weakest-link claim and any unconfirmed spine facts behind it.

nodes.name: combine_axes
nodes.summary: Deterministic arithmetic combining one coverage grade and one grounding grade into a grid cell, using the judge's raw majority for the covered axis so a truncated pack cannot hide the headline contradiction.

nodes.name: build_rubric_report
nodes.summary: Assembles the rubric grid report from the combined cells and the run metadata.

nodes.name: render_report
nodes.summary: Renders the rubric grid as text with the two axes printed side by side and no blended score anywhere.

nodes.name: grade_all
nodes.summary: Grades the full grid: for every applicable expectation and mapped section, derives both axes and combines them into a cell.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Rubric CLI entry point that re-renders or regrades the E5 grid report.

nodes.name: SpineFact
nodes.summary: One spine fact with its effective status and an unconfirmed predicate, used to explain weak grounding.

nodes.name: SpineRegistry
nodes.summary: The loaded spine-fact registry with lookups by id, by claim and over the unconfirmed subset.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.summary: A recorded high-coverage / weak-grounding contradiction - the grid's headline cell.

nodes.name: ExpectationCell
nodes.summary: One grid cell carrying both axes separately, their covered and grounded bits, and the clean-pass override state.

nodes.name: RubricReport
nodes.summary: The E5 grid report, structurally carrying no blended field so the contradiction cell can never be averaged away.

nodes.name: rubrics.py
nodes.summary: Rubric set loader (E5b): parses the profile's versioned rubric file, cross-checks every rubric's expectation text byte-for-byte against the scorecard aspect and the E5a substrate, fails closed on divergence, and renders and hashes the pinned (system, user) rubric prompt pair.

nodes.name: status_calibration.py
nodes.summary: Claim-status calibration (E3): detects label drift in both directions, reusing E2 verdicts to find overclaimed confirmed claims as hard findings and asking the confirmed-bar question counterfactually to flag underclaimed inferred claims as soft advisory drift.

nodes.name: status_faithfulness.py
nodes.summary: Status-aware faithfulness (E2), the gap-masked-as-confirmed detector: partitions Tier-5 claims by status and judges each against the standard its status claims - confirmed strictly against its source_ref, assumed against the operator-declared value, inferred softly - and owns the baseline freeze and invariance comparison.
nodes.languageNotes: The source_ref mini-grammar parser (segments, parentheticals, top-level splitting) is a hand-rolled recursive-descent reader over a free-text citation field.

nodes.name: verdict.py
nodes.summary: Judge verdict vocabulary: pure types that stamp every verdict with the section 12.2 status Inferred and make a Confirmed verdict impossible to construct, plus the N>=3 majority-vote scaffold required wherever a score will inform a decision.
nodes.languageNotes: A deliberately pure module - no I/O, no network - so the verdict invariants are enforced in frozen dataclass __post_init__ validation.

nodes.name: working_assumptions.py
nodes.summary: Shared reader for the Tier 3 working_assumptions.json declaration file, the single mechanism by which a human operator turns an honest block into a conscious green; one parse serves both the unit-cost budget gate (by declared key) and the claim layer's W1 predicate (by checklist ref).

nodes.name: _parse_rubric
nodes.summary: Parses one rubric entry (text, steps, pass threshold, selection terms, anchor sub-sections) from the profile's rubric-set file.

nodes.name: load_rubric_set
nodes.summary: Loads and cross-checks the rubric set against the E5a substrate and the scorecard, failing closed on a missing or extra rubric, a paraphrased expectation text, a criterion mismatch or a stale scorecard version.

nodes.name: load_profile_bundle
nodes.summary: Loads the full profile bundle - profile document, expectation substrate, rubric set and scoring - as one version-consistent unit.

nodes.name: build_pack_for
nodes.summary: Builds the evidence pack for one rubric and section using the rubric's declared selection terms and anchor sub-sections.

nodes.name: build_rubric_system_prompt
nodes.summary: Renders the system half of the integrity-framed rubric prompt, which asks whether the section addresses and grounds the expectation rather than whether the prose is good.

nodes.name: build_rubric_user_prompt
nodes.summary: Renders the user half of the rubric prompt over the evidence pack.

nodes.name: Rubric
nodes.summary: One versioned rubric: expectation text traceable byte-for-byte to a scorecard aspect, evaluation steps, pass threshold and deterministic selection basis.

nodes.name: RubricSet
nodes.summary: The loaded rubric set with lookup by expectation key and a content fingerprint that moves whenever a rubric changes.

nodes.name: _drift_from_e2_finding
nodes.summary: Reinterprets an existing E2 integrity finding as an overclaimed status-drift finding, spending no additional judge calls on the confirmed direction.

nodes.name: evaluate_status_calibration
nodes.summary: Evaluates status drift in both directions: reuses E2 verdicts for overclaimed confirmed claims as hard findings and asks the confirmed-bar question counterfactually over inferred claims to flag soft underclaimed drift.

nodes.name: ClaimDrift
nodes.summary: One claim's status-drift finding with its direction, hard/soft classification and flag.

nodes.name: StatusCalibrationResult
nodes.summary: The aggregate status-calibration result partitioning claims into overclaimed, underclaimed and unverifiable with drift counts and a report builder.

nodes.name: load_section_claims
nodes.summary: Loads a Tier-5 section's validation_status claim entries into the typed claim surface E2 judges.

nodes.name: build_faithfulness_prompt_for_status
nodes.summary: Renders the status-specific faithfulness prompt - strict against the source for confirmed, against the operator-declared value for assumed, softer for inferred.

nodes.name: _parse_segment
nodes.summary: Parses one segment of a claim's source_ref citation string into its structured parts.

nodes.name: _split_top_level
nodes.summary: Splits a source_ref string on top-level separators while respecting nested parentheses and brackets.

nodes.name: _parse_source_segments
nodes.summary: Parses a full source_ref field into its ordered list of structured citation segments.

nodes.name: _render_text
nodes.summary: Renders a resolved source document region into the bounded text the judge is shown.

nodes.name: resolve_claim_source_text
nodes.summary: Resolves a claim's source_ref to the actual source text, walking the parsed segments and locating the cited region by id or hint tokens.

nodes.name: _render_segment
nodes.summary: Renders one resolved citation segment into its judge-facing text form.

nodes.name: resolve_assumed_declared_text
nodes.summary: Resolves an assumed claim's operator-declared value from working_assumptions.json, the text an assumed claim is judged against instead of a source.

nodes.name: meets_bar
nodes.summary: Decides whether a judge verdict clears the bar the claim's status promises, the single public owner of the status-specific threshold.

nodes.name: _judge_claim
nodes.summary: Runs one claim's status-specific faithfulness question through the judge and returns the typed verdict.

nodes.name: evaluate_claim
nodes.summary: Public per-claim E2 entry point: resolves the claim's comparison text, judges it against its status bar and returns the faithfulness verdict with severity.

nodes.name: _evaluate_claim_routed
nodes.summary: Routes one claim through the deterministic-first router before judging and records the routing decision on the verdict.

nodes.name: evaluate_status_aware_faithfulness
nodes.summary: Evaluates a whole section: partitions claims by status, judges each under its own bar and aggregates the verdicts into the E2 result with severity counts.

nodes.name: compare_to_baseline
nodes.summary: Compares current per-claim grounding verdicts against a frozen baseline and reports the invariance violations, classifying a lost grounding as breaking.

nodes.name: SectionClaim
nodes.summary: One Tier-5 claim with its status, summary and source_ref, validated on construction and keyed by meaning rather than claim_id.

nodes.name: StatusPolicy
nodes.summary: The per-status faithfulness policy - what a claim of this status is judged against and at what bar.

nodes.name: ClaimFaithfulness
nodes.summary: One claim's E2 verdict with its severity, pass bit, score and hard-finding classification.

nodes.name: StatusFaithfulnessResult
nodes.summary: The aggregate E2 result for a section: verdicts partitioned by status, flagged and integrity findings, severity counts and a report builder.

nodes.name: ClaimGroundingSnapshot
nodes.summary: A frozen per-claim grounding verdict as stored in a baseline, with round-trip serialization.

nodes.name: FaithfulnessBaseline
nodes.summary: The frozen grounding baseline for a section, bound to the judge pin it was measured under, with lookups and serialization.

nodes.name: InvarianceViolation
nodes.summary: One baseline invariance violation with its breaking classification.

nodes.name: InvarianceReport
nodes.summary: The aggregate invariance report over a baseline comparison, exposing whether the invariant held.

nodes.name: majority_vote
nodes.summary: Combines N>=3 individual verdicts into a majority verdict, validating the sample count and synthesizing a combined rationale; the scaffold required wherever a score will inform a decision.

nodes.name: _synthesize_rationale
nodes.summary: Synthesizes the combined rationale of a majority verdict from its member rationales.

nodes.name: Verdict
nodes.summary: One judge verdict, stamped Inferred on construction and impossible to build as Confirmed, so a judge score can never certify a fact.

nodes.name: MajorityVerdict
nodes.summary: The combined N>=3 majority verdict carrying its members, the combined rationale and the same Inferred stamp.

nodes.name: declared_claim_summary
nodes.summary: Returns the operator-declared value a claim's summary must equal, the shared accessor the W1 predicate and the assumption applier both read.

nodes.name: _parse_declaration
nodes.summary: Parses one working-assumption declaration fail-closed, requiring its declared value, placement and checklist reference.

nodes.name: load_working_assumptions
nodes.summary: Loads and validates Tier 3 working_assumptions.json into the single reader both the unit-cost budget gate and the claim layer consume.

nodes.name: Declaration
nodes.summary: One operator-declared working assumption: declared value, placement, checklist reference and the claim ids it backs.

nodes.name: WorkingAssumptions
nodes.summary: The parsed declaration set, resolving a declaration by key, by checklist ref, or as the surface and canonical-pack entries the budget and claim layers read.

nodes.name: assumption_applier.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic component that flips drafted claims from `unresolved` to `assumed` wherever a Tier 3 operator declaration backs them, then re-derives the section spine's overall status. Implements the constitution's mode-beta "conscious green" without inventing any claim.
nodes.languageNotes: Idempotent by construction: a second pass finds no unresolved claim left to flip and writes nothing.

nodes.name: _resolve_declaration
nodes.summary: Resolves a claim id to an operator declaration, first by declaration key and then through the unique `checklist_ref` bridge.

nodes.name: _read_json_object
nodes.summary: Reads a JSON object from disk, raising `AssumptionApplierError` on a missing or malformed artifact (fail-closed).

nodes.name: _flip_declared_claims
nodes.summary: Rewrites every `unresolved` claim backed by a declaration into an `assumed` claim carrying the declared summary and the `assumption_declared` flag.

nodes.name: apply_assumptions
nodes.summary: Component entry point: loads the working assumptions, flips the per-sub-section drafts, re-derives the spine's `overall_status`, and atomically rewrites only the touched drafts.

nodes.name: atomic_write.py
nodes.summary: Shared atomic-write helpers (temp file plus rename) that every deterministic component and exporter uses to publish canonical artifacts. Owns the canonical JSON serialisation that the byte-equal replay checks depend on.
nodes.languageNotes: Windows-safe finalisation: `os.rename` requires an absent target, so an existing file is unlinked first.

nodes.name: canonical_json_bytes
nodes.summary: Serialises an object to the canonical pretty UTF-8 JSON bytes (`indent=2, ensure_ascii=False`) that every byte-equal replay comparison uses.

nodes.name: atomic_write_json
nodes.summary: Writes an object as canonical JSON to a path atomically, creating parents and leaving no partial output on failure.

nodes.name: atomic_write_text
nodes.summary: Writes UTF-8 text to a path atomically with the same temp-file-and-rename discipline as the JSON writer.

nodes.name: atomic_write_via
nodes.summary: Atomic-write adapter for third-party writers that need a file path of their own (used by the `.docx` exporter).

nodes.name: budget_request.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic composer of the lump-sum budget request sent to the external Lump Sum Budget Planner. Every effort and cost field carries an explicit "requires external computation" sentinel, so the repository prepares the request without computing any budget figure.
nodes.languageNotes: Fails closed: a missing or malformed upstream artifact raises and writes nothing, because a partial request would be priced by the planner.

nodes.name: _wp_month_windows
nodes.summary: Derives each work package's start/end month window from the Phase 4 Gantt task spans, yielding `null` where no task exists.

nodes.name: _management_roles
nodes.summary: Lifts each partner's management roles verbatim from the Phase 6 implementation architecture.

nodes.name: _entry_ids
nodes.summary: Collects the declared identifiers of a record collection, refusing a malformed container.

nodes.name: _partner_identity
nodes.summary: Copies a partner's identity verbatim from Tier 3, halting when a country has escaped its anonymised slot.

nodes.name: compose_budget_request
nodes.summary: Composes the full budget-request payload from the call binding, WP structure, Gantt, implementation architecture and partners, stamping the external-computation sentinel on every cost field.

nodes.name: _read_json
nodes.summary: Reads one repo-relative JSON artifact, raising `BudgetRequestError` when absent or malformed.

nodes.name: derive_budget_request
nodes.summary: Component entry point: checks the instrument owns the lump-sum regime, composes the request, validates it against the interface contract, and writes it atomically.

nodes.name: claim_status.py
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for the constitution's four-value validation vocabulary and its worst-wins ordering. Pure lookups with no I/O, so both the drafter and the assumption applier derive a section's overall status identically.

nodes.name: normalize_status
nodes.summary: Maps any casing of a known status onto its canonical lowercase spelling and returns `None` for anything outside the vocabulary.

nodes.name: worst_status
nodes.summary: Returns the least-resolved status among an iterable, ignoring unknown values; an empty iterable yields `confirmed`.

nodes.name: rollup_inconsistency
nodes.summary: Detects a section whose declared `overall_status` disagrees with the worst of its per-claim statuses, naming the inconsistency for the gate.

nodes.name: decomposed_drafting.py
nodes.summary: Drafting driver that replaces one monolithic Claude call per section with one bounded call per sub-section, passing prior drafts forward as sequential context. Writes the per-sub-section drafts and the section spine that the deterministic assembler then composes.
nodes.languageNotes: The per-sub-section call sits behind an injectable `drafter` callable, so the loop, spine derivation and atomic writes are unit-testable with a fake.

nodes.name: _resolve_drafting_sub_sections
nodes.summary: Reads the section's drafting sub-sections from the instrument profile, so granularity never hardcodes an instrument literal.

nodes.name: _build_draft
nodes.summary: Drafts one sub-section through the injected drafter, handing it the criterion and the prior sub-sections as sequential context.

nodes.name: _derive_overall_status
nodes.summary: Derives the spine's overall status as the worst status over all freshly drafted per-sub-section claims.

nodes.name: _capture_raw_response
nodes.summary: Persists a drafter's raw response under the run's capture directory so a parse failure can be replayed offline.

nodes.name: _default_claude_drafter
nodes.summary: Builds the production drafter closure: assembles the bounded per-sub-section prompt, invokes the Claude runtime transport, captures the raw response and returns the parsed draft.

nodes.name: _parse_drafter_response
nodes.summary: Parses and validates a drafter response into a sub-section draft, refusing a malformed or incomplete payload rather than repairing it.

nodes.name: _read_upstream_json
nodes.summary: Reads a required upstream Tier 3/4 artifact, raising `DecomposedDraftingError` when absent.

nodes.name: source_section_extra_fields
nodes.summary: Sources the per-section extra fields (criterion, declarations, schema identity) that the assembled section artifact must carry.

nodes.name: draft_section_decomposed
nodes.summary: Entry point: resolves the sub-section set, drafts each one in order, derives the spine and atomically writes the drafts plus `section_spine.json`.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Public API barrel for the dev graph — a rebuildable operational index over the repository's authoritative records. Re-exports the snapshot builder, closed vocabularies, document import, evidence packaging, change recording, impact planning, revisions, shadow comparison and ESR intake.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package barrel: the docstring is the module's API contract, listing each re-exported entry point and the vocabulary it belongs to.

nodes.name: builder.py
nodes.summary: Builds the immutable dev-graph snapshot: reads the Tier 3 records that own project facts, derives typed nodes and edges from their declared keys, validates against the closed schema and returns a content-addressed `Snapshot`. The graph owns nothing and a rebuild from the same records is byte-identical.
nodes.languageNotes: Identity model: node id is the record's own declared key, node version is the record's content hash, and every edge references both endpoints as `{id, version}`.

nodes.name: Snapshot
nodes.summary: Immutable snapshot value object holding the canonical nodes, edges and content-derived snapshot id, with JSON round-tripping and an empty constructor.

nodes.name: _Assembler
nodes.summary: Internal accumulator that collects nodes and edges with de-duplication and per-id version tracking, then finalises them into a canonical graph.

nodes.name: canonical_graph
nodes.summary: Returns nodes and edges in their canonical sorted order, the form every snapshot id is hashed over.

nodes.name: _read_records
nodes.summary: Reads one Tier 3 record file and extracts its declared list, recording the path on every record it yields.

nodes.name: _objects
nodes.summary: Extracts a list of nested objects from a record, refusing a malformed shape with a located error.

nodes.name: _add_work_package
nodes.summary: Derives the work-package node plus its lead, objective, constraint and deliverable edges from the record's declared keys.

nodes.name: _add_verified_span
nodes.summary: Adds a `source_span` node for a claim's verified span and links the claim to both the span and its source.

nodes.name: _add_document
nodes.summary: Turns one immutable document snapshot record into its document, passage, claim and commitment nodes, stamping the document's declared tags on all of them.

nodes.name: _assemble
nodes.summary: Drives the whole build: reads every record kind in order and feeds it to the per-type node/edge derivation.

nodes.name: build_snapshot
nodes.summary: Public entry point: assembles the graph from a repository root, validates it against the closed schema and returns the immutable snapshot.

nodes.name: current_commitments
nodes.summary: Returns the commitments of current document snapshots only, skipping submitted and superseded versions.

nodes.name: superseded_versions
nodes.summary: Computes which document snapshots a later version supersedes — a fact of the whole graph rather than a per-node tag.

nodes.name: derived_from_version
nodes.summary: Reports the document snapshot a derived node (passage, claim, commitment) came from.

nodes.name: changes.py
nodes.summary: Records an operator-approved new version of one Tier 3 record while keeping the old one: archives the prior content, stores the before/after snapshots content-addressed, and writes one immutable change record carrying the pure snapshot diff.
nodes.languageNotes: On a failed after-build the record file is restored byte for byte and nothing is written — the diff distinguishes a directly changed node from one whose version only moved because a nested record changed.

nodes.name: ChangeRecord
nodes.summary: Immutable record of one approved change: both snapshot ids, both record versions and the computed change set.

nodes.name: snapshot_path
nodes.summary: Returns the content-addressed path a stored snapshot lands at.

nodes.name: store_snapshot
nodes.summary: Stores a snapshot content-addressed under the snapshots directory so the planner can read it later without rebuilding.

nodes.name: load_snapshot
nodes.summary: Loads a stored snapshot by id, refusing a missing or malformed file.

nodes.name: _archive_record
nodes.summary: Archives the current record content by its content hash so the superseded version stays retrievable.

nodes.name: read_record_version
nodes.summary: Reads an archived record version back by its content hash.

nodes.name: _own_content
nodes.summary: Extracts a node's own content, excluding nested records, so a contained change is not mistaken for a direct one.

nodes.name: change_set
nodes.summary: Pure diff of two snapshots: classifies each node as added, removed, direct (with the changed fields) or contained, and compares edges by label.

nodes.name: record_change
nodes.summary: Builds the before snapshot, archives and replaces the record content, rebuilds after, and writes the immutable change record — restoring the file if the rebuild refuses.

nodes.name: read_change_record
nodes.summary: Reads one change record by id, validating its schema identity and shape.

nodes.name: documents.py
nodes.summary: Imports a candidate proposal document as an immutable, content-versioned record — the snapshot builder's only source for document, passage, claim and commitment nodes. Re-importing identical content is a no-op; the same content under a different lifecycle state is refused.
nodes.languageNotes: Carries no wall-clock field, so a replay produces the same bytes at the same `<document_id>/<version>.json` path.

nodes.name: DocumentRef
nodes.summary: Reference to one imported document record: its id, content version and record path.

nodes.name: _str
nodes.summary: Reads a string field from a candidate record, refusing a blank or wrong-typed value with a located error.

nodes.name: _ids
nodes.summary: Reads a declared list of identifiers from a candidate record.

nodes.name: _objects
nodes.summary: Reads a declared list of nested objects from a candidate record.

nodes.name: _sub_sections
nodes.summary: Normalises a section's optional sub-sections, carrying each id, title and content verbatim.

nodes.name: _section
nodes.summary: Normalises one candidate section, including the ids it addresses and its sub-sections.

nodes.name: _verified_span
nodes.summary: Normalises a claim's verified span (source id plus byte offsets), refusing a partial span.

nodes.name: _claim
nodes.summary: Normalises one claim, keeping its declared status, verified span and approval as three separate fields and mapping evidence strength through the shared lookup.

nodes.name: _commitment
nodes.summary: Normalises one commitment and binds it to its section and the ids it addresses.

nodes.name: normalise_candidate
nodes.summary: Validates and normalises a whole candidate document — the single owner of candidate shape, also run by external converters before import.

nodes.name: render_document
nodes.summary: Renders the sections into the plain text that every passage span's byte offsets resolve against.

nodes.name: node_content
nodes.summary: Builds the record content the document node carries, the input to its content-derived version.

nodes.name: read_candidate
nodes.summary: Reads a candidate JSON file from disk and normalises it.

nodes.name: import_document
nodes.summary: Imports a candidate as an immutable document snapshot record, returning a no-op on identical content and refusing a state change disguised as a re-import.

nodes.name: read_document_records
nodes.summary: Reads every stored document snapshot record, the builder's document input.

nodes.name: identity.py
nodes.summary: Dev-graph identity primitives: canonical JSON serialisation, a record's content-hash version, and the content-derived snapshot id. Reads no clock, path or filesystem stamp, so two builds over the same content agree byte for byte.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately does not reuse the directory fingerprint helper, which hashes direct child names only.

nodes.name: canonical_json
nodes.summary: Canonical serialisation — sorted keys, no whitespace, ASCII-escaped — the only form hashed here.

nodes.name: content_hash
nodes.summary: Returns `sha256:<hex>` over the canonical JSON of an object, recursively through nested values.

nodes.name: snapshot_id
nodes.summary: Content-derived snapshot identity over the sorted nodes and edges.

nodes.name: impact.py
nodes.summary: Shadow impact planner: given the snapshots before and after an approved change plus the durable run records, it returns an advisory plan naming each affected record, passage, artifact or check with a reason path, a hit kind and one action from a closed set.
nodes.languageNotes: Breadth-first reach is bounded by a view policy applied before expansion; it refuses a broken index rather than returning a smaller plan.

nodes.name: ImpactPlan
nodes.summary: The advisory plan: its entries, the origins, newly relevant sources and the nothing-changed flag, with a dict projection for the writer.

nodes.name: _id_list
nodes.summary: Reads a declared list of identifiers from a run record, refusing a malformed shape.

nodes.name: normalise_run_records
nodes.summary: Validates and normalises the durable run records that declare each artifact's inputs and dependencies.

nodes.name: read_run_records
nodes.summary: Reads the stored run records from Tier 4 and normalises them.

nodes.name: _adjacency
nodes.summary: Builds the traversal adjacency over the union of before and after edges, filtered by the view policy's permitted predicates.

nodes.name: _reach
nodes.summary: Breadth-first reach from the origins to the policy's depth, recording the edge labels traversed and stopping at non-expanding containers.

nodes.name: plan_identity
nodes.summary: Returns the content-derived identity of an impact plan.

nodes.name: plan_nothing_changed
nodes.summary: Builds the trivial plan for a change set that moved nothing.

nodes.name: plan_impact
nodes.summary: Core planner: derives the origins, walks the bounded reach, classifies each hit, assigns the action and flags newly relevant sources.

nodes.name: read_impact_request
nodes.summary: Reads the operator's impact-plan request from Tier 4.

nodes.name: write_impact_plan
nodes.summary: Writes the advisory plan atomically to its canonical Tier 4 path.

nodes.name: run_impact_plan_writer
nodes.summary: Deterministic-component adapter `(run_id, repo_root) -> written`; the run id never enters the artifact.

nodes.name: intake.py
nodes.summary: Records what is known about an Evaluation Summary Report at intake, from a closed availability set and never by inference. One immutable record per intake id: identical content is a no-op, different content under the same id is refused.
nodes.languageNotes: `available` requires a bound reference, and a reference without that declaration is refused rather than read as availability.

nodes.name: EsrIntake
nodes.summary: The intake record: declared availability, bound submission and call ids, the document concerned, prior-submission flag and permitted purpose.

nodes.name: normalise_intake
nodes.summary: Validates and normalises an intake payload, enforcing the closed availability set and the available-means-bound rule.

nodes.name: record_esr_intake
nodes.summary: Writes one immutable intake record, returning a no-op on identical content and refusing a conflicting rewrite of the same id.

nodes.name: read_esr_intake
nodes.summary: Reads an intake record by id, validating its schema identity.

nodes.name: packages.py
nodes.summary: Builds a bounded, task-scoped evidence package under one view policy and one budget, returning the included items plus a manifest saying what was included and why, what was excluded and why, what is unresolved, and whether the package is complete.
nodes.languageNotes: Policy is applied before expansion, so a refused node is never a traversal step and nothing can enter through a side path; nothing is ever dropped silently.

nodes.name: Package
nodes.summary: Immutable evidence package: its included items, manifest and content-derived package id, with dict and JSON projections.

nodes.name: _mandatory_step
nodes.summary: Decides whether one predicate traversal counts as a mandatory step for the given direction and endpoint type.

nodes.name: estimate_cost
nodes.summary: Returns the budget cost of one item's content — the single measure the budget fill spends against.

nodes.name: _check_request
nodes.summary: Refuses a stale snapshot id, a stale policy version, an unknown view, an absent task or a non-positive budget before any work is done.

nodes.name: _expand
nodes.summary: Breadth-first expansion from the seed over the permitted graph to the view's maximum depth, recording the edges traversed.

nodes.name: _unresolved_items
nodes.summary: Lists unresolved items in both scopes: those included in the package and those the whole graph still owes.

nodes.name: _declared_status_items
nodes.summary: Rolls up each included item's declared status by node type rather than sniffing it from a value.

nodes.name: build_package
nodes.summary: The selection algorithm: refuse, apply policy, expand, mark mandatory, fill the budget in order, record exclusions and list unresolved items.

nodes.name: read_package_request
nodes.summary: Reads the operator's package request from Tier 4.

nodes.name: package_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the directory one package's artifacts land in.

nodes.name: write_package
nodes.summary: Writes the package items and manifest atomically under their content-derived package directory.

nodes.name: run_package_manifest_writer
nodes.summary: Deterministic-component adapter `(run_id, repo_root) -> written`; the run id never enters the artifact.

nodes.name: policies.py
nodes.summary: Configuration data for the six dev-graph view policies — permitted node types and traversals, maximum depth, forbidden types and tags — plus a content-hash policy version so a policy edit can never silently reinterpret an existing package.
nodes.languageNotes: The blind pre-evaluation policy also hides superseded document versions; whether a snapshot is superseded is computed by the package builder, not tagged on a node.

nodes.name: ViewPolicy
nodes.summary: One view's policy: permitted types and traversals, depth, forbidden types and tags, with the per-node `refusal` lookup the builder applies before expansion.

nodes.name: revisions.py
nodes.summary: Three closed operations over declared data: checking a proposed change set against a revision contract, creating a superseding candidate version with provenance, and deciding whether an existing assessment still applies. Also hosts the registered revision-record writer component.
nodes.languageNotes: Change classes come from a closed lookup table keyed by predicate, node type or changed field — never by inference; rejection outranks review.

nodes.name: RevisionContract
nodes.summary: The contract: the protected nodes, the permitted change classes and the unresolved items a change may bear on.

nodes.name: ContractCheck
nodes.summary: The verdict with its reasons: rejected protected nodes, unpermitted change classes and the unresolved items touched.

nodes.name: Applicability
nodes.summary: Whether an assessment still applies, with one reason per changed binding from the closed reason set.

nodes.name: RevisionRecord
nodes.summary: The immutable revision record: the contract check, the created candidate version and the change record it rests on.

nodes.name: _id_list
nodes.summary: Reads a declared list of identifiers from a contract payload.

nodes.name: _unresolved_item
nodes.summary: Normalises one declared unresolved item the contract names.

nodes.name: normalise_contract
nodes.summary: Validates and normalises a revision contract payload into its typed form.

nodes.name: _touches
nodes.summary: Collects every node id a change set touches, across added, removed and directly changed entries.

nodes.name: _validate_change_set
nodes.summary: Refuses a malformed change set before any classification is attempted.

nodes.name: classify_change_set
nodes.summary: Classifies a change set into change classes by closed lookup over predicates, node types and changed fields.

nodes.name: check_revision
nodes.summary: Pure contract check returning one verdict: rejected names every protected node touched, flagged carries unpermitted classes and unresolved items, accepted is the rest.

nodes.name: build_provenance
nodes.summary: Builds a candidate version's provenance: the snapshot it supersedes, the change record and the evidence nodes it rests on.

nodes.name: create_candidate_version
nodes.summary: Imports a new candidate as a second immutable document snapshot whose provenance supersedes the old one, leaving the old record byte for byte as it was.

nodes.name: bind_assessment
nodes.summary: Binds an assessment to the candidate id and version, the profile version and the policy version in force when it was made.

nodes.name: check_applicability
nodes.summary: Pure check of whether an assessment still applies to the current candidate, naming each changed binding as a reason.

nodes.name: read_revision_request
nodes.summary: Reads and validates the operator's revision request from Tier 4.

nodes.name: write_revision_record
nodes.summary: Component body: runs the contract check, creates the candidate version only on acceptance, and writes one immutable revision record.

nodes.name: read_revision_record
nodes.summary: Reads a revision record by id, validating its schema identity and shape.

nodes.name: run_revision_record_writer
nodes.summary: Deterministic-component adapter `(run_id, repo_root) -> written`; the run id never enters the artifact.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: The dev graph's closed vocabularies as data: the node-type set and the relationship set, each relationship declaring its permitted endpoint pairs, direction, cardinality and whether it is a domain link or an execution dependency. Also owns the fail-closed graph validator.
nodes.languageNotes: Carries no project noun, reads no file and evaluates no gate — adding a node type or predicate is a schema change that needs a test.

nodes.name: RelationshipSpec
nodes.summary: One relationship's declaration: permitted endpoint type pairs, direction, cardinality and operational effect, with `permits` and `single_target` checks.

nodes.name: DevGraphError
nodes.summary: The package's fail-closed error, naming the first invalid node, edge or record and where it came from.

nodes.name: declared_status
nodes.summary: Pure read of a node's declared validation status from the field its node type declares it in — never sniffed from a value.

nodes.name: validate_graph
nodes.summary: Fail-closed validation of nodes and edges against the closed vocabularies, endpoint pairs and cardinality, naming the first offender.

nodes.name: shadow.py
nodes.summary: Compares the impact planner's advisory against the reuse decision the scheduler actually recorded, emitting one diagnostic from a closed set (agreed, planner narrower, planner broader). Pure shadow mode: nothing consumes the diagnostic at runtime.
nodes.languageNotes: A node with no artifact-path binding is a refusal rather than a silent skip, and `planner_broader` outranks `planner_narrower` because it is the safety-relevant finding.

nodes.name: ShadowComparison
nodes.summary: The comparison result: the diagnostic, the per-node rows and the plan and run it compared.

nodes.name: _plan_dict
nodes.summary: Indexes a plan's entries by the artifact path each one concerns.

nodes.name: _decisions
nodes.summary: Normalises the scheduler's recorded reuse decisions into reuse/rerun verdicts.

nodes.name: _planner_verdict
nodes.summary: Derives the planner's reuse/rerun verdict for one artifact path by lookup over the plan's entries, defaulting to rerun when no run record vouches for it.

nodes.name: compare_shadow
nodes.summary: Core comparison: binds each node through its artifact path, compares the two verdicts and emits the ranked diagnostic with every row kept.

nodes.name: read_shadow_request
nodes.summary: Reads the operator's shadow-comparison request from Tier 4.

nodes.name: read_plan
nodes.summary: Reads a stored advisory impact plan by id.

nodes.name: read_reuse_decisions
nodes.summary: Reads a run manifest's recorded reuse decisions from runtime state.

nodes.name: write_shadow_comparison
nodes.summary: Writes the comparison atomically to its canonical Tier 4 path.

nodes.name: run_shadow_comparison_writer
nodes.summary: Deterministic-component adapter `(run_id, repo_root) -> written`.

nodes.name: writer.py
nodes.summary: The registered deterministic component behind the dev-graph index: builds the snapshot and writes it atomically to its canonical Tier 4 path. The snapshot carries no run id and no clock, so a replay from the same records is byte-equal.

nodes.name: write_snapshot
nodes.summary: Builds the snapshot and writes it atomically, returning the absolute path.

nodes.name: run_snapshot_writer
nodes.summary: Component adapter `(run_id, repo_root) -> written`; the run id is accepted for the contract and never enters the artifact.

nodes.name: docx_exporter.py
nodes.summary: Renders the assembled Part B (or whatever individual section artifacts exist) into a Microsoft Word `.docx` under Tier 5 final exports. Invents no content: every heading and paragraph is copied verbatim from the section JSON.
nodes.languageNotes: Fails soft — with no section content it returns `None` rather than writing an empty document.

nodes.name: _synthetic_override_active
nodes.summary: Detects whether the fictional-budget operator override is in force, which the export must disclose.

nodes.name: _read_optional_json
nodes.summary: Reads a JSON artifact if it exists, returning `None` rather than raising when absent.

nodes.name: _resolve_section_paths
nodes.summary: Resolves which section artifacts to render: the assembled Part B when present, otherwise whatever individual sections are on disk.

nodes.name: split_content_blocks
nodes.summary: Splits a sub-section's prose into the paragraph blocks the renderer emits.

nodes.name: _add_content_paragraphs
nodes.summary: Appends each content block to the document as a paragraph, verbatim.

nodes.name: _render_section
nodes.summary: Renders one section: its criterion heading and each sub-section's title and content, all copied from the artifact.

nodes.name: export_part_b_docx
nodes.summary: Entry point: resolves the sections, renders the whole document and writes the `.docx` atomically, returning `None` when there is nothing to render.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for running the exporter from the repository root.

nodes.name: final_export_writer.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic node-body component for the revision phase that writes the terminal Tier 5 export artifacts: a self-contained JSON bundle embedding the assembled draft and every referenced section verbatim, plus the schema-bound export manifest.
nodes.languageNotes: The manifest is written after the bundle, so a partial failure can never leave a manifest pointing at a missing export; only `exported_at` is excluded from the replay invariant.

nodes.name: _read_json_dict
nodes.summary: Reads a required JSON object, raising `FinalExportError` when absent or malformed.

nodes.name: _validate_sections
nodes.summary: Validates the assembled draft's section list and the referenced section artifacts before anything is bundled.

nodes.name: write_final_export
nodes.summary: Component entry point: bundles the assembled draft and sections verbatim, then writes the schema-bound export manifest with its derived section index.

nodes.name: instrument_profile.py
nodes.summary: Resolves a per-instrument profile — mandatory sub-sections, hard page limit, budget regime and phases in scope — from the two Tier 2A extracted registries keyed on the selected call's instrument type, so no instrument literal is baked into the drafting path.
nodes.languageNotes: Never defaults silently: an absent or unknown instrument type, or any missing profile field, raises rather than guessing.

nodes.name: InstrumentProfile
nodes.summary: The consolidated profile: instrument type, sub-section set, page limit, budget regime and phases in scope, with the mandatory and drafting sub-section views.

nodes.name: _read_json
nodes.summary: Reads one Tier 2A registry, raising `InstrumentProfileError` when absent or malformed.

nodes.name: _find_instrument_entry
nodes.summary: Finds the registry entry for an instrument type, refusing an unknown or ambiguous key.

nodes.name: resolve_instrument_type
nodes.summary: Reads the selected call's declared instrument type from Tier 3.

nodes.name: resolve_instrument_profile
nodes.summary: Consolidates the section-schema and instrument registries into one profile, failing closed on any missing required field.

nodes.name: resolve_budget_regime
nodes.summary: Resolves the instrument's budget regime — lump sum or unit cost — the value the budget gate branches on.

nodes.name: owns_budget_regime
nodes.summary: Guard answering whether the active instrument owns a given budget regime, so each budget component writes only under its own regime.

nodes.name: interface_contract.py
nodes.summary: Validator for the Lump Sum Budget Planner interface contract, interpreting that document on its own terms rather than as a JSON Schema (which would accept every payload). Pure, with no I/O or run state, and used by both the request composer and the response-side gate predicate.
nodes.languageNotes: Walks every number for the no-negative-values rule rather than guessing which field is a budget field, because that judgment is deliberately out of scope.

nodes.name: ContractViolation
nodes.summary: One located contract violation, with a human-readable rendering for the gate's finding list.

nodes.name: carries_json_schema_keywords
nodes.summary: Reports whether a contract document carries any recognised JSON Schema keyword — the check that proves it must not be read as a schema.

nodes.name: is_planner_contract
nodes.summary: Recognises a payload as the planner's contract document by its own declared blocks.

nodes.name: _check_required
nodes.summary: Checks each named required field is present and non-empty, treating `None`, `""`, `[]` and `{}` as missing but `0` and `False` as values.

nodes.name: _check_negatives
nodes.summary: Walks the whole payload refusing any negative number, excluding booleans since a flag is not a value.

nodes.name: validate_payload
nodes.summary: Validates a request or response payload against the contract's required fields, entry shapes and validation rules, returning every located violation.

nodes.name: phase8_canonical_pack.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic builder of the canonical reference pack that Phase 8 drafting skills use for objective, work-package, deliverable, partner and outcome identities. Confirmed Tier 3/4 values are lifted verbatim; operator declarations are quarantined in a separate provenance-tagged array.
nodes.languageNotes: An assumed value is structurally incapable of being emitted as confirmed: the deriver does no inference about which typed entity a declaration backs.

nodes.name: _read_json
nodes.summary: Reads one source artifact, returning an empty mapping when it is absent.

nodes.name: _lift
nodes.summary: Lifts named keys (with aliases) verbatim from a source record into a pack entry, preserving source values exactly.

nodes.name: _extract_objectives
nodes.summary: Extracts the confirmed objective identities and titles from Tier 3.

nodes.name: _extract_outcomes
nodes.summary: Extracts the confirmed outcome identities and titles from Tier 3.

nodes.name: _extract_wps_and_deliverables
nodes.summary: Extracts the confirmed work-package and deliverable identities from the Phase 3 structure.

nodes.name: _extract_partners
nodes.summary: Extracts the confirmed partner identities from the Tier 3 consortium record.

nodes.name: _extract_declared_assumptions
nodes.summary: Passes the operator's declarations through verbatim into the quarantined assumed array, failing closed on a malformed declarations file.

nodes.name: build_phase8_canonical_reference_pack
nodes.summary: Component entry point: assembles every typed array with its provenance tag and writes the pack atomically.

nodes.name: section_assembler.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic section assembler: array-appends the per-sub-section drafts into the Tier 5 section artifact in spine order, carrying claim statuses and declarations verbatim and deriving exactly two things — each sub-section's word count and the de-duplicated union of source refs.
nodes.languageNotes: "No synthesis" holds by construction and is enforced by a byte-equal replay check: the assembler never authors prose and never sets a claim's status.

nodes.name: _read_json_object
nodes.summary: Reads a required JSON object, raising `SectionAssemblerError` when absent or malformed.

nodes.name: _build_sub_section
nodes.summary: Builds one assembled sub-section, carrying the draft verbatim and deriving only its word count.

nodes.name: _coerce_tier
nodes.summary: Normalises a source ref's tier label so refs from different drafts de-duplicate correctly.

nodes.name: _source_ref_key
nodes.summary: Builds the de-duplication key for one source ref.

nodes.name: _union_source_refs
nodes.summary: Computes the de-duplicated union of every draft's source refs — one of the assembler's two derived values.

nodes.name: _load_drafts_in_order
nodes.summary: Loads the per-sub-section drafts in the spine-declared order, refusing a missing, extra or duplicate draft.

nodes.name: _carry_claim_statuses
nodes.summary: Concatenates each draft's claim statuses verbatim, without re-judging any of them.

nodes.name: assemble_section
