nodes.summary: Component entry point: loads the spine and drafts, array-appends the sub-sections, carries the validation block verbatim and writes the section artifact atomically.

nodes.name: source_index.py
nodes.summary: Verifier for the Tier 3 source index, enforcing the one rule the snapshot builder cannot: a source carries verbatim text only when that text can be re-derived byte for byte from a file stored in this repository. Everything else is a reference, which carries no text and therefore no verifiable span.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately has only two transcription states with no third "paraphrased" option, closing the one place in Tier 3 where a claim could be laundered.

nodes.name: SourceProblem
nodes.summary: One located finding about a source record: its kind, the record it concerns and the detail.

nodes.name: SourceIndexReport
nodes.summary: The verification report: every problem found, with an `ok` verdict and a human-readable rendering.

nodes.name: SourceIndex
nodes.summary: The loaded index with its records and an id lookup.

nodes.name: normalise_whitespace
nodes.summary: Normalises whitespace the way the byte-equal transcription check requires.

nodes.name: read_page_text
nodes.summary: Transcribes one page of a stored PDF to text — the only mechanism by which a source may carry verbatim text.

nodes.name: load_index
nodes.summary: Loads and shape-checks the source index from Tier 3 source materials.

nodes.name: candidate_names
nodes.summary: Collects the candidate names an external reference's anchor may be checked against.

nodes.name: _check_shape
nodes.summary: Checks one record's declared shape against its source kind, refusing text on a reference.

nodes.name: _check_resolution
nodes.summary: Checks that a record resolves: a page source to a stored file and page, a reference to a registered identifier.

nodes.name: _check_transcription
nodes.summary: Re-derives a page source's text from the stored document and refuses any byte-level divergence.

nodes.name: span_id
nodes.summary: Builds the canonical span identifier from a source id and its byte offsets.

nodes.name: _check_spans
nodes.summary: Checks every claim span resolves inside the source's stored text at its declared byte offsets.

nodes.name: _check_anchor
nodes.summary: Checks an external reference's anchor string actually occurs in the stored artifact that names it.

nodes.name: _check_no_overclaim
nodes.summary: Refuses a record that claims more verification than its kind and evidence support.

nodes.name: _check_names
nodes.summary: Checks a reference's recorded name occurs in the swept project texts.

nodes.name: _registered_document_ids
nodes.summary: Collects the registered document ids a page source may resolve against.

nodes.name: _concept_claim_ids
nodes.summary: Collects the concept claim ids whose spans the index must cover.

nodes.name: _check_coverage
nodes.summary: Checks every claim that needs a source has one, and flags sources nothing cites.

nodes.name: verify
nodes.summary: Entry point: runs every per-record and index-wide check and returns the full report.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that renders the report and exits non-zero on any finding.

nodes.name: unit_cost_budget.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic unit-cost budget deriver: computes a unit-cost (MSCA-style) budget as confirmed months times published rates times host-country coefficient, in a pure core plus a component wrapper that resolves inputs from durable state and writes the artifact atomically.
nodes.languageNotes: Determinism is the anti-fabrication guarantee here, closed by a byte-equal replay check; an unresolved host coefficient still yields every host-independent line plus an explicit unresolved marker.

nodes.name: _monthly_rate
nodes.summary: Looks up one monthly published unit rate for a researcher group and budget line, refusing an absent rate.

nodes.name: compute_unit_cost_budget
nodes.summary: The pure figure: given confirmed months, the rate table and the host coefficient it returns every derived line item and the total, marking the host-dependent line unresolved when the coefficient is absent.

nodes.name: _read_json
nodes.summary: Reads one durable input artifact, raising `UnitCostBudgetError` when absent or malformed.

nodes.name: _resolve_confirmed_months
nodes.summary: Resolves the confirmed effort months from the call binding or an operator declaration, never from an estimate.

nodes.name: _lookup_coefficient
nodes.summary: Looks up the published country-correction coefficient for the host country.

nodes.name: _resolve_host_country
nodes.summary: Resolves the host country from the call binding or an operator declaration, leaving it unresolved rather than guessing.

nodes.name: derive_unit_cost_budget
nodes.summary: Component entry point: resolves rates, months and host country from durable state, calls the pure core and writes the budget artifact with its pass/fail gate declaration.

nodes.name: build_demo_dev_graph.py
nodes.summary: Authoring tool that writes the first dev-graph snapshot over the populated demo Tier 3 records plus one bounded evidence package per view policy for three structurally chosen seed tasks, bisecting the minimum budget at which each package fits and completes.
nodes.languageNotes: Idempotent and content-derived: `--check` writes nothing and exits non-zero if any artifact would change.

nodes.name: _package
nodes.summary: Builds one evidence package for a seed task under one view and budget.

nodes.name: count_by
nodes.summary: Counts items grouped by a declared key, so every reported count is derived rather than typed.

nodes.name: _minimum_budget
nodes.summary: Bisects the smallest budget at which a predicate over the built package holds, so "incomplete" comes with a measurement.

nodes.name: _package_row
nodes.summary: Builds the summary row for one package: its derived counts and both bisected minimum budgets.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Writes the snapshot and every package, returning the full derived run summary.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point supporting write and `--check` modes.

nodes.name: build_part_b_candidate.py
nodes.summary: Converter that turns Phase 8's Tier 5 section artifacts into a blind-lane candidate document, the missing route from a drafted Part B to a graded one. Deterministic and Claude-free: every field is copied verbatim and nothing is repaired.
nodes.languageNotes: Every `sub_section_id` is carried verbatim because the rubric anchor map fails closed on an absent anchor, so a renumbered sub-section would break grading silently.

nodes.name: SectionSpec
nodes.summary: Declares one expected section: its slug, criterion, artifact path and schema identity.

nodes.name: _section_specs
nodes.summary: Returns the expected section specs the converter requires to be present.

nodes.name: _read_section
nodes.summary: Reads and refuses one section artifact: a wrong schema id, a disagreeing criterion, an invalid artifact status or no sub-sections.

nodes.name: _sub_sections
nodes.summary: Copies each sub-section's id, title and content verbatim into candidate sections, refusing a duplicate or empty one.

nodes.name: _claims
nodes.summary: Converts each claim status into a candidate claim, refusing an unknown status rather than mapping it.

nodes.name: build_candidate
nodes.summary: Builds the whole candidate and re-checks it against the importer's own normaliser, so identifier shape is judged once by its owner.

nodes.name: write_candidate
nodes.summary: Writes the candidate to its canonical path atomically.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point supporting write and `--check` modes.

nodes.name: derive_run_phase_costs.py
nodes.summary: Recovers per-phase invocation counts, tokens and wall clock for a run by partitioning the append-only transport ledger on the phase gates' evaluation timestamps — the attribution the ledger supports but does not record, since every row carries a null node id.
nodes.languageNotes: The attribution is explicitly Inferred, resting on two structural checks that both fail closed; monetary cost is written as null because no rate exists to price the tokens against.

nodes.name: collect_phase_gates
nodes.summary: Collects each phase gate's result and evaluation timestamp, checking they ascend with phase number and share one run id.

nodes.name: resolve_run_id
nodes.summary: Resolves which run to measure, refusing a requested id the gate results do not agree on.

nodes.name: read_ledger
nodes.summary: Reads the append-only transport invocation ledger for a run.

nodes.name: read_monetary_cost
nodes.summary: Attempts to resolve a monetary rate, returning unresolved rather than substituting a figure.

nodes.name: partition
nodes.summary: Partitions the ledger rows into per-phase windows on the gate boundaries.

nodes.name: _measure
nodes.summary: Measures one partition: invocation count, token totals and wall clock, all derived off the rows.

nodes.name: build_record
nodes.summary: Builds the whole per-phase cost record, with every number measured and no clock in the artifact.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point supporting write and `--check` modes.

nodes.name: preserve_run_manifests.py
nodes.summary: Copies the run manifests that dispatched the workflow phases out of gitignored runtime state into the durable Tier 4 record, preserving the run id, node states, per-node failure metadata and reuse decisions. It copies and never edits a manifest.
nodes.languageNotes: Output files are named by a slug derived from the run id with the true id recorded inside, and two runs whose ids slugify alike are refused rather than silently merged.

nodes.name: slug
nodes.summary: Derives the filename slug from a run id, since nothing validates a pasted run id.

nodes.name: collect
nodes.summary: Collects each run's manifest fields, reuse policy and surviving run summary, refusing two runs that slugify to the same name.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point supporting write and `--check` modes.

nodes.name: fingerprints.py
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for reducing a gate input artifact to a deterministic SHA-256 content fingerprint. Imported by both the writer side (gate_evaluator, which stamps input_artifact_fingerprints into every gate result) and the reader side (is_gate_fresh), so content-based staleness cannot diverge.
nodes.languageNotes: Kept as a leaf module depending only on runner.paths and the standard library, because importing the helper back from gate_evaluator would form an import cycle.

nodes.name: gate_evaluator.py
nodes.summary: The sole entry point for evaluating one gate: resolves predicates from the compiled manifest's predicate_refs, runs every deterministic predicate without fast-fail, dispatches semantic predicates only when all deterministic ones pass, writes the canonical Tier 4 GateResult, updates node state and propagates HARD_BLOCK from the budget gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Approach B predicate resolution: the compiled manifest is the composition source (predicate_refs) and the gate library is the implementation registry, with Approach A (library predicate list) as fallback when the manifest is absent.

nodes.name: gate_library.py
nodes.summary: Loader and validator for gate_rules_library.yaml, the implementation registry that maps each gate_id to its executable predicates, and refuses to load when the library's manifest_version disagrees with the runner's.

nodes.name: gate_result_registry.py
nodes.summary: Authoritative table of canonical Tier 4 gate result paths, plus the shared gate-result schema_id, Tier 4 root and version-field constants that the evaluator, the gate_pass_recorded predicate and the backfill tool all read instead of re-hardcoding.

nodes.name: paths.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic repository-root discovery (an ancestor holding both CLAUDE.md and .git/) and repo-relative artifact path resolution. Every predicate resolves paths through it rather than inlining path logic.

nodes.name: fingerprint_path
nodes.summary: Computes the deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint of one path, returning a MISSING sentinel when the file is absent so an input appearing or disappearing counts as a real content change.

nodes.name: compute_fingerprints
nodes.summary: Fingerprints a list of repo-relative artifact paths, returning the per-artifact map plus the combined fingerprint the gate evaluator records in every gate result.

nodes.name: _substitute_runtime_args
nodes.summary: Substitutes runtime placeholders such as the current run_id into a predicate's declared argument map before invocation.

nodes.name: _gate_result_path
nodes.summary: Resolves the canonical Tier 4 write path for a gate result from the registry, falling back to the gate_results subdirectory for gate_ids absent from the table.

nodes.name: _call_predicate
nodes.summary: Dispatches one deterministic predicate by registered function name with its resolved arguments, converting an unknown name or raised exception into a failing PredicateResult rather than an abort.

nodes.name: _is_hard_block_failure
nodes.summary: Decides whether a gate's failed predicates constitute a HARD_BLOCK, the propagation that freezes every Phase 8 node behind the budget gate.

nodes.name: _resolve_budget_regime
nodes.summary: Reads the active instrument's budget regime (lump-sum versus unit-cost) so the budget gate evaluates the predicate set that matches the instrument.

nodes.name: _partition_predicates_by_instrument
nodes.summary: Splits a gate's predicate list into the ones applicable to the resolved instrument and the ones skipped by applies_when, so an instrument-conditional gate neither over- nor under-checks.

nodes.name: evaluate_gate
nodes.summary: The gate evaluation entry point: loads the library and run context, resolves predicate_refs from the compiled manifest, computes input fingerprints, runs all deterministic predicates collecting every failure, dispatches semantic predicates only when the deterministic set passes, writes the GateResult and updates node state.

nodes.name: GateLibraryError
nodes.summary: Base exception for every gate rules library load or validation failure.

nodes.name: ManifestVersionMismatchError
nodes.summary: Raised when the library's declared manifest_version disagrees with the runner's constant, which means the compiled manifest and the gate rules have drifted apart.

nodes.name: GateNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Raised when a requested gate_id has no entry in the loaded gate rules library.

nodes.name: GateLibrary
nodes.summary: Loads and validates gate_rules_library.yaml once per evaluation and serves gate entries and individual predicate definitions by id, exposing the library, manifest and constitution versions the gate result records.

nodes.name: find_repo_root
nodes.summary: Walks up from a starting directory to the first ancestor containing both CLAUDE.md and .git/, requiring both markers to avoid false positives in nested checkouts.

nodes.name: resolve_repo_path
nodes.summary: Resolves a repo-relative artifact path against an explicit repository root, passing absolute paths through unchanged; the single resolution point every predicate uses.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel that re-exports every gate predicate implementation and the shared failure-category constants under one public namespace, grouped by the implementation step that introduced them.

nodes.name: coverage_predicates.py
nodes.summary: Cross-artifact join predicates checking coverage between work packages, partners, budget lines, expected impacts, KPIs, Gantt tasks and drafted sections. Mismatches between two present artifacts fail as CROSS_ARTIFACT_INCONSISTENCY rather than as a malformed input.
nodes.languageNotes: Each public predicate pairs with bounded private extractors that tolerate several documented artifact shapes instead of assuming one schema.

nodes.name: criterion_predicates.py
nodes.summary: Phase 8 criterion-aligned predicates for gates 10a-10d: schema_id agreement, claim-status discipline (no unresolved material claims, assumed claims operator-declared, declared facts not silently inferred), impact and implementation coverage, and cross-section consistency against canonical Tier 3 data.

nodes.name: cycle_predicates.py
nodes.summary: Holds the single cycle-detection predicate: reads the dependency_map of the Phase 3 wp_structure.json and proves the work-package and task dependency graph is acyclic, reporting the offending cycle when it is not.

nodes.name: file_predicates.py
nodes.summary: Stateless filesystem predicates (exists, non_empty, non_empty_json, dir_non_empty) plus artifact_owned_by_run, the run-ownership check that separates an artifact written by the current run from one legitimately reused under the reuse policy.
nodes.languageNotes: JSON is read with utf-8-sig so a byte-order mark never masquerades as a malformed artifact.

nodes.name: _read_json_object
nodes.summary: Defensive JSON object reader returning either the parsed mapping or a failing PredicateResult categorised as missing or malformed.

nodes.name: _read_json_any
nodes.summary: Variant of the JSON reader that accepts any top-level type, for artifacts legitimately shaped as arrays.

nodes.name: _extract_partner_ids_from_array
nodes.summary: Extracts partner identifiers from an array-shaped consortium artifact, tolerating the documented key variants.

nodes.name: _extract_partner_ids
nodes.summary: Extracts the full set of partner identifiers from a Tier 3 consortium artifact regardless of which documented shape it uses.

nodes.name: _extract_expected_impact_ids
nodes.summary: Extracts expected-impact identifiers from the Tier 2B expected_impacts artifact, including destination-level groupings.

nodes.name: _extract_required_section_ids
nodes.summary: Extracts the set of section ids the active instrument's application-form schema requires.

nodes.name: _extract_required_impl_section_ids
nodes.summary: Extracts the implementation-section ids the instrument mandates, which gate_06 checks for coverage.

nodes.name: _collect_field_values_deep
nodes.summary: Recursively collects every value of a named field anywhere in a nested structure, used when a coverage key may appear at several depths.

nodes.name: _scan_budget_dir
nodes.summary: Scans a budget response directory and gathers the values of one field across all budget files, so coverage works whether the budget arrives as one file or many.

nodes.name: _extract_wp_ids
nodes.summary: Extracts the work-package identifiers declared in the Phase 3 work-package structure.

nodes.name: _extract_all_deliverable_ids
nodes.summary: Collects every deliverable identifier across all work packages.

nodes.name: _extract_all_task_ids
nodes.summary: Collects every task identifier across all work packages.

nodes.name: _extract_all_wp_partners
nodes.summary: Collects the partner identifiers referenced as leads or participants across all work packages.

nodes.name: all_wps_have_deliverable_and_lead
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every work package must declare objectives, at least one deliverable and a responsible lead, which is the structural half of the Phase 3 gate condition.

nodes.name: all_partners_in_tier3
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every partner referenced by the work-package structure must exist in the Tier 3 consortium data, blocking fabricated partners.

nodes.name: all_management_roles_in_tier3
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every management role assigned in the implementation architecture must map to a partner present in Tier 3.

nodes.name: all_tasks_have_months
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every task in the work-package structure must be assigned start and end months in the Gantt, the Phase 4 scheduling completeness check.

nodes.name: all_impacts_mapped
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every expected impact declared in Tier 2B must have at least one mapped project output in the impact architecture.

nodes.name: kpis_traceable_to_wps
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every KPI in the impact architecture must trace to a work package, so no impact claim stands without a project mechanism.

nodes.name: instrument_sections_addressed
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every implementation section the instrument mandates must be addressed in the Phase 6 output.

nodes.name: all_sections_drafted
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every section required by the active application form must have a draft present, the Phase 8 completeness check.

nodes.name: all_sections_have_traceability_footer
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every drafted section must carry its traceability footer, so each deliverable states the tiered sources it derives from.

nodes.name: wp_budget_coverage_match
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the work-package ids in the budget response must match the designed work-package structure exactly, a structural consistency half of the budget gate.

nodes.name: partner_budget_coverage_match
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the partners in the budget response must match the Tier 3 consortium, catching a budget computed for a different consortium.

nodes.name: _read_json_object
nodes.summary: Defensive JSON object reader shared by the criterion predicates, returning a categorised failing result instead of raising.

nodes.name: schema_id_matches
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the artifact's schema_id must equal the expected value, so a draft written against a superseded schema cannot pass a gate.

nodes.name: no_unresolved_material_claims
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the section's overall validation status must not be unresolved, enforcing that a gap is declared rather than drafted over.

nodes.name: assumed_claims_are_operator_declared
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every claim marked Assumed must cite a matching operator declaration in working_assumptions, so an assumption is never adopted by the drafter alone.

nodes.name: _cites_working_assumptions
nodes.summary: Checks whether a claim's source reference actually cites the working-assumptions register.

nodes.name: declared_facts_are_not_inferred
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: a fact traceable to a declared Tier 3 source must not be downgraded to Inferred, catching status drift in the drafted sections.

nodes.name: impact_pathways_covered
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the Impact section's pathway references must cover every pathway in the Phase 5 impact architecture.

nodes.name: implementation_coverage_complete
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the Implementation section must populate its work-package table, Gantt, milestone and risk-register references.

nodes.name: _check_objective_coverage
nodes.summary: Checks that every Tier 3 objective is addressed somewhere across the criterion-aligned sections.

nodes.name: _check_partner_naming
nodes.summary: Checks that partner names used in the drafted sections match the canonical Tier 3 spellings.

nodes.name: _check_metric_completeness
nodes.summary: Checks that each objective's quantitative metric survives into the drafted prose.

nodes.name: _check_terminology_consistency
nodes.summary: Checks that canonical terminology is used consistently across sections rather than paraphrased per section.

nodes.name: _check_deliverable_kpi_alignment
nodes.summary: Checks that deliverable and KPI references in the sections align with the canonical registers.

nodes.name: cross_section_consistency
nodes.summary: Gate predicate behind gate_10d: cross-checks objectives, work-package ids, partner names, deliverable ids, metrics and terminology across all criterion-aligned sections against canonical Tier 3 and Tier 4 artifacts.

nodes.name: no_dependency_cycles
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: parses the dependency_map of wp_structure.json, validates its node and edge contract, and proves the directed dependency graph is acyclic, naming the cycle when one exists.

nodes.name: exists
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the resolved path must exist, the most basic fail-closed input check.

nodes.name: non_empty
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the file must exist and contain non-whitespace content.

nodes.name: non_empty_json
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the file must parse as JSON and carry a non-empty top-level structure, distinguishing an absent input from a placeholder empty object.

nodes.name: dir_non_empty
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the directory must exist and have at least one direct child, scanned non-recursively.

nodes.name: artifact_owned_by_run
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the artifact must declare the current run_id, or qualify for reuse under the declared reuse policy, which is what keeps a gate from passing on a stale artifact from an earlier run.

nodes.name: gate_pass_predicates.py
nodes.summary: Verifies an upstream gate result exists at its canonical path, declares the required schema_id, records status pass, belongs to the current run and is fresh with respect to its upstream inputs - where freshness is decided by content fingerprint, with file mtime used only as a trigger (ST-1).

nodes.name: phase8_section_predicates.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic preflight checks over Phase 8 section drafts that catch stale run_ids, partner-name conflation, deliverable identity corruption, canonical-term drift and lost measurable targets before the cross-section gate runs.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately fails only on contradictory explicit attachments, never on merely absent context, so ID-only prose references stay legal.

nodes.name: schema_predicates.py
nodes.summary: The largest predicate module: field-presence and canonical-shape checks over artifacts, including instrument/schema agreement, lump-sum interface-contract conformance, unit-cost budget resolution, risk register, ethics and governance completeness, review findings, and checkpoint provenance validation.

nodes.name: scope_coverage_predicates.py
nodes.summary: Phase 2 predicate asserting that every mandatory Tier 2B scope requirement has an explicit entry in the concept refinement summary's scope_coverage, replacing a semantic check that could not distinguish 'covered but not logged' from 'not covered'.

nodes.name: source_ref_predicates.py
nodes.summary: Traceability predicates confirming that every extracted Tier 2B fact and every topic mapping entry carries a non-empty source reference; an absent reference in a structurally valid artifact fails as POLICY_VIOLATION.

nodes.name: _parse_iso8601
nodes.summary: Parses a gate result's evaluated_at timestamp into an aware datetime, returning None when it is unusable.

nodes.name: _mtime_suspect_inputs
nodes.summary: Lists the gate's upstream inputs whose mtime is later than its evaluated_at - the trigger set whose content fingerprints are then compared.

nodes.name: _check_continuation_acceptance
nodes.summary: Decides whether a gate result recorded under a different run_id may be accepted as a continuation of the current run.

nodes.name: is_gate_fresh
nodes.summary: Judges a gate result fresh or stale by recomputing the content fingerprint of each mtime-suspect upstream input and comparing it with the recorded one, so a touched but unchanged file no longer invalidates a gate (ST-1).

nodes.name: gate_pass_recorded
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: an upstream gate result must exist at its canonical path, declare the required schema_id and versions, record status pass, belong to this run and be fresh - the mechanism that makes upstream gates mandatory for downstream phases.

nodes.name: _read_json
nodes.summary: Defensive JSON reader for Phase 8 section artifacts, returning a categorised failing result rather than raising.

nodes.name: _is_title_attempt
nodes.summary: Decides whether a found appositive is an attempt at the canonical title, so a genuine paraphrase is flagged while unrelated prose is not.

nodes.name: _find_appositives
nodes.summary: Finds the appositive phrases attached to an entity id in the drafted prose.

nodes.name: _appositive_is_other_entity
nodes.summary: Checks whether an appositive attached to one id actually names a different canonical entity, which is the conflation signature the predicate reports.

nodes.name: _find_truncated_legal_name
nodes.summary: Detects a partner's legal name rendered in truncated form in the prose.

nodes.name: _check_partner_conflation
nodes.summary: Checks that a partner's short name and legal name are not swapped or merged with another partner's in the drafted content.

nodes.name: _extract_attached_wps
nodes.summary: Extracts the work-package attributions the prose explicitly attaches to a deliverable id.

nodes.name: _extract_attached_months
nodes.summary: Extracts the due months the prose explicitly attaches to a deliverable id.

nodes.name: no_stale_run_id
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the section artifact must declare the current run_id, catching a draft carried over from an earlier run.

nodes.name: partner_names_preserved
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: partner short and legal names in the drafted section must match the canonical pack without conflation or truncation.

nodes.name: deliverable_identity_preserved
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: a deliverable referenced in the prose must not be given a contradictory title, work package or due month relative to the canonical pack.

nodes.name: canonical_terms_preserved
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: canonical terms from the pack must appear verbatim rather than paraphrased, the check that caught drafters rewriting canonical outcome titles.

nodes.name: _detect_section_type
nodes.summary: Infers which criterion section an artifact path belongs to, so the quantitative checks apply the right expectations.

nodes.name: _check_quantitative_components
nodes.summary: Checks that every numeric component of a measurable target survives in the drafted content.

nodes.name: measurable_targets_preserved
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: each objective's measurable target must keep its quantitative components in the drafted section, so a number is never softened into prose.

nodes.name: _read_json_object
nodes.summary: Defensive JSON object reader shared by the schema predicates, mapping read and parse problems onto the canonical failure categories.

nodes.name: json_field_present
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the named top-level field must be present and non-empty in the artifact.

nodes.name: json_fields_present
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every named field must be present and non-empty, reporting all missing fields at once rather than the first.

nodes.name: instrument_type_matches_schema
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the instrument declared in the selected call must match the instrument the loaded section schema describes, preventing a proposal drafted against the wrong application form.

nodes.name: interface_contract_conforms
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: a received lump-sum budget response must conform to the interface contract, distinguishing a planner-shaped contract from a JSON-Schema-shaped one so a response is validated rather than waved through.

nodes.name: risk_register_populated
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the implementation architecture's risk register must carry risks with mitigation measures, not an empty placeholder.

nodes.name: ethics_assessment_explicit
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: ethics flags must be explicitly stated rather than omitted, enforcing the Phase 6 rule that silence is not an answer.

nodes.name: governance_matrix_present
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the management structure must declare a decision-making matrix with assigned, non-overlapping roles.

nodes.name: no_blocking_inconsistencies
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the artifact must declare no unresolved blocking inconsistency, the honest-failure check that keeps a known contradiction from passing as complete.

nodes.name: unit_cost_budget_resolved
nodes.summary: Gate predicate for unit-cost instruments: every budget component, host-dependent lines included, must resolve to Confirmed or an operator-declared Assumed before the budget gate can pass.

nodes.name: budget_gate_confirmation_present
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the Phase 7 budget gate assessment must record its confirmation of receipt and structural consistency, the artifact that unblocks Phase 8.

nodes.name: findings_categorised_by_severity
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every review finding must carry a severity category, so a critical finding cannot hide in an uncategorised list.

nodes.name: revision_action_list_present
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the review packet must carry an actionable revision list rather than prose commentary alone.

nodes.name: all_critical_revisions_resolved
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every revision marked critical must be resolved before the final compliance gate passes.

nodes.name: _read_gate_result_json
nodes.summary: Reads a gate result JSON file for provenance validation, returning None when it is unreadable.

nodes.name: _validate_checkpoint_provenance
nodes.summary: Validates a published checkpoint's provenance quad against the gate results it claims, so a checkpoint cannot assert a pass the gate results do not show.

nodes.name: checkpoint_published
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: a durable checkpoint must exist with a valid provenance quad, the cross-run evidence that a validated phase state was actually published.

nodes.name: _read_json
nodes.summary: Defensive JSON reader for the Phase 2 scope artifacts, returning a categorised failing result on any read or parse problem.

nodes.name: all_mandatory_scope_covered
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every mandatory Tier 2B scope requirement must have an explicit scope_coverage entry, and any unresolved entry must be matched by a logged scope conflict.

nodes.name: _read_json
nodes.summary: Defensive JSON reader for the traceability predicates, mapping read and parse problems onto canonical failure categories.

nodes.name: _ref_value_is_present
nodes.summary: Decides whether a source-reference value counts as present, rejecting empty strings and placeholder values.

nodes.name: _extract_entries_for_source_ref
nodes.summary: Collects the entries of a Tier 2B extracted artifact that must each carry a source reference.

nodes.name: _extract_mapping_entries
nodes.summary: Collects the mapping entries of a topic-mapping artifact that must each carry a source reference.

nodes.name: source_refs_present
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every relevant entry in an extracted artifact must carry a non-empty source reference, so no extracted fact is unattributed.

nodes.name: all_mappings_have_source_refs
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every topic-mapping entry must cite its source section, which is what makes the Phase 2 mapping auditable.

nodes.name: timeline_predicates.py
nodes.summary: Scheduling-consistency predicates over the Phase 4 Gantt: timeline within the call-specified duration, every milestone carrying a verifiable criterion, work-package count within the instrument limit, a declared critical path, and dependency/schedule agreement.

nodes.name: types.py
nodes.summary: Defines PredicateResult, the uniform return type of every gate predicate, together with the five canonical failure-category constants that drive gate triage and the GateResult writer.

nodes.name: upstream_inputs.py
nodes.summary: Table mapping each gate_id to the substantive upstream source artifacts whose change invalidates its result. Generated derivatives such as call slices and directory paths are deliberately excluded so freshness tracking never fires on a deterministic regeneration.

nodes.name: versions.py
nodes.summary: Manifest, library and constitution version constants stamped into every gate result, so a result produced under a prior compilation is detected as stale rather than accepted.

nodes.name: backfill_gate_result_schema_id.py
nodes.summary: One-time idempotent migration that adds the required schema_id to legacy gate result files, discovering them from the runtime's own path registry. A file already declaring a different schema_id is reported as a conflict and never rewritten, since silent repair is the auto-correction the constitution forbids.

nodes.name: _read_json_object
nodes.summary: Defensive JSON object reader shared by the timeline predicates.

nodes.name: _extract_max_wp_values
nodes.summary: Reads the instrument registry for the maximum work-package and deliverable counts the active instrument allows.

nodes.name: timeline_within_duration
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the latest Gantt month must fit inside the call-specified project duration, the arithmetic half of the Phase 4 gate condition.

nodes.name: all_milestones_have_criteria
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: every milestone must declare a month, a verifiable achievement criterion and a responsible party.

nodes.name: wp_count_within_limit
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the designed work-package count must stay within the limit the active instrument's schema sets.

nodes.name: critical_path_present
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: the Gantt must declare a critical path, so no critical-path dependency is left unresolved at the Phase 4 gate.

nodes.name: dependency_schedule_consistency
nodes.summary: Gate predicate: each declared dependency must be consistent with the scheduled months of the tasks and work packages it links.

nodes.name: _resolve_max_end_month
nodes.summary: Resolves the latest end month of a dependency node, expanding a work package to its tasks.

nodes.name: _resolve_min_start_month
nodes.summary: Resolves the earliest start month of a dependency node, expanding a work package to its tasks.

nodes.name: PredicateResult
nodes.summary: The uniform result dataclass every predicate returns: passed, failure_category, reason and details, with a post-init rule that a failing result must carry a category.

nodes.name: _discover
nodes.summary: Discovers gate result files from three de-duplicated sources - the canonical path registry, the evaluator's fallback subdirectory and a shape-checked tier-4 sweep - instead of a glob that would miss sibling locations.

nodes.name: backfill
nodes.summary: Adds the required schema_id to each discovered gate result that lacks it, reporting a file carrying a different schema_id as a conflict rather than rewriting it.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses arguments, runs the dry-run or applied backfill, prints the report and exits non-zero when conflicts remain.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the DAG scheduler, invoked as `python -m runner`. Parses run scoping flags (--run-id, --phase, --node, --dry-run), loads the manifest graph and run context, optionally bootstraps phase prerequisites, dispatches the scheduler, and maps the run outcome onto four distinct process exit codes.
nodes.languageNotes: Python `__main__.py` package-executable convention; `load_dotenv()` is called at import time before any other runner import so transport configuration is present.

nodes.name: _parse_phase
nodes.summary: Normalizes the several accepted spellings of a --phase argument (`1`, `phase1`, `phase_01`) into a single integer phase number.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: The CLI driver: builds the argument parser, resolves repo root and manifest/library paths, enforces the mutual exclusion of --phase and --node, loads or initializes the RunContext, seeds phase prerequisites from durable Tier 4 gate evidence, runs the DAGScheduler, and translates RunSummary / RunAbortedError / DAGSchedulerError outcomes into exit codes 0-3.

nodes.name: agent_runtime.py
nodes.summary: The middle layer of the three-tier runtime stack: an orchestration adapter that loads agent and prompt specifications, resolves canonical tier inputs, sequences skill invocations through `run_skill()`, invokes Claude-free deterministic components, propagates failures, and determines `can_evaluate_exit_gate` by inspecting artifacts on disk. It never evaluates gates and never calls the scheduler.
nodes.languageNotes: The agent/prompt `.md` files it loads are specifications, not executable code — all domain reasoning happens inside the Claude invocations made by `run_skill()`.

nodes.name: AgentRuntimeError
nodes.summary: Exception raised for agent-runtime-layer faults such as a missing agent catalog entry or an unloadable prompt specification.

nodes.name: drafting_skills_superseded_by
nodes.summary: Returns the Phase-8 drafting skills that a given deterministic section assembler supersedes, so the monolithic drafter is not run when the assembler already composes the section from bounded sub-section drafts.

nodes.name: _load_agent_catalog
nodes.summary: Loads and caches `agent_catalog.yaml`, the authoritative registry of agent declarations (reads_from, writes_to, must_not) used to resolve inputs and constrain agent behavior.

nodes.name: _load_artifact_registry
nodes.summary: Loads the artifact schema specification so the runtime can map node IDs to the canonical artifact paths they produce and consume.

nodes.name: _load_prompt_spec
nodes.summary: Reads an agent's prompt specification Markdown file from disk, raising when the spec is absent.

nodes.name: _resolve_agent_inputs
nodes.summary: Resolves an agent's declared `reads_from` tier paths into concrete existing files on disk, expanding directory declarations and reporting which declared inputs are missing.

nodes.name: _resolve_skill_sequence
nodes.summary: Determines the ordered skill sequence for a node body from the manifest-resolved skill IDs, honoring suppression of drafting skills under reuse, preseed, or assembler supersession.

nodes.name: _resolve_budget_regime_safe
nodes.summary: Resolves the instrument's budget regime (lump-sum versus unit-cost) without raising, so skill applicability checks can degrade gracefully when the regime cannot be determined.
nodes.languageNotes: Reflects the instrument-conditional budget gate: lump-sum budgets come from the external planner, unit-cost budgets from a deterministic internal derivation.

nodes.name: _get_artifacts_produced_by_node
nodes.summary: Looks up every canonical artifact path a node is contractually expected to write, which is the basis for the on-disk gate-readiness check.

nodes.name: _determine_can_evaluate_exit_gate
nodes.summary: Decides whether the scheduler may evaluate the node's exit gate by inspecting actual file-system state for the gate-relevant artifacts, never by assuming that successful skill invocations imply artifact presence.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the constitutional rule that `can_evaluate_exit_gate` is derived from disk, not from optimistic assumption.

nodes.name: _get_exit_gate_for_node
nodes.summary: Reads the manifest to find which gate is bound as the given node's exit gate, so the runtime knows which artifacts are gate-relevant.

nodes.name: _resolve_instrument_type
nodes.summary: Resolves the active Horizon Europe instrument type (RIA/IA, CSA, MSCA, ERC and so on) from the Tier 3 call binding, which drives instrument-conditional skill applicability.

nodes.name: _context_sources_for
nodes.summary: Lists the upstream artifacts that must be passed as caller context into a given skill invocation.

nodes.name: _build_caller_context
nodes.summary: Assembles the caller-context payload handed to a skill invocation, reading the declared upstream artifacts from disk and threading prior-skill outputs through the sequence.

nodes.name: _missing_context_sources
nodes.summary: Returns the declared context sources that are absent from disk, so a skill is failed closed rather than invoked with incomplete context.

nodes.name: _resolve_auditable_artifact
nodes.summary: Identifies the artifact that an audit skill (traceability-check, compliance-check) should examine, so audit passes always target the authoritative section on disk even when drafting was skipped.

nodes.name: _check_skill_applicability
nodes.summary: Evaluates a skill's `applies_when` condition against the resolved instrument type and budget regime, so instrument-inapplicable skills are skipped rather than run against absent inputs.

nodes.name: run_agent
nodes.summary: The single public entry point of the agent runtime and the node body of every scheduler dispatch: it resolves the node's agent, inputs and skill sequence, runs decomposed drafting and deterministic components where bound, invokes each applicable skill through `run_skill()`, coordinates sub-agents and pre-gate agents, halts immediately on CONSTITUTIONAL_HALT, and returns an AgentResult carrying the invocation records and the disk-derived `can_evaluate_exit_gate` flag.
nodes.languageNotes: The only caller is the scheduler's `_dispatch_node()`; the function itself never evaluates a gate nor calls back into the scheduler.

nodes.name: _identify_agent_skills
nodes.summary: Resolves the skill IDs declared for an agent, used when the manifest node binding must be cross-checked against the agent catalog.

nodes.name: _refresh_inputs_from_outputs
nodes.summary: Folds the artifacts a skill just wrote back into the resolved input set, so later skills in the same node body see the freshly produced files.

nodes.name: _sub_agent_inputs_ready
nodes.summary: Checks on disk whether a sub-agent's or pre-gate agent's declared inputs are all present before that nested agent is coordinated within the same node body.

nodes.name: call_slicer.py
nodes.summary: The deterministic Step-0 input bounding pass: before any Claude invocation, it extracts the single target call entry from a large grouped work-programme JSON (338-794 KB) into a bounded ~5-10 KB call slice so downstream skills read only call-specific data. Pure Python with no Claude dependency and no domain reasoning.
nodes.languageNotes: Called once by `DAGScheduler.run()` before the dispatch loop; failure is non-blocking because skills fall back to reading the full grouped JSON.

nodes.name: CallSlicerError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when the call slice cannot be produced — missing selected-call binding, unknown work programme, no topic match, or a slice exceeding the 20 KB hard limit.

nodes.name: generate_call_slice
nodes.summary: Reads the Tier 3 selected call, locates its work programme in the grouped-JSON map, scans the destinations/calls structure for the matching topic code, and writes the bounded slice to `call_extracts/<topic_code>.slice.json`, failing closed when the result exceeds MAX_SLICE_BYTES.

nodes.name: checkpoint_publisher.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic node-body component that publishes the immutable Phase-8 `phase8_checkpoint.json` to Tier 4 after confirming the six Phase-8 gate results. Cross-run gate results are authorized by deterministic set membership against `accepted_upstream_gates` and recorded verbatim as a provenance quad, so the checkpoint stays auditable against durable evidence without re-stamping.
nodes.languageNotes: Replaces the retired `checkpoint-publish` skill once it was found to be entirely mechanical; the only non-deterministic field, `published_at`, is excluded from the byte-equal replay invariant.

nodes.name: CheckpointPublishError
nodes.summary: Exception raised on any structural fault — missing, malformed, non-pass or wrong-schema gate result, an unauthorized cross-run gate, or an attempt to overwrite an already-published checkpoint.

nodes.name: _read_json_dict
nodes.summary: Reads a required JSON object from disk, raising CheckpointPublishError when the file is missing, unreadable, or not a JSON object.

nodes.name: _validate_gate_result
nodes.summary: Confirms that a durable gate result artifact carries the expected schema ID and a `status: pass` verdict before the checkpoint may assert the gate passed.

nodes.name: _authorize_and_build_quad
nodes.summary: Authorizes a gate result whose durable run_id differs from the current run by deterministic set membership against `accepted_upstream_gates`, then copies the provenance quad (gate_id, original_run_id, evidence_path, input_fingerprint, versions) verbatim from the durable result.

nodes.name: _build_tier3_snapshot
nodes.summary: Captures the Tier 3 project-instantiation state referenced by the checkpoint so the published record identifies exactly which project data the Phase-8 outcome was built on.

nodes.name: publish_checkpoint
nodes.summary: The component entry point for node n08f: validates all six Phase-8 gate results, authorizes any cross-run evidence, assembles the checkpoint document with its optional `inherited_gate_provenance` array, and atomically writes the immutable artifact — refusing to overwrite a checkpoint already marked published.

nodes.name: dag_scheduler.py
nodes.summary: The top layer of the runtime stack and the largest module in the repository: it builds a read-only ManifestGraph from the compiled manifest, runs a synchronous dispatch loop over the DAG, and owns gate evaluation exclusively. Each dispatch follows the five-step contract (set running, entry gate, node body via run_agent, exit gate, NodeExecutionResult), propagates HARD_BLOCK to Phase 8 on budget-gate failure, and writes a durable RunSummary on every exit path.
nodes.languageNotes: Explicitly forbidden from calling `run_skill()` directly; all skill execution flows through the agent runtime, and the exit gate is skipped if and only if the entry gate failed, the agent body failed, or `can_evaluate_exit_gate` is False.

nodes.name: _gate_result_repo_path
nodes.summary: Resolves a gate ID to its canonical repo-relative Tier 4 gate result path via the gate result registry.

nodes.name: format_unsatisfied_condition
nodes.summary: Renders an unsatisfied DAG incoming condition as a human-readable line for CLI and summary output.

nodes.name: format_evidence_violation
nodes.summary: Renders a predecessor-evidence violation dict (node, gate, evidence path, reason code) as a readable diagnostic line.

nodes.name: verify_released_predecessors
nodes.summary: Re-verifies every transitively upstream `released` predecessor against its durable Tier 4 exit-gate result — present, schema-valid, status pass, and content-fresh — because a persisted state string in `.claude/runs/` is runtime memory rather than source truth. Read-only and scheduler-side: it writes nothing and returns one violation dict per unproven claim so a scoped step fails closed.

nodes.name: _collect_upstream_nodes
nodes.summary: Recursively accumulates all transitive upstream node IDs for a target set by tracing incoming conditions, terminating on acyclic graphs via a visited set.

nodes.name: bootstrap_phase_prerequisites
nodes.summary: Seeds upstream prerequisite nodes as `released` in a fresh RunContext from durable Tier 4 gate evidence, so `--phase N` execution can proceed with a new run-id per invocation. This is a bootstrap step run before dispatch, not resume logic — readiness still derives from current RunContext state.

nodes.name: DAGSchedulerError
nodes.summary: Base exception for scheduler configuration faults such as an empty phase scope, an unmatched node scope, or a dispatched node with no exit gate defined.

nodes.name: RunSummary
nodes.summary: Typed dataclass capturing the full outcome of a run — overall status, node states in manifest order, terminal nodes reached, stalled and hard-blocked nodes, the gate results index, and per-node failure details. It computes scope-aware status for `--phase` and `--node` runs and writes `run_summary.json` before `run()` returns or raises.

nodes.name: RunAbortedError
nodes.summary: Raised when in-scope nodes remain pending after the dispatch loop exits; carries the already-built RunSummary on `.summary` so the CLI can still report the run.

nodes.name: IncomingCondition
nodes.summary: Immutable record of one DAG edge condition: the source node whose release unblocks the target, as declared in the manifest.

nodes.name: ManifestGraph
nodes.summary: Read-only in-memory graph built from `manifest.compile.yaml`: exposes canonical node IDs, entry and exit gate bindings, terminal flags, incoming conditions, readiness checks against current RunContext state, phase membership, and resolution of `--node` scope from canonical IDs or phase+substep shorthand.

nodes.name: DAGScheduler
nodes.summary: The synchronous dispatch loop and sole owner of gate evaluation. `run()` generates the Step-0 call slice, iterates ready nodes, and settles stalled ones; `_dispatch_node()` implements the five-step contract — set running, evaluate entry gate, execute the node body via `run_agent()`, evaluate the exit gate, return a NodeExecutionResult — applying Phase-8 preseed and reuse decisions, suppressing draft-consuming components, propagating HARD_BLOCK from the budget gate, and reloading RunContext after every gate evaluation.
nodes.languageNotes: Failure origins form a closed set of three (`entry_gate`, `agent_body`, `exit_gate`) and are persisted alongside node state; node states are `pending`, `running`, `released`, `blocked_at_entry`, `blocked_at_exit`, `deterministic_pass_semantic_pending`, `hard_block_upstream`.

nodes.name: deterministic_components.py
nodes.summary: The generic binding substrate for deterministic components — Claude-free, pure-Python node-body passes that read declared artifacts and write canonical ones under a determinism guarantee. A node declares component IDs in the manifest, the node resolver returns them, and this module resolves each ID in its registry, invokes it, and hands back a ComponentInvocationRecord for `AgentResult.invoked_components`.
nodes.languageNotes: Each registered component is lazily imported inside its thin `_run_*` adapter, so a broken or optional component module cannot break the registry at import time.

nodes.name: _run_dependency_normalizer
nodes.summary: Adapter for the Phase-4 dependency normalizer — the one pre-existing hardcoded deterministic pass, now registered so it runs through the same generic component path as the rest.

nodes.name: _run_unit_cost_budget_deriver
nodes.summary: Adapter for the unit-cost budget deriver, the sanctioned internal budget source for unit-cost instruments: a byte-equal-checked computation of confirmed months by published rates by host-country coefficient, which is a derivation rather than an estimate.
nodes.languageNotes: For lump-sum instruments budget computation stays external; only unit-cost instruments are derived internally, and determinism is the anti-fabrication guarantee.

nodes.name: _run_checkpoint_publisher
nodes.summary: Adapter that invokes `publish_checkpoint` to write the immutable Phase-8 checkpoint, returning the written artifact path to the invocation record.

nodes.name: partition_draft_consuming
nodes.summary: Splits a list of component IDs into kept and suppressed by draft consumption, preserving order and deliberately keeping unknown IDs so they still reach `invoke_component` and fail closed there rather than being silently dropped.

nodes.name: invoke_component
nodes.summary: Resolves a component ID against the registry, invokes it with the run ID and repo root, and captures the artifact paths it wrote. It never raises for a component fault: an unknown ID or raised exception comes back as a failure ComponentInvocationRecord, which the agent runtime maps to AGENT_EXECUTION_ERROR with `can_evaluate_exit_gate=False`.

nodes.name: manifest_reader.py
nodes.summary: Read-only loader for `manifest.compile.yaml` that indexes the gate registry by gate ID and exposes each gate's `predicate_refs`. Under Approach B the manifest is the predicate composition source and the gate rules library is only the implementation registry, so a predicate runs only if the manifest names it.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately does not validate manifest/library version coupling — that remains the responsibility of `GateLibrary`.

nodes.name: ManifestReaderError
nodes.summary: Base exception for manifest loading and structural errors.

nodes.name: ManifestGateNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Raised when a requested gate ID is not present in the manifest gate registry.

nodes.name: ManifestReader
nodes.summary: In-memory representation of the loaded compiled manifest, constructed via `load()`. Indexes the gate registry by gate ID and answers `get_predicate_refs`, `gate_ids`, and `has_predicate_refs` for the gate evaluator.

nodes.name: node_resolver.py
nodes.summary: Read-only resolution layer that maps a canonical manifest node ID to its agent, sub-agent and pre-gate agent identifiers, its deterministic component bindings, its skill IDs, its phase ID, and the on-disk paths of the agent definition and prompt spec. It contains no business logic, executes nothing, and evaluates no gates.
nodes.languageNotes: The manifest `node_registry` is the sole authoritative source for node-to-agent binding; this module only reads it and queries the file system.

nodes.name: NodeResolverError
nodes.summary: Exception raised for an unknown node ID or a missing agent definition / prompt spec file.

nodes.name: NodeResolver
nodes.summary: Loads the compiled manifest and answers every node-binding question the runtime needs: `resolve_agent_id`, `resolve_sub_agent_id`, `resolve_pre_gate_agent_id`, `resolve_deterministic_components`, `resolve_skill_ids`, `resolve_phase_id`, plus the agent definition and prompt spec paths. All methods are side-effect free.

nodes.name: phase8_preseed.py
nodes.summary: Phase-8 manual preseed: copies an operator-prepared section artifact from the Tier 4 preseed directory into its canonical Tier 5 path before agent dispatch and suppresses only the primary drafting skill. Unlike reuse it needs no `.reuse.json` metadata, no input fingerprint and no prior run ID; audit skills, exit gate evaluation and downstream assembly still run normally.
nodes.languageNotes: Fail-closed by design: an existing but invalid preseed file (bad JSON, wrong schema_id, missing required fields) blocks the node before dispatch rather than silently falling back to LLM drafting.

nodes.name: _validation_status_inconsistency
nodes.summary: Checks that a preseeded section's declared validation status is consistent with the rolled-up status of its claims, so an artifact cannot overstate how well evidenced it is.

nodes.name: Phase8PreseedResult
nodes.summary: Immutable three-way result of a preseed attempt: applied (artifact copied, audit written, skill to skip), not applied without error (no preseed file, proceed normally), or not applied with error (invalid preseed, block the node).

nodes.name: maybe_apply_phase8_preseed
nodes.summary: The entry point the scheduler calls before dispatching a Phase-8 drafting node: looks for a preseed file for the node, validates its JSON, schema ID, required fields and claim-status consistency, copies it to the canonical Tier 5 path, writes the preseed audit record, and returns which drafting skill to suppress.

nodes.name: _write_preseed_audit
nodes.summary: Writes the durable Tier 4 audit record for an applied preseed, naming the source file, the canonical destination, the suppressed drafting skill and the current run ID.

nodes.name: phase8_reuse.py
nodes.summary: Minimal, fail-closed reuse layer that avoids rerunning the expensive Phase-8 section drafting for n08a/n08b/n08c when a previously produced section artifact is still input-equivalent and gate-approved. Provides pure functions for input fingerprinting, SHA-256 artifact hashing, reuse metadata I/O, eligibility validation and cross-run ownership checks; it evaluates no gates and invokes no agents.
nodes.languageNotes: Any parse error, missing field, hash mismatch or missing gate result falls back to normal execution — no artifact is ever reused without passing every eligibility check.

nodes.name: ReuseDecision
nodes.summary: Immutable record of a reuse verdict for one node: whether the artifact is reused, the reuse mode, the artifact path and run ID it came from, and the reason the decision was reached.

nodes.name: _collect_fingerprint_files
nodes.summary: Enumerates, in a stable order, the upstream input files whose contents define a Phase-8 node's input fingerprint.

nodes.name: compute_input_fingerprint
nodes.summary: Computes a content-based hash over a node's collected input files, the value against which a candidate reuse artifact's recorded fingerprint must match exactly.

nodes.name: artifact_sha256
nodes.summary: Returns the SHA-256 digest of an artifact file, used to prove the on-disk section has not changed since the reuse metadata was written.

nodes.name: read_artifact_run_id
nodes.summary: Reads the `run_id` stamped inside a section artifact so the runtime can tell current-run output from a prior-run candidate.

nodes.name: load_reuse_metadata
nodes.summary: Loads a node's reuse metadata sidecar from the Tier 4 reuse directory, returning None when it is absent or unreadable.

nodes.name: write_reuse_metadata
nodes.summary: Writes the reuse metadata sidecar after a Phase-8 node passes its exit gate, recording the policy version, artifact SHA-256, input fingerprint and owning run ID so a later run can validate reuse.

nodes.name: _load_gate_result
nodes.summary: Reads a durable gate result artifact so reuse eligibility can require that the candidate artifact was actually gate-approved.

nodes.name: validate_reuse_candidate
nodes.summary: The central eligibility check: confirms the node is reuse-eligible, the artifact and its metadata exist, the recorded SHA-256 and input fingerprint still match, the owning gate result passed, and the claim statuses roll up consistently — returning a ReuseDecision that falls back to normal execution on any doubt.

nodes.name: _audit_report_exists
nodes.summary: Confirms a current-run audit report exists for a required audit skill, since reuse suppresses only drafting and the traceability and compliance checks must still have run this run.

nodes.name: is_reuse_owned_artifact_valid
nodes.summary: Validates ownership of a reused section artifact whose run_id differs from the current run, enforcing ten conjunctive fail-closed conditions: node eligibility, a persisted reuse decision in drafting-skipped mode matching the artifact run ID and canonical path, metadata on disk with matching hash and fingerprint, current-run audit reports for both audit skills, and structural validation of schema ID, validation status and traceability footer.
nodes.languageNotes: Called by the `artifact_owned_by_run` gate predicate — it is the single sanctioned exception to the rule that a gate-relevant artifact must carry the current run's ID.

nodes.name: phase8_skip_binding.py
nodes.summary: The single authoritative `node_id -> drafting-skill-id` map for Phase-8 section nodes, plus the import-time assertions and dispatch-time validation that keep every derived table in agreement with it. It exists because the skip binding was once named independently in four places with none checked against the manifest, which made a stale skip id a silent no-op that let the drafter overwrite a preseeded or reused section.
nodes.languageNotes: A pure data-and-validation leaf module: it imports nothing from `runner`, names no project facts, evaluates no gates and invokes no agents.

nodes.name: SkipBindingError
nodes.summary: Raised at import time when a derived skip-binding table has drifted from the single authoritative map, and at dispatch when the chosen skip ID does not resolve against the node's manifest skill IDs.

nodes.name: drafting_skill_for
nodes.summary: Returns the drafting skill ID bound to a Phase-8 section node, the one place that answers which skill a node drafts with.

nodes.name: validate_skip_binding
nodes.summary: Resolves the chosen skip ID against the node's manifest-resolved `skill_ids` at dispatch time, failing closed on any drift between this map and the manifest rather than recording a skip that silently matches nothing.

nodes.name: assert_agrees_with_source
nodes.summary: Import-time guard asserting that a derived table maps the same skill for every node as the authoritative binding, so the copies in the reuse, preseed and agent-runtime tables can never drift apart.

nodes.name: assert_nodes_match_source
nodes.summary: Import-time guard asserting that a derived table covers exactly the same node set as the authoritative binding, closing the eligible-but-unbound defect where a node recorded a skipped drafting skill and still recomposed over stale drafts.

nodes.name: run_context.py
nodes.summary: Owns the per-run state directory `.claude/runs/<run_id>/`, holding `run_manifest.json` (run identity, versions, node state map, HARD_BLOCK metadata, accepted upstream gates, reuse decisions) and `reuse_policy.json`. The RunContext is the single point of truth for node state during a run and is read back and updated after every gate evaluation.
nodes.languageNotes: Constitutionally this is runtime execution memory, not source truth — a persisted `released` state must still be provable against durable Tier 4 gate evidence.

nodes.name: RunContext
nodes.summary: Creates or loads the run directory and manages all per-run state: node state get/set across the seven-state machine, per-node failure details (origin, reason, category), accepted upstream gate records for phase-scoped continuation, reuse decisions, artifact reuse approvals, HARD_BLOCK propagation to downstream nodes, and atomic persistence of the run manifest.
nodes.languageNotes: States: `pending`, `running`, `released`, `blocked_at_entry`, `blocked_at_exit`, `deterministic_pass_semantic_pending`, and `hard_block_upstream` for Phase-8 nodes frozen by a failed budget gate.

nodes.name: runtime_models.py
nodes.summary: Defines the frozen-dataclass data contracts exchanged between the three runtime layers — SkillResult, AgentResult and NodeExecutionResult plus the two invocation records — together with the closed vocabularies of valid failure origins and failure categories. Contains no business logic: it evaluates no gates, invokes nothing, and modifies no scheduler state.
nodes.languageNotes: All types are frozen dataclasses, and the valid value sets are `frozenset` constants, so a contract violation is a construction-time failure rather than a silently tolerated string.

nodes.name: SkillResult
nodes.summary: The contract returned by `run_skill()` to the agent runtime: success or failure status, the repo-relative paths of artifacts written, and on failure a human-readable reason plus one of the five skill failure categories.

nodes.name: SkillInvocationRecord
nodes.summary: One entry in the agent runtime's ordered record of skill invocations, pairing the skill ID with its SkillResult so the node body's execution is fully auditable.

nodes.name: ComponentInvocationRecord
nodes.summary: One entry in `AgentResult.invoked_components`, recording a deterministic Claude-free component invocation: its ID, status, the artifacts it wrote, and the failure reason when it faulted.

nodes.name: AgentResult
nodes.summary: The contract returned by `run_agent()` to the scheduler: status, the disk-derived `can_evaluate_exit_gate` flag, a failure origin that is always `agent_body`, a failure category drawn from the skill categories plus SKILL_FAILURE and AGENT_EXECUTION_ERROR, and the ordered `invoked_skills` and `invoked_components` records.

nodes.name: NodeExecutionResult
nodes.summary: The contract returned by `_dispatch_node()` to the scheduler's run loop: the canonical node ID, the terminal state, the failure origin from the closed set of three, whether the exit gate was actually evaluated, and the AgentResult (None when the entry gate failed before the body ran).

nodes.name: claude_transport.py
nodes.summary: Sole runtime transport boundary for Claude invocations: subprocesses the local `claude` CLI in print mode, reassembles the response from multi-turn stream-json output, and enforces timeouts with a full process-tree kill. Authenticated by the user's Claude Code Max subscription, so no Anthropic API key is involved.
nodes.languageNotes: Platform-split Popen kwargs (POSIX new session vs Windows no-window creation flags) plus a stdin writer thread are what make the CLI child both drainable and killable as a tree.

nodes.name: ClaudeTransportError
nodes.summary: Base transport exception carrying the diagnostic context of a failed CLI invocation - the command, exit code and captured output.

nodes.name: ClaudeCLIUnavailableError
nodes.summary: Raised when no `claude` executable can be resolved at all, distinguishing a missing CLI from a failed invocation.

nodes.name: ClaudeCLIRateLimitError
nodes.summary: Raised when the CLI reports subscription usage-limit exhaustion, carrying the detected rate-limit notice line for the operator.

nodes.name: ClaudeCLITimeoutError
nodes.summary: Raised when the CLI exceeds its invocation timeout, carrying the elapsed time and the process-tree snapshot taken before the kill.

nodes.name: ClaudeCLIResolution
nodes.summary: NamedTuple recording how the `claude` executable was resolved - the absolute path and whether it came from the environment pin or the OS search path.

nodes.name: AssistantTurn
nodes.summary: NamedTuple for one assistant turn parsed out of stream-json, carrying its text and whether it is a restart-style continuation of a truncated turn.

nodes.name: _effective_max_output_tokens
nodes.summary: Resolves the output-token ceiling handed to the CLI, preferring a positive ORCHESTRATOR_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS override and ignoring an invalid value with a warning rather than passing it through.

nodes.name: _rate_limit_notice
nodes.summary: Scans stdout and stderr line by line for usage-limit signals and returns the first matching line, surfacing subscription quota exhaustion as a human-readable notice.

nodes.name: resolve_claude_cli
nodes.summary: Resolves which `claude` executable to spawn, honouring the ORCHESTRATOR_CLAUDE_CLI_PATH pin (quotes stripped, `~` and env vars expanded) before falling back to the OS search path.

nodes.name: _announce_cli_resolution
nodes.summary: Logs the resolved executable once per distinct path, so a run record names which installed CLI build served its invocations.

nodes.name: _splice_continuation
nodes.summary: Splices a restart-style continuation onto a truncated turn: when an output-token cut lands inside a fenced block the CLI re-opens the fence and re-emits the element, so the overlap must be detected rather than appended.

nodes.name: _join_assistant_turns
nodes.summary: Joins assistant turns with no separator so a turn split mid-token rejoins seamlessly, with restart continuations spliced instead of concatenated.

nodes.name: _reassemble_stream_json
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the complete assistant-visible text from `--output-format stream-json` events, recovering every assistant turn rather than only the final message the CLI's text mode prints.

nodes.name: _tree_killable_popen_kwargs
nodes.summary: Platform-specific Popen keyword arguments that make the spawned CLI tree signalable as a group - a new session on POSIX, no-window creation flags on Windows.

nodes.name: _kill_process_tree
nodes.summary: Forcibly terminates the child and every descendant including the CLI's Node subtree, because Python's own timeout handling kills only the direct child and orphans the rest.

nodes.name: _child_tree_snapshot
nodes.summary: Best-effort process-tree snapshot taken on the timeout path before the kill, so a recurrence of the pre-main CLI stall records what the hung tree actually looked like.

nodes.name: _drain_after_kill
nodes.summary: Drains and reaps the killed child's pipes to return any buffered output; it never raises, so a drain failure cannot mask the transport error being surfaced.

nodes.name: invoke_claude_text
nodes.summary: The single public transport entry point: builds the `claude -p` argument vector, streams the prompt over stdin, reassembles the response, and raises typed transport errors on timeout, non-zero exit, empty output or a missing CLI.

nodes.name: json_extract.py
nodes.summary: Pure string-to-JSON helper that recovers the first JSON object from a model response - bare, fenced, or wrapped in prose - shared by the semantic dispatcher and the out-of-band harness judge. It never repairs: an unparseable response yields None and the caller decides what that means.

nodes.name: extract_first_json_object
nodes.summary: Returns the first top-level JSON object in a response by trying the whole string, then a fenced block, then the first brace span; rejects a nested object pulled out of a top-level array and never raises or repairs malformed input.

nodes.name: semantic_dispatch.py
nodes.summary: Dispatches each semantic gate predicate to its designated agent through the runtime transport: reads the artifacts under evaluation, builds a system prompt stating the constitutional rule and the mandatory result schema, and returns the agent's structured verdict. Dispatch failures become schema-valid fail results flagged `_dispatch_error`, never fabricated passes.
nodes.languageNotes: No local rule about what constitutes a violation is encoded here - the agent reasons from the artifact content and the rule quoted in its system prompt.

nodes.name: SemanticPredicateConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing one semantic predicate - its function name, designated agent, description, and the constitutional rule it enforces.

nodes.name: validate_semantic_result
nodes.summary: Validates an agent result against the result schema, rejecting any `fail` finding that omits `violated_rule` or `evidence_path` and returning a machine-readable reason for every rejection.

nodes.name: _dispatch_error_result
nodes.summary: Builds a schema-valid fail result with `_dispatch_error: True` and empty findings, so a transport or parse failure surfaces as a gate failure with its real cause rather than as a semantic verdict.

nodes.name: _write_semantic_diagnostics
nodes.summary: Writes a diagnostic bundle for a dispatch failure under `.claude/semantic_diag/`, mirroring the skill runtime's diagnostic pattern; a failure to write is swallowed rather than masking the original error.

nodes.name: _read_artifacts
nodes.summary: Reads artifact content from every string-valued predicate arg, expanding a directory arg to its direct-child JSON files and silently skipping absent paths - presence is the deterministic layer's responsibility.

nodes.name: _build_system_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the agent system prompt stating its constitutional role, the predicate to evaluate, the rule it enforces, and the exact JSON schema the response must conform to.

nodes.name: _build_user_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the user turn carrying the artifact content the agent must inspect.

nodes.name: _extract_json
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper delegating JSON recovery from the agent response to the shared extractor.

nodes.name: _resolve_semantic_backend
nodes.summary: Resolves and caches the transport backend for semantic predicates, sharing the skill runtime's provider resolution so production-mode enforcement applies equally here.

nodes.name: _invoke_via_backend
nodes.summary: Routes the invocation to the Claude CLI, the native Bedrock Converse backend, or a generic OpenAI-compatible backend according to the resolved provider config, returning the raw response text.

nodes.name: invoke_agent
nodes.summary: Invokes the designated agent end to end - artifact reads, prompt assembly, backend invocation, JSON recovery - and returns the raw result dict for schema validation by the caller.

nodes.name: dispatch_semantic_predicate
nodes.summary: Public entry point called by the gate evaluator once deterministic predicates have passed; delegates to invoke_agent and leaves result validation to the caller.

nodes.name: skill_runtime.py
nodes.summary: Claude runtime transport adapter for skills: loads a skill `.md` specification, resolves canonical inputs from disk, assembles the prompt in TAPM or cli-prompt mode, invokes Claude, parses and validates the structured response against the artifact schema, writes canonical artifacts atomically, and returns a SkillResult. It holds no domain knowledge.
nodes.languageNotes: Skill `.md` files are specifications, not executable code - nothing here interprets them. Claude performs the reasoning; Python owns every write and never silently repairs a response.

nodes.name: SkillRuntimeError
nodes.summary: Exception raised for skill runtime configuration and loading failures, distinct from a SkillResult carrying a structured failure category.

nodes.name: _run_id_echo_directive
nodes.summary: Builds the directive instructing Claude to copy the run_id verbatim rather than retype it - a regenerated UUID looks plausible but is wrong, and the validator treats it as a failure.

nodes.name: _resolve_transport_backend
nodes.summary: Resolves and caches the active transport backend from the ORCHESTRATOR_TRANSPORT_* environment, defaulting to the Claude CLI path when unset.

nodes.name: _load_skill_catalog
nodes.summary: Loads and caches `skill_catalog.yaml`, the source of each skill's reads_from, writes_to and constitutional constraints.

nodes.name: _load_artifact_schemas
nodes.summary: Loads and caches `artifact_schema_specification.yaml`, the authority for canonical artifact paths and their required fields.

nodes.name: _find_schema_for_path
nodes.summary: Finds the artifact schema entry whose canonical_path matches a given path, searching every known schema section.

nodes.name: _extract_schema_requirements
nodes.summary: Extracts the schema_id value and the required field names from a schema entry.

nodes.name: _sanitize_filename
nodes.summary: Sanitizes a descriptor into a filesystem-safe component for diagnostic filenames.

nodes.name: _is_contextual_descriptor
nodes.summary: Decides whether an input descriptor is contextual rather than a canonical artifact path, so context-only inputs are not validated as artifacts on disk.

nodes.name: _resolve_inputs
nodes.summary: Reads the skill's declared `reads_from` artifacts from disk and merges them with caller-supplied inputs, keyed by repo-relative path.

nodes.name: _validate_skill_inputs
nodes.summary: Verifies every declared input is present and non-empty, treating a path that is both read and written as an upsert target where an empty object is a valid initial state.

nodes.name: _anchor_field
nodes.summary: Returns the first required non-metadata field of a schema - the key a multi-artifact response is anchored on, by both the prompt directive and the canonical writer, so the two must agree.

nodes.name: _artifacts_under_directory
nodes.summary: Searches the artifact schema sections for every canonical artifact living under a directory path, returning each with its schema entry.

nodes.name: _resolve_output_artifacts
nodes.summary: Expands a `writes_to` entry into the canonical artifacts it covers - a directory fanning out to every artifact beneath it - dropping entries that resolve to nothing.

nodes.name: _collect_schema_hints
nodes.summary: Resolves `writes_to` into ordered canonical schema hints - path, schema_id and required fields - and reports whether any schema requires a run_id. The field order is part of the contract.

nodes.name: _multi_artifact_directive
nodes.summary: Builds the prompt directive naming the top-level anchor keys a multi-artifact response must carry, kept in agreement with how the canonical writer extracts each sub-artifact.

nodes.name: _assemble_skill_prompt
nodes.summary: Assembles the cli-prompt mode system and user prompts with every resolved input serialized inline.

nodes.name: _assemble_tapm_prompt
nodes.summary: Assembles Tool-Augmented Prompt Mode prompts that pass declared input *paths* instead of serialized contents, so Claude reads them from disk through the Read tool and the prompt stays bounded.

nodes.name: _invoke_claude
