nodes.summary: Invokes the shared Claude transport and returns either the response text or an error message, keeping transport exceptions out of the main control flow.

nodes.name: _classify_transport_failure
nodes.summary: Maps a transport exception onto a diagnostic failure class - timeout, non-zero exit, empty output, CLI unavailable, or other.

nodes.name: _write_transport_failure_diagnostics
nodes.summary: Writes a uniform diagnostic bundle - structured meta JSON plus prompt and stdout/stderr companion files - for every transport failure class in both execution modes.

nodes.name: _json_break_point
nodes.summary: Describes in one clause where a response stopped being valid JSON, so a break tens of thousands of characters in is actionable instead of reported as a generic non-JSON response.

nodes.name: _extract_json_response
nodes.summary: Extracts the artifact JSON from Claude's response, handling bare, fenced and prose-wrapped payloads and picking the real object by largest-span candidate competition so a fenced decoy from an intermediate turn cannot win.

nodes.name: _validate_skill_output
nodes.summary: Checks a parsed skill response against its schema expectations: a missing or regenerated run_id, a wrong schema_id, or a present artifact_status are validation failures, never auto-corrected.

nodes.name: _atomic_write
nodes.summary: Writes a canonical artifact atomically via a same-directory temp file plus read-back validation, so the canonical path is never left partially written.

nodes.name: run_skill
nodes.summary: Executes one skill end to end - input validation, prompt assembly in the chosen mode, Claude invocation, response extraction, schema validation and atomic canonical writes - returning a SkillResult whose failure_category classifies any break in that chain.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel for the backend-agnostic transport package, re-exporting only the dependency-free surface - provider capabilities, provider config and presets, the error taxonomy, the tool executor and the tool loop - so importing the package never pulls in the optional httpx or boto3 clients.

nodes.name: bedrock_converse.py
nodes.summary: Native AWS Bedrock Converse backend implementing the ToolLoopBackend protocol through boto3, bypassing the OpenAI-compatible proxy and using the standard AWS credential chain plus inference profiles for on-demand throughput.
nodes.languageNotes: boto3 is imported inside a try/except so the module stays importable when the optional dependency is absent.

nodes.name: BedrockConverseBackend
nodes.summary: Callable backend that converts OpenAI-shaped messages and tool schemas into the Bedrock Converse format, invokes bedrock-runtime, extracts the response text and token usage, and classifies boto3 client errors into the shared transport taxonomy.

nodes.name: capabilities.py
nodes.summary: Static per-provider capability metadata - streaming, tool calling, structured-output level, usage reporting, auth type and OpenAI compatibility - declared as a frozen dataclass registry with no dynamic detection or extra API calls.

nodes.name: ProviderCapabilities
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass declaring one provider's static feature surface, consulted by the benchmark engine and the error-handling layer rather than negotiated at runtime.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Resolves the ORCHESTRATOR_TRANSPORT_* environment (and named presets) into a ProviderConfig, selecting among the claude_cli, bedrock, bedrock_converse, together_ai, ollama and generic OpenAI-compatible backends, and constructs the chosen backend with optional imports deferred.
nodes.languageNotes: The httpx and boto3 imports live inside the builder functions, so the default Claude CLI path never requires either dependency.

nodes.name: TransportPreset
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass bundling a named preset's backend, endpoint, model, region and capability declarations.

nodes.name: ProviderConfig
nodes.summary: Resolved transport configuration - backend name, endpoint, model, credentials and capabilities - that the backend factories and callers consume.

nodes.name: validate_bedrock_model_id
nodes.summary: Checks a model identifier against the Bedrock `<provider>.<model>` format.

nodes.name: is_production_mode
nodes.summary: Reports whether production mode is active, which gates the set of admissible backends.

nodes.name: _enforce_production_backend
nodes.summary: Rejects any non-production backend when production mode is active, raising ValueError rather than silently downgrading the transport.

nodes.name: list_transport_presets
nodes.summary: Returns the names of all registered transport presets.

nodes.name: get_transport_preset
nodes.summary: Looks up a named transport preset, raising ValueError for an unrecognised name.

nodes.name: resolve_provider_config_from_preset
nodes.summary: Resolves a ProviderConfig from a named preset, letting explicit environment variables override preset defaults under a backend-safety rule that prevents a mismatched backend/endpoint pairing.

nodes.name: resolve_provider_config
nodes.summary: Reads the transport environment and returns the resolved ProviderConfig, delegating to the preset resolver when ORCHESTRATOR_TRANSPORT_PRESET is set.

nodes.name: _resolve_bedrock
nodes.summary: Resolves Bedrock configuration for the bedrock-mantle OpenAI-compatible endpoint, constructing the regional URL and validating the model identifier.

nodes.name: _resolve_bedrock_converse
nodes.summary: Resolves native Bedrock Converse configuration - region, model and inference profile - for the boto3 backend.

nodes.name: _resolve_together_ai
nodes.summary: Resolves Together AI endpoint, model and API-key configuration.

nodes.name: _resolve_ollama
nodes.summary: Resolves local Ollama endpoint and model configuration, which needs no API key.

nodes.name: _resolve_generic
nodes.summary: Resolves a generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint configuration from explicit environment variables.

nodes.name: build_openai_backend
nodes.summary: Constructs an OpenAICompatBackend from a resolved config, deferring the httpx import to the point a non-Claude backend is actually needed.

nodes.name: build_converse_backend
nodes.summary: Constructs a BedrockConverseBackend from a resolved bedrock_converse config, converting any OpenAI-format tool schemas internally.

nodes.name: errors.py
nodes.summary: Transport-layer error taxonomy for the OpenAI-compatible backends: an ErrorCategory enum aligned with the SkillResult failure categories, typed exceptions carrying retryability metadata, and an HTTP status-to-exception normalizer.

nodes.name: ErrorCategory
nodes.summary: String enum of transport failure categories - rate limited, provider error, auth failure, malformed request, model not found, timeout - each annotated with whether it is retryable.

nodes.name: OpenAICompatTransportError
nodes.summary: Base transport exception for OpenAI-compatible backends, carrying its error category, retryability flag and a truncated response body for diagnostics.

nodes.name: OpenAICompatAuthError
nodes.summary: Raised on HTTP 401/403 or an AWS access-denied error; non-retryable.

nodes.name: OpenAICompatRateLimitError
nodes.summary: Raised on HTTP 429 or a provider throttling exception; retryable.

nodes.name: OpenAICompatProviderError
nodes.summary: Raised on provider-side 5xx, service-unavailable or internal-failure responses; retryable.

nodes.name: OpenAICompatTimeoutError
nodes.summary: Raised when a provider request exceeds its timeout.

nodes.name: OpenAICompatModelNotFoundError
nodes.summary: Raised on HTTP 404 or a missing-resource error naming an unknown model; non-retryable.

nodes.name: normalize_http_error
nodes.summary: Maps an HTTP status code and response body onto a typed transport exception carrying its category and retryability metadata.

nodes.name: openai_compatible.py
nodes.summary: HTTP backend implementing the ToolLoopBackend protocol by POSTing to any OpenAI Chat Completions endpoint - used for Bedrock via bedrock-mantle, Together AI and Ollama. Requires httpx, which the config factory imports lazily.

nodes.name: OpenAICompatBackend
nodes.summary: Callable backend that builds the chat-completions payload, posts it with httpx, normalizes HTTP errors into the shared taxonomy, and extracts the message text, tool calls and token usage.

nodes.name: tool_executor.py
nodes.summary: Local Read/Glob tool executor that emulates the file access Claude Code provides natively, for non-Claude backends whose tool loop Python must drive. Read-only by construction, with path authorisation applied after symlink resolution and every denial returned as a structured tool error.
nodes.languageNotes: Containment is checked with Path.resolve() plus Path.relative_to, which is what makes `../` escapes and symlink traversal out of the declared input roots impossible rather than merely detected.

nodes.name: ToolExecutor
nodes.summary: Honours or denies a model's Read/Glob tool calls against the repository root and the skill's declared input prefixes, tracking bytes read and files touched; it exposes no write, edit or delete tool at all.

nodes.name: is_within
nodes.summary: Returns whether a resolved path lies inside a resolved root - the symlink- and `../`-safe containment check every authorisation path depends on.

nodes.name: tool_loop.py
nodes.summary: Drives the iterative request to tool_calls to execute to re-send cycle for backends without native Read/Glob support, bounded by a max-round limit and deliberately decoupled from any particular HTTP client.

nodes.name: ToolLoopResponse
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing a loop outcome - the final text, rounds taken, tool calls executed and accumulated token usage.

nodes.name: ToolLoopBackend
nodes.summary: Protocol a backend must satisfy to be driven by the tool loop: callable on a message list, returning a response dict.

nodes.name: FakeBackend
nodes.summary: Test double returning a pre-programmed sequence of responses, including synthetic tool calls, so the loop can be exercised without a live provider.

nodes.name: run_tool_loop
nodes.summary: Runs the tool-call loop against a backend callable, executing each honoured Read/Glob call through the sandboxed executor, injecting structured errors for unknown tool names or malformed arguments, and stopping after max_rounds to bound runaway model behaviour.

nodes.name: graph_canonical_pack.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic, Claude-free deriver that builds the Phase-8 canonical reference pack (objectives, outcomes, work packages, deliverables, partners) from graph vault nodes instead of docs/** JSON, so the pack and the compiled prose share one source and cannot drift. Operator-declared assumptions are read from a separate substrate and quarantined into their own array rather than merged into confirmed facts.
nodes.languageNotes: Every emitted field is a verbatim copy of declared node front-matter; the only computed value is a pure dict lookup from evidence_strength to a provenance tag, which is what makes the same vault yield a byte-identical pack.

nodes.name: _tag
nodes.summary: Stamps a pack entry with its source node id and the provenance tag derived from that node's evidence_strength via the Appendix-B lookup.

nodes.name: _bound_extraction_nodes
nodes.summary: Selects the vault nodes of a given node_type that a config binding actually routes, giving each extractor a bounded and deterministically ordered node population.

nodes.name: _extract_objectives
nodes.summary: Extracts the confirmed objectives array for the canonical pack by copying declared fields verbatim from the bound objective nodes.

nodes.name: _extract_outcomes
nodes.summary: Extracts the outcomes array for the canonical pack from the bound outcome nodes, carrying each entry's source node and provenance.

nodes.name: _extract_wps_and_deliverables
nodes.summary: Extracts the work-package and deliverable arrays together, so each deliverable keeps its owning work package without any inferred linkage.

nodes.name: _extract_partners
nodes.summary: Extracts the consortium partner array from the bound partner nodes, copying declared identity and role fields verbatim.

nodes.name: build_canonical_pack_from_graph
nodes.summary: Top-level deriver: loads the project config, reads the vault, runs every extractor, appends the quarantined declared assumptions, and atomically writes the canonical reference pack artifact.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line front end for the pack deriver: parses arguments, invokes the build, and reports the written artifact or the fail-closed error.

nodes.name: graph_claim_verifier.py
nodes.summary: Independent claim-to-node traceability auditor: reads the committed Tier 5 section artifacts from disk (never a fresh compile) plus the vault, and asserts that every published claim_id is a bound vault node whose status equals the schema's evidence mapping. Distinguishes audit findings from fail-closed preconditions, and refuses to pass vacuously when there is nothing to verify.
nodes.languageNotes: Its independence is structural: it imports the shared vault reader and schema but deliberately not the compiler, so a compiler whose status projection drifted is caught rather than blessed.

nodes.name: GraphClaimVerificationError
nodes.summary: Raised when the audit cannot be run at all — a malformed config or vault, an unparseable section file, or no published sections to verify.

nodes.name: ClaimFinding
nodes.summary: One traceability discrepancy between a published claim and its vault node: an unknown claim_id, a status mismatch, a wrong-section membership, or a dropped node.

nodes.name: ClaimVerificationResult
nodes.summary: Aggregate audit outcome carrying the verified claim counts and the collected findings, with an ok property that is true only when no finding was raised.

nodes.name: _as_dir
nodes.summary: Normalises a configured artifact_path into the directory that actually holds the published section files.

nodes.name: _tier5_sections_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the published sections directory from the project config's tier-5 bindings, failing closed when the config declares none.

nodes.name: _bound_section_nodes
nodes.summary: Collects the bound proposal_section vault nodes — the exact population the compiler draws claims from — so the audit can check both directions of the claim ledger.

nodes.name: _check_claim
nodes.summary: Audits a single published claim: resolves its claim_id to a vault node, recomputes the expected status from the node's evidence_strength, and checks that the node declares the same section slug as the file it appears in.

nodes.name: verify_claim_traceability
nodes.summary: Runs the whole audit: loads config and vault, walks every committed section artifact, checks each claim, and reports any bound node that no published section claims.

nodes.name: format_report
nodes.summary: Renders an audit result as a human-readable report listing the verified counts and each finding.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line front end for the traceability auditor, returning a non-zero exit code on findings or fail-closed preconditions.

nodes.name: graph_compiler.py
nodes.summary: The graph-to-docs compiler: reads a config-bound vault and deterministically extracts both the Tier 3 architecture_inputs JSON and the Part B proposal_section deliverables, writing them into a Tier 4 staging tree and diffing against the existing hand-lift rather than overwriting it. Record validation status is always computed from the node's evidence_strength, never read from the node, so an unconfirmed node can never land as a confirmed fact.
nodes.languageNotes: The largest module in the graph substrate; two extraction slices (Tier 3 and Part B) share one mechanism — read the vault, route by config binding, copy declared fields verbatim, compute status by lookup — so adding a slice means adding a binding, not a code path.

nodes.name: GraphCompileError
nodes.summary: Raised when compilation cannot proceed honestly — a node whose self-declared tier or artifact_path contradicts the binding that routes it, or a config routing conflicting collection keys to one artifact. Always names the offending node or binding.

nodes.name: CompiledArtifact
nodes.summary: One staged Tier 3 artifact: its canonical path, collection key, extracted records, and the source node ids it was built from.

nodes.name: Tier3CompileResult
nodes.summary: Outcome of a Tier 3 compile: the staged artifacts, the staging root, and the vault they came from.

nodes.name: CompiledSection
nodes.summary: One compiled Part B proposal section: its slug, the sub-sections built from individual vault nodes, the derived overall status, and the contributing node ids.

nodes.name: PartBCompileResult
nodes.summary: Outcome of a Part B compile: the compiled sections, the staging root, and the run id stamped into each section artifact.

nodes.name: extract_record
nodes.summary: Turns one vault node into a Tier 3 record by copying its declared front-matter fields verbatim and computing the validation status from evidence_strength.

nodes.name: _collection_key_for
nodes.summary: Resolves the JSON collection key a binding writes its records under, failing closed rather than defaulting silently.

nodes.name: _check_node_self_binding
nodes.summary: Asserts that a node's self-declared tier and artifact_path agree with the config binding that routed it, raising a named error on contradiction.

nodes.name: _build_artifact_obj
nodes.summary: Assembles the serialisable Tier 3 artifact object, attaching the provenance block (source node ids, vault, project id, compile stamp) alongside the records.

nodes.name: compile_tier3
nodes.summary: Compiles the Tier 3 architecture_inputs slice: reads the vault, routes every node through its config binding, groups records by target artifact, and atomically stages each artifact under Tier 4.

nodes.name: _diff_one
nodes.summary: Diffs one compiled artifact against the corresponding hand-lifted JSON, classifying records as matched, compiled-only, or hand-lift-only residual.

nodes.name: diff_against_hand_lift
nodes.summary: Builds the full diff report comparing every staged Tier 3 artifact against the committed hand-lift, which serves as the compiler's oracle.

nodes.name: compile_and_diff
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that compiles Tier 3 and then atomically writes the hand-lift diff report into the repository.

nodes.name: _require_section_str
nodes.summary: Reads a mandatory string field from a proposal_section node, raising a named compile error when it is missing or blank.

nodes.name: extract_sub_section
nodes.summary: Builds one Part B sub-section from a proposal_section node, using the node's body prose as content and its evidence_strength to compute the claim status.

nodes.name: _section_claim
nodes.summary: Constructs the claim-status entry for a sub-section, stamping the source node id as the claim id and its mapped status.

nodes.name: _derive_overall_status
nodes.summary: Reduces a section's per-claim statuses to one overall status by taking the weakest status present.

nodes.name: _partb_out_dir
nodes.summary: Normalises the configured Part B artifact_path into the output directory the section files are staged into.

nodes.name: _union_section_source_refs
nodes.summary: Merges the source references declared by every node of a section into one de-duplicated, deterministically ordered list.

nodes.name: _merge_section_extra_fields
nodes.summary: Merges the optional section-level extra fields contributed by individual nodes, refusing to resolve conflicting declarations silently.

nodes.name: _load_required_section_fields
nodes.summary: Loads the per-section-type required-field expectations from the deliverable schema so the compiler validates against the schema rather than a hard-coded list.

nodes.name: _validate_compiled_section
nodes.summary: Checks a compiled section object against the schema's required fields before it is staged, failing closed on any gap.

nodes.name: compile_part_b
nodes.summary: Compiles the Part B slice: groups proposal_section nodes by section slug, builds one sub-section per node, derives the section's overall status, validates it, and atomically stages each section artifact.

nodes.name: part_b_report
nodes.summary: Builds the Part B compile report summarising each section's slug, sub-section count, overall status, and contributing nodes.

nodes.name: compile_part_b_and_report
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that compiles Part B and then atomically writes its compile report into the repository.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line front end driving the --from-graph compile: selects the Tier 3 or Part B slice, runs it with reporting, and surfaces fail-closed errors as a non-zero exit.

nodes.name: graph_config.py
nodes.summary: Defines and validates the per-project graph.config.yaml binding contract — which vault folders and node types map to which target tier and canonical docs/** artifact path. This is the only place project specifics enter the graph substrate, which is what keeps the generic layer free of project nouns.
nodes.languageNotes: Bindings are scanned in file order with first-match-wins, so a config author must place specific bindings before general ones; every malformed field raises a named error rather than taking a silent default.

nodes.name: GraphConfigError
nodes.summary: Raised on any malformed or missing config field, always naming the offending binding.

nodes.name: Binding
nodes.summary: One node-to-artifact binding: the match criteria (folder prefix and/or node type), the target tier, the optional canonical artifact path, and the collection key. Its matches method decides whether a given node is routed by this binding.

nodes.name: GraphConfig
nodes.summary: A validated project config: the opaque project id, the vault node root, and the ordered bindings, with helpers to resolve the vault directory and to resolve the first binding matching a node.

nodes.name: _optional_stripped_str
nodes.summary: Reads an optional string config field, rejecting a present-but-blank value instead of treating it as absent.

nodes.name: _parse_binding
nodes.summary: Parses and validates one raw binding entry — checking the match keys, the tier vocabulary, and the node type vocabulary — and raises a named error identifying the binding by index.

nodes.name: load_graph_config
nodes.summary: Loads a graph.config.yaml from disk, validates its shape and every binding, and returns a GraphConfig — the single entry point every graph tool uses to become project-specific.

nodes.name: graph_determinism_check.py
nodes.summary: Replay auditor that proves the compiler is a pure function of the vault: it compiles the same vault twice into two separate staging roots with deliberately different compiled_at stamps and shows the outputs are byte-identical apart from that one documented exclusion. Byte-exact on the fast path, falling back to order-preserving canonical JSON so a reordered key or array element is flagged rather than masked.
nodes.languageNotes: Feeding the two compiles maximally different timestamps turns a weak claim (two runs happened to agree) into a strong one (even when the stamp differs, nothing else does).

nodes.name: DeterminismCheckError
nodes.summary: Raised when the check cannot run at all — a malformed config or vault, or a config that compiles to nothing, which is refused rather than vacuously passed.

nodes.name: DeterminismFinding
nodes.summary: One divergence between the two compiles: the staged path, the kind of divergence, and a detail locating it.

nodes.name: StagingComparison
nodes.summary: The result of comparing two staging trees: the paths present in each, the compared file count, and the findings, with an ok property that is true only when nothing diverged.

nodes.name: DeterminismResult
nodes.summary: The overall replay-check outcome, wrapping the Tier 3 and Part B staging comparisons and exposing the aggregate ok verdict and staged file count.

nodes.name: _strip_exclusions
nodes.summary: Recursively removes the documented replay-invariant fields (the compiler's wall-clock publication stamp) so only vault-derived content is compared.

nodes.name: _canonical_json
nodes.summary: Serialises an object to order-preserving canonical JSON for the slow-path comparison, so key or element reordering still registers as a divergence.

nodes.name: _staged_rel_paths
nodes.summary: Enumerates a staging root's files as sorted repo-relative paths so the two trees can be compared set-wise and in a stable order.

nodes.name: _divergence_detail
nodes.summary: Describes where two staged objects first differ, so a divergence report points at the offending field rather than just the file.

nodes.name: compare_staging_trees
nodes.summary: Compares two staging trees file by file: checks for paths present in only one tree, then compares each shared file byte-exactly and falls back to exclusion-stripped canonical JSON when only the stamp forces the bytes apart.

nodes.name: verify_compile_determinism
nodes.summary: Runs the full replay check: compiles Tier 3 and Part B twice into two ephemeral staging roots with different compile stamps but an identical vault and run id, then compares both trees.

nodes.name: format_report
nodes.summary: Renders a determinism result as a human-readable report listing the compared file counts and every divergence.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line front end for the replay auditor, cleaning up its ephemeral staging roots and exiting non-zero on divergence or a fail-closed precondition.

nodes.name: graph_projector.py
nodes.summary: The docs-to-graph projector: scans durable Tier 4 phase and gate state and mirrors it into the vault as derived, read-only phase_gate_state nodes so the Obsidian dashboards reflect run state. It is deterministic and idempotent, writes only its own owned vault folder, and enforces that the two sync directions never write the same docs path or vault folder.
nodes.languageNotes: The mirror is deliberately one-way and derived: it carries no fresh timestamp and the gate evaluator never reads the vault, so projecting cannot change a gate outcome or input freshness.

nodes.name: GraphProjectionError
nodes.summary: Raised when projection cannot proceed — unreadable Tier 4 state or an invalid mirror node.

nodes.name: SyncOverlapError
nodes.summary: Raised when a project config would let both sync directions write the same docs path or vault folder, breaking the non-overlap invariant.

nodes.name: GateState
nodes.summary: One gate's durable state read from Tier 4 — its id, phase, status, predicate counts and provenance — with a mirror_id property naming the vault node that reflects it.

nodes.name: Tier4Scan
nodes.summary: The result of scanning the Tier 4 phase outputs: the discovered gate states and the files they came from.

nodes.name: ProjectionResult
nodes.summary: The outcome of a projection run: the mirror nodes written, unchanged, and pruned, plus the target folder they live in.

nodes.name: SyncPartition
nodes.summary: The audited write and read sets of the two sync directions, exposing the compiler-owned and projector-owned paths for the non-overlap check.

nodes.name: _phase_from_path
nodes.summary: Derives the owning phase from a Tier 4 phase-output path so each mirror node can be attributed to its phase without a lookup table.

nodes.name: _predicate_counts
nodes.summary: Counts the passed and total predicates in a gate-result block so the mirror node can display a pass ratio.

nodes.name: scan_tier4_gate_states
nodes.summary: Walks the Tier 4 phase-output tree and reads every durable gate-result artifact into an ordered set of GateState records.

nodes.name: read_tier4_gate_states
nodes.summary: Thin accessor returning just the gate states from a Tier 4 scan.

nodes.name: _render_mirror_node
nodes.summary: Renders one gate state as a complete vault note — front-matter marked derived and read_only plus a body — and validates the front-matter against the schema before it is written.

nodes.name: project
nodes.summary: Runs the projection: renders a mirror node per gate state, atomically writes only those whose content changed, and prunes mirror notes whose gate state no longer exists.

nodes.name: compute_sync_partition
nodes.summary: Computes the write and read sets of both sync directions from a project config, exposing the partition for auditing.

nodes.name: check_no_overlap
nodes.summary: Enforces the non-overlap invariant against a project config, raising SyncOverlapError when any docs path or vault folder would be written by both directions.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line front end for the projector, supporting both the projection run and the standalone non-overlap check.

nodes.name: graph_schema.py
nodes.summary: The project-agnostic schema half of the graph substrate: the controlled node_type and evidence_strength vocabularies, the pure lookup from evidence strength to a validation status, the required-core versus additive-optional front-matter split, and fail-closed validation that names the offending node. Carries no folder names, call, or partner nouns.
nodes.languageNotes: Vocabularies are frozensets and the evidence-to-status map is a plain dict lookup, never a judgement — that purity is what lets provenance be carried end to end. The newer tier/phase/artifact_path/sub_section_id keys are additive-optional so existing nodes still validate unchanged.

nodes.name: GraphSchemaError
nodes.summary: Raised on a front-matter violation, always naming the offending node reference.

nodes.name: map_evidence_to_status
nodes.summary: Maps an evidence_strength value to its constitutional validation status by pure dict lookup — source-grounded to confirmed, synthesis and inference to inferred, unconfirmed to unresolved — and is the single authority every graph tool reads that mapping from.

nodes.name: validate_front_matter
nodes.summary: Validates a node's front-matter against the schema: the required identity and provenance core must be present and non-blank, every controlled-vocabulary value must be in range, and any violation raises a named error rather than a silent default.

nodes.name: vault_reader.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic pure-Python parse layer of the graph substrate: reads every vault note's YAML front-matter, body prose, and wikilinks, validates each against the generic schema, and returns an indexed Vault. This is the single substrate the compiler, projector, pack deriver, and auditors all build on.
nodes.languageNotes: Wikilink resolution mirrors Obsidian's basename semantics, so [[Target]], [[Target|Display]] and [[folder/Target#Heading]] all land on the same node. A dangling link is recorded as a graph-quality signal rather than raised, while a duplicate id or basename fails closed.

nodes.name: VaultReadError
nodes.summary: Raised when a node has missing or malformed front-matter, an unparseable YAML block, a duplicate id or basename, or a schema violation — always naming the node.

nodes.name: WikiLink
nodes.summary: One parsed wikilink: its target basename plus the optional display text and heading anchor.

nodes.name: GraphNode
nodes.summary: One parsed vault node: its id, path, validated front-matter, body prose, outbound wikilinks, and mapped status, with accessors for the additive-optional tier, phase, artifact_path, and sub_section_id keys.

nodes.name: Vault
nodes.summary: The indexed parse result: path-ordered nodes plus id and basename indices, with methods to resolve a wikilink, find the config binding for a node, and enumerate dangling links.

nodes.name: _parse_wikilink
nodes.summary: Parses the inside of a wikilink into target, display text, and heading, handling the folder-prefixed and aliased forms.

nodes.name: _extract_wikilinks
nodes.summary: Scans a node body for wikilinks and returns them de-duplicated in first-seen order, keeping the parse deterministic.

nodes.name: _split_front_matter
nodes.summary: Splits a note into its YAML front-matter block and body, failing closed with the node reference when the block is missing or unparseable.

nodes.name: _parse_node
nodes.summary: Parses one note file into a GraphNode: splits the front-matter, validates it against the schema, extracts wikilinks, and computes the node's status from its evidence_strength.

nodes.name: read_vault
nodes.summary: Reads a whole vault directory into an indexed Vault: parses every note in sorted path order, builds the id and basename indices, and rejects duplicate ids or basenames.

nodes.name: vault_scaffold.py
nodes.summary: Instantiates a fresh per-project graph vault by copying the generic template — schema superset, folder skeleton, and a noun-free config — and rewriting a single project_id line, then validates the result by reading it back through the reader. Pure and Claude-free: a scaffolded vault holds no project facts until a human authors nodes into it.
nodes.languageNotes: The project_id swap is a single targeted regex substitution so the template config's explanatory comments survive the copy.

nodes.name: VaultScaffoldError
nodes.summary: Raised when a vault cannot be scaffolded — a bad template, a target collision, or a config with no project_id line to rewrite.

nodes.name: ScaffoldResult
nodes.summary: The outcome of scaffolding: the written vault root, the written config path, and the node root the reader and compiler will read.

nodes.name: scaffold_vault
nodes.summary: Copies the generic template to the target directory, rewrites the config's project_id, and returns the resolved vault, config, and node roots — refusing an existing target unless forced.

nodes.name: validate_scaffold
nodes.summary: Validates a scaffold by loading its config and reading the vault back through the reader, proving the new vault is one the compiler will accept.

nodes.name: agnosticism_lint.py
nodes.summary: Static "no project nouns" lint that proves the generic graph layer stays project-agnostic: it scans the enumerated generic-layer sources (runner/graph_*.py, runner/vault_*.py, runner/dev_graph/**, the vault template, the obsidian-graph skill) for a denylist of reference-instance proper nouns and domain terms and reports every file:line:noun hit. Pure, deterministic and Claude-free — it reads and reports, writes nothing and evaluates no gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses as the result contract, a single compiled word-boundary case-insensitive regex alternation built from a frozenset denylist, and a `python -m` CLI entry point with distinct exit codes (0 clean / 1 violations / 3 error).

nodes.name: LintViolation
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass recording one denylisted project noun found in a generic-layer source: the repo-relative path, 1-based line, the verbatim matched noun, and the stripped offending line for an actionable report.

nodes.name: LintReport
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding the outcome of a generic-layer scan — every scanned file plus every violation in (path, line) order — with an `ok` property that is true only when no project noun was found.

nodes.name: scan_text
nodes.summary: Pure matcher that finds every denylisted noun in a text, returning (line_number, matched_noun, stripped_line) tuples in document order. Word-boundary and case-insensitive matching keeps whole-word nouns from hitting substrings of unrelated words.

nodes.name: iter_generic_layer_files
nodes.summary: Resolves the GENERIC_LAYER_GLOBS to the authored text files worth scanning: de-duplicated, sorted by repo-relative POSIX path for determinism, restricted to the allowed text suffixes, and excluding vendored segments such as the Obsidian app directory.

nodes.name: lint_generic_layer
nodes.summary: Top-level scan entry point: reads every enumerated generic-layer source as BOM-tolerant UTF-8 and collects a LintViolation per denylisted-noun hit into a LintReport. Never raises on a leak — it reports one, leaving the non-zero exit to the CLI.

nodes.name: format_report
nodes.summary: Renders a LintReport as human-readable text: a one-line OK summary when clean, or a FAIL block listing every path:line:noun with the offending line plus remediation guidance pointing the project-specific fact back to the per-project config or vault.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for `python -m runner.agnosticism_lint`: parses an optional --repo-root (otherwise auto-discovering it), runs the lint, and returns exit code 0 when clean, 1 when project nouns leaked, or 3 on an unexpected error.

nodes.name: consortium_composition.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic evaluator for the Horizon Europe consortium-composition condition: it reads the four thresholds and their verbatim citations out of the Tier 1 participation rules and the partner records out of the Tier 3 registry, then reports whether the consortium is met and which of the four limbs fails. No threshold is supplied from programme knowledge and no partner fact is inferred — it reads, evaluates and reports, writing nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: Country is modelled as a pseudonymous slot (C1, C2, …) carrying only a Member State / Associated Country class, so the evaluator can never see or leak a real country name. Evaluation is order-independent by construction: every grouping sorts by partner id before a setdefault, so a last-wins dict cannot silently break reproducibility.

nodes.name: CompositionError
nodes.summary: Fail-closed exception raised when Tier 1 or Tier 3 cannot be read as the evaluator needs it. A missing threshold or an unreadable partner record is never defaulted, because guessing either would decide eligibility on an invention.

nodes.name: Citation
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding one verbatim span of a Tier 1 source — quote, source document, page and section — tagged with the limb of the condition it evidences so a result carries the text it was decided on.

nodes.name: CompositionRule
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass carrying the composition condition exactly as Tier 1 states it: the four minimum thresholds, whether affiliated entities count, the verbatim rule text, the supporting citations, and the source artifact path.

nodes.name: Beneficiary
nodes.summary: One partner record reduced to what the condition asks about: partner id, pseudonymous country slot, slot class, and the independent / is_beneficiary flags, with a `counts` property that is true only when both hold.

nodes.name: CompositionResult
nodes.summary: The verdict of evaluating one consortium: whether the condition is met, which partners counted or were excluded, the distinct and class-partitioned country slots, the failed limbs, a satisfying selection, and the thresholds and citations it was judged against. Its `status` and `reason` properties are derived from those fields, so the printed sentence cannot drift from the verdict.

nodes.name: Scenario
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass pairing one consortium variant — its name, the question it answers, and the partner ids it includes — with the CompositionResult that variant produced.

nodes.name: _load_json
nodes.summary: Reads a JSON object from disk, failing closed with a CompositionError naming the path when the file is absent, not parseable, or does not hold an object at the top level.

nodes.name: _citation
nodes.summary: Builds a Citation from a verbatim-span block of the Tier 1 rule artifact, type-checking quote, source document, page and section and tagging the span with the limb it evidences; returns None when the span is absent or malformed.

nodes.name: load_composition_rule
nodes.summary: Reads the composition condition out of the Tier 1 extracted participation rules: the four integer thresholds, the affiliated-entities flag, the verbatim rule text and its citations, raising CompositionError rather than defaulting anything so no threshold ever comes from programme knowledge.

nodes.name: load_partners
nodes.summary: Reads the Tier 3 partner registry into a tuple of Beneficiary records, requiring a partner id, a country slot and a slot class on every entry and raising CompositionError on any missing or mistyped field rather than guessing a value that would decide eligibility.

nodes.name: partners_by_capability_basis
nodes.summary: Groups partner ids by their recorded `capability_basis`, reading the fact from the Tier 3 registry so a CLI default or a report can never disagree with it; always exposes the 'derived' and 'fictional' groups, sorted.

nodes.name: evaluate_composition
nodes.summary: The core pure evaluation: filters partners down to independent beneficiaries, collapses them onto distinct country slots, classifies each slot as Member State, Associated Country or neither, tests the four limbs (counting only the further eligible slots for the 'other countries' limb so one slot is never spent twice), and returns a CompositionResult with a satisfying selection when all limbs pass.
nodes.languageNotes: Order-independence is explicit: counted partners are sorted by id before every setdefault, so two partners disagreeing about a shared slot's class resolve identically on every run.

nodes.name: evaluate_scenarios
nodes.summary: Evaluates the three readings the consortium analysis asks for: all partners, the derived partners alone without the fictional gap partners, and each gap partner removed in turn — the redundancy question of whether the condition still holds if any single unconfirmed partner withdraws.

nodes.name: format_scenarios
nodes.summary: Renders the scenario table a human reads: one line per scenario with its met/not-met status, partner count and derived reason sentence, followed by the Tier 1 citations the verdict rests on.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for `python -m runner.consortium_composition`: resolves the repo root, loads the Tier 1 rule and Tier 3 partners, derives the derived/gap partner sets from the registry unless overridden by --derived/--gap, prints the scenario table, and exits 0 when the condition is met, 1 when it is not, or 3 when a tier could not be read.

nodes.name: leakage_scan.py
nodes.summary: The anonymity scan guarding the blind-assessment lane: it checks that no reference-instance organisation name, person, place, web address or project identifier appears in Tier 3, Tier 4, Tier 5 or the vault. Two mechanisms do the work — a word scan over a denylist derived from the agnosticism lint's PROJECT_NOUNS (partitioned into identity, re-identifying and deliberately scoped-out nouns), and a structural pseudonymity check that reads the real country lists out of Tier 1 and fails on any country name, URL or email in a Tier 3 self-description.
nodes.languageNotes: The report deliberately separates `ok` (no new leak — the regression guard) from `clean` (no leak at all — the constraint itself), with KNOWN_PRE_EXISTING_LEAKS pinning each recorded leak to its path and reason so a known leak can never be reported as clean. The denylist is derived from PROJECT_NOUNS rather than re-typed, so a noun added there is scanned at once. Known scope gap: SCAN_GLOBS cover Tier 3/4/5 and the vault but do not reach docs/integrations/.

nodes.name: LeakageError
nodes.summary: Fail-closed exception raised when the scan cannot read a source it needs — notably the Tier 1 country list — on the principle that a check which cannot run must not report clean.

nodes.name: LeakageViolation
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass recording one leak: its path (a file path, or a file plus JSON field path for a record-level hit), line number (0 when located structurally), the verbatim matched text, a snippet, the kind of leak (identity noun, country name, web address or email), and whether the path is a recorded pre-existing leak.

nodes.name: LeakageReport
nodes.summary: The outcome of a scan, with three outcomes rather than two: `ok` (no new leak, what a regression guard answers), `clean` (no leak at all, what the anonymity constraint asks), and a `format` method that renders OK, 'OK, NOT CLEAN' with the recorded pre-existing leaks, or FAIL with remediation guidance.

nodes.name: leakage_denylist
nodes.summary: Compiles the scan's matcher: a single word-boundary, case-insensitive alternation over LEAKAGE_NOUNS plus any operator-supplied extra nouns, sorted longest-first so an overlapping longer noun wins the report.

nodes.name: scan_text
nodes.summary: Pure matcher applying a compiled pattern line by line to a text, returning (line_number, matched_text, stripped_line) tuples in document order. Reused by both the word scan and the prose leg of the pseudonymity check.

nodes.name: iter_vault_roots
nodes.summary: Discovers every project vault by reading the `vault_path` out of each graph.config.yaml, skipping the generic template and test fixtures, so a vault is scanned wherever it actually lives. Conservative on failure: an unreadable config or a missing PyYAML widens the scan to the config's own directory rather than narrowing it.

nodes.name: iter_scanned_files
nodes.summary: Resolves the scan scope — the Tier 3/4/5 globs plus every discovered vault root — into a deterministic, de-duplicated, sorted list of text files, dropping non-text suffixes and vendored path segments.

nodes.name: scan_tree
nodes.summary: The word-scan entry point: reads every in-scope file in Tier 3, Tier 4, Tier 5 and the vault and collects a LeakageViolation per denylist hit, flagging hits at recorded paths as pre_existing so they do not fail the scan.

nodes.name: real_country_names
nodes.summary: Reads the real country names — Member States, Associated Countries and Overseas Countries and Territories — out of the Tier 1 participation rules rather than listing them, so the pseudonymity check cannot drift from the General Annexes. Fails closed with LeakageError when Tier 1 is unreadable.

nodes.name: _iter_strings
nodes.summary: Recursively walks a parsed JSON tree yielding (json_path, string) for every string value, so a record-level hit can be located by field path rather than by line number.

nodes.name: _iter_globbed
nodes.summary: Shared resolver for both pseudonymity legs: expands a glob set to existing files, deterministically sorted and de-duplicated, minus the declared exemptions — one resolver so an exemption can never apply to the JSON leg and not the prose leg.

nodes.name: scan_partner_records
nodes.summary: The structural pseudonymity check and the only mechanism that catches a country name: it builds a pattern from the Tier 1 country lists and matches it, along with URL and email patterns, against every string in the in-scope Tier 3 JSON self-descriptions (located by field path) and every line of the in-scope Tier 3 prose. An absent artifact yields no violation; an unreadable Tier 1 raises LeakageError.

nodes.name: _read_extra_nouns
nodes.summary: Reads the operator's noun extension file — one noun per line, comments skipped — which is deliberately kept outside the repository so that writing those names into the branch does not itself become the leak the scan exists to prevent.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for `python -m runner.leakage_scan`: resolves the repo root, runs the word scan with any --extra-nouns extension and the pseudonymity record check, merges both into one report, and exits 0 when no new leak was found (still printing 'NOT CLEAN' for recorded leaks), 1 on a new leak, or 3 when a needed source could not be read.

nodes.name: manifest.compile.yaml
nodes.summary: The compiled workflow manifest and executable spine of the engine: it declares the DAG execution model, a node_registry of 13 phase nodes binding each to its agent, skills, deterministic components and entry/exit gates, a 17-entry edge_registry of gate-guarded transitions, a 14-entry gate_registry and a 31-entry artifact registry. Its gate_registry predicate_refs are authoritative over which gate predicates actually execute.
nodes.languageNotes: The gate_registry nests predicate_refs inside prose conditions, so a predicate defined in gate_rules_library.yaml but absent from a condition's predicate_refs is never evaluated.

nodes.name: agent_catalog.yaml
nodes.summary: Declares the 20 workflow agents with their role, constitutional scope, declared tier reads and writes, explicit must_not prohibitions and phase alignment. Named by the constitution as an authoritative source of agent scope; three agents are cross-phase and proposal_writer is marked deprecated by the Phase 8 refactor.

nodes.name: skill_catalog.yaml
nodes.summary: Declares the 27 skills, each an atomic single-Claude-invocation unit, with its execution mode (predominantly TAPM), output contract, purpose, consuming agents, declared tier reads and writes and constitutional constraints. A skill may never invoke another skill.
nodes.languageNotes: execution_mode separates TAPM skills (Claude reads declared inputs from disk via tools) from the lightweight cli-prompt path; a few entries leave it unset.

nodes.name: gate_rules_library.yaml
nodes.summary: The machine-evaluable predicate library behind all 14 gates: 149 declared predicates, each carrying a predicate_id, type, evaluation function, args, prose condition and operator-facing fail message. The manifest's predicate_refs select which of these actually run.
nodes.languageNotes: Predicate ids follow a gNN_pNN scheme keyed to gate ordinal rather than gate_id, so the g02_* predicates belong to phase_01_gate.

nodes.name: quality_gates.yaml
nodes.summary: The prose-level definition of the 15 quality gates: name, description, evaluation point, fail action and the human-readable conditions each gate enforces. Budget Consistency is the only gate flagged bypass_prohibited, matching the constitution's categorical Phase 8 block.

nodes.name: artifact_schema_specification.yaml
nodes.summary: The canonical artifact schema specification: field-level schemas for Tier 4 phase outputs, Tier 5 deliverables, proposal sections, gate results, operational and dev-graph artifacts, Tier 3 sources, Tier 2A/2B extracts and integration validation, plus a 22-entry schema_id_registry mapping each schema_id to its artifact and section. Agent output that diverges from these schemas is a failure, not an alternative valid reading.
nodes.languageNotes: Every canonical artifact carries a versioned schema_id of the form orch.<scope>.<artifact>.v1, which the runtime validates rather than repairs.

nodes.name: tier_bindings.yaml
nodes.summary: Maps the workflow onto the repository document model: for Tier 1 through Tier 5 plus integrations and runtime it declares the root path, role, subpaths, extracted artifacts, read authority and write constraint, including the Tier 2A constraint against treating grant agreement annexes as a proposal schema.

nodes.name: global_rules.yaml
nodes.summary: Cross-cutting invariants binding every phase: determinism, failure on missing required inputs, mandatory tier traceability, durable Tier 4 writes, prohibitions on fabricating project facts, call constraints and budget estimates, the budget-gate-before-finalization rule and the evaluation-success optimisation target.

nodes.name: state_rules.yaml
nodes.summary: Rules governing orchestration state: Tier 4 durability, checkpoint preservation, decision logging, deterministic rerun behaviour, conflict logging, the agent-memory boundary, the four-value validation status vocabulary (Confirmed, Inferred, Assumed, Unresolved) and index maintenance.

nodes.name: integration_rules.yaml

nodes.name: meta.yaml

nodes.name: phase_01_call_analysis.yaml
nodes.summary: Node specification for Phase 1 (Call Analysis): binds the call_analyzer agent and five extraction skills to parse the work programme and call topic into the six Tier 2B extracted files plus the Tier 2A section and evaluator registries. Its gate requires all six extracted files non-empty with source section references and a resolved instrument type.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML phase spec with a fixed key shape (id/phase/name/purpose/agent/skills/depends_on/required_inputs/outputs/instructions/validation/gate_condition); required_inputs splits into mandatory and conditional path entries each carrying role and validation prose.

nodes.name: phase_02_concept_refinement.yaml
nodes.summary: Node specification for Phase 2 (Concept Refinement): binds the concept_refiner agent to align the Tier 3 concept note with the confirmed call scope and vocabulary, writing topic_mapping.json and compliance_profile.json back to Tier 3. Its gate requires a complete topic mapping with source references and no unresolved scope conflicts against Tier 2B.

nodes.name: phase_03_wp_design.yaml
nodes.summary: Node specification for Phase 3 (Work Package Design and Dependency Mapping): binds the wp_designer agent to build work packages, tasks, deliverables, milestones and an acyclic inter-WP dependency map from Tier 3 objectives and consortium data. Its gate requires every WP to carry objectives, tasks, at least one deliverable, a responsible lead and declared dependencies, with the WP count inside the Tier 2A instrument limit and no dependency cycles.
nodes.languageNotes: Declares dependency mapping as a required sub-task rather than a separate phase, so the dependency map is the Tier 4 artifact that Phase 4 and Phase 6 consume.

nodes.name: phase_04_gantt_milestones.yaml
nodes.summary: Node specification for Phase 4 (Gantt and Milestones): binds the gantt_designer agent plus the deterministic dependency_normalizer component to assign every task to months, define milestones with verifiable criteria and derive scheduling_constraints.json. Its gate requires all tasks scheduled within the call duration, every milestone verifiable, a critical path consistent with the dependency map, and the normalized constraints written to Tier 4.
nodes.languageNotes: One of only two phase specs carrying a deterministic_components key — the Claude-free node-body pass sanctioned by CLAUDE.md §16.5/§17.5.3, bound in the spec rather than hardcoded in the agent runtime.

nodes.name: phase_05_impact_architecture.yaml
nodes.summary: Node specification for Phase 5 (Impact Architecture): binds the impact_architect agent to build the output-to-outcome-to-impact pathway with KPIs, dissemination, exploitation, communication and sustainability logic. Its gate requires every Tier 2B expected impact to have at least one mapped project output and every KPI to trace to a named WP deliverable, with no impact claim asserted without a project mechanism.
nodes.languageNotes: Depends on Phases 2 and 3 only, so it can run in parallel with Phase 4 — the one fork in the otherwise linear phase chain.

nodes.name: phase_06_implementation_architecture.yaml
nodes.summary: Node specification for Phase 6 (Implementation Architecture): binds the implementation_architect agent to define the management structure, governance and decision-making matrix, quality assurance plan, populated risk register, ethics self-assessment and any instrument-mandated gender and diversity plan. Its gate requires ethics flags to be stated explicitly rather than omitted and all management roles to be assigned to named Tier 3 partners.

nodes.name: phase_07_budget_gate.yaml
nodes.summary: Node specification for Phase 7 (Budget Gate): binds the budget_gate_validator agent to confirm a validated external Lump Sum Budget Planner response exists and is structurally consistent with the Phase 3 WP structure, Phase 4 timeline and Phase 6 consortium roles, without computing any figure itself. The gate is marked mandatory with bypass_prohibited, and a pre_gate_action delegates request preparation to budget_interface_coordinator when no response is present.
nodes.languageNotes: Carries the unique pre_gate_action block and the mandatory/bypass_prohibited gate flags, plus a trailing v1.1 semantic-correction note recording that the earlier non-failing hold_behavior key was removed as a CLAUDE.md §8.4 conflict — absent budget artifacts now compile unconditionally as a blocking failure.

nodes.name: phase_08_drafting_review.yaml
nodes.summary: Node specification for Phase 8 (Drafting and Review), the only phase decomposed into substeps: three parallel criterion-aligned drafting nodes (Excellence, Impact, Implementation), then sequential assembly, evaluator-style review and revision. It depends on all seven preceding phases and its gate aggregates gate_10a-d, gate_11, resolved critical revision actions, the final export and a published Phase 8 checkpoint.
nodes.languageNotes: Unlike the other seven specs, the phase-level keys carry no agent or skills binding; those move into each entry of the substeps list, which also introduces depends_on_substep for the intra-phase DAG.

nodes.name: phase_08a_excellence_drafting
nodes.summary: Substep 8a: binds the excellence_writer agent and the excellence-section-drafting skill to produce excellence_section.json covering objectives, relation to work programme, concept and methodology, ambition, interdisciplinarity and gender dimension. Runs in parallel with 8b and 8c and must verify the budget gate has passed before producing any content.

nodes.name: phase_08b_impact_drafting
nodes.summary: Substep 8b: binds the impact_writer agent and the impact-section-drafting skill to produce impact_section.json, mapping every Tier 2B expected impact to a Phase 5 pathway and populating impact_pathway_refs and dec_coverage. Runs in parallel with 8a and 8c and forbids fabricated coverage of an expected impact no project output addresses.

nodes.name: phase_08c_implementation_drafting
nodes.summary: Substep 8c: binds the implementation_writer agent and the implementation-section-drafting skill to produce implementation_section.json covering the work plan, Gantt, deliverables and milestones tables, management structure, risk management, consortium and resources. Populates wp_table_refs, gantt_ref, milestone_refs and risk_register_ref from the Phase 3, 4 and 6 artifacts without redesigning them.

nodes.name: phase_08d_assembly
nodes.summary: Substep 8d: binds the proposal_integrator agent and the cross-section-consistency-check skill to assemble the three criterion sections into part_b_assembled_draft.json in Part B order, recording cross-section findings in a consistency_log. It depends on substeps 8a, 8b and 8c and is forbidden from rewriting section content — inconsistencies are flagged, never silently normalised.

nodes.name: phase_08e_evaluator_review
nodes.summary: Substep 8e: binds the evaluator_reviewer agent and the evaluator-criteria-review skill to simulate evaluator assessment of the assembled draft against the Phase 1 evaluation matrix, producing review_packet.json with weaknesses categorised critical, major or minor and a prioritised revision action list. It depends on substep 8d and may not revise the draft itself.

nodes.name: phase_08f_revision
nodes.summary: Substep 8f: binds the revision_integrator agent plus the deterministic checkpoint_publisher component to apply critical then major revision actions, write the final export and publish phase8_checkpoint.json to Tier 4. It depends on substep 8e and must flag unresolvable gaps in the revision log rather than fabricate content.
nodes.languageNotes: Its inline comment records that checkpoint_publisher replaced the retired checkpoint-publish skill and writes the cross-run provenance quad that gate_12's checkpoint_published predicate re-validates.
