nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: The repository constitution and highest interpretive authority: it defines the programme-agnostic proposal-orchestration mission, a ten-level authority hierarchy, the six-tier document model (Tier 1 normative framework through Tier 5 deliverables), the eight canonical gated phases, the budget-integration rules, twelve categories of forbidden action, the agent derivation and execution binding rules, and the three-layer runtime execution architecture. Every agent, skill and workflow in the repository is subordinate to it, and five formal amendment records track how it has changed.
nodes.languageNotes: 46 headed sections. Each tier, phase and prohibition is addressable by number (§8.4, §17.5.3), and the file is written to be cited by that number from code docstrings — so engine modules declare their constitutional subordination inline rather than in a separate design doc.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the out-of-band judge runners (E4 baseline freeze, E1.5 faithfulness calibration, E5f rubric grading, blind assessment), each invoked as a module from the repo root. The docstring records why they live inside the harness package: so the one-way harness-to-runner import boundary holds for the auxiliary runtime surfaces too.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains the E1.5 faithfulness gold sets — human-labelled (claim, source_ref, supported?) triples used to calibrate the judge — and states the independence rule: the `supported` label is human ground truth, deliberately not the engine's own status, and an AI must never fill it.

nodes.name: LABELLING_GUIDE.md
nodes.summary: Hand-labelling rubric for the E3.1 materiality calibration: the single question a labeller asks of each text span, worked examples of material versus non-material prose, tie-breaks for edge cases, and the independence rule that a human — never an AI — writes the answer key.

nodes.name: e3.1-materiality-calibration_TEMPLATE.json
nodes.summary: Skeleton decision record for the E3.1 materiality-classifier calibration: placeholders for the judge model and pin, gold-set counts, the precision and escape-recall metrics, the operator's threshold policy (0.85 / 0.80), and the advisory-versus-gating decision keyed to that exact judge version.

nodes.name: materiality_calibration.py
nodes.summary: Turnkey runner for the E3.1 materiality-classifier calibration: it reads a human-labelled spreadsheet, writes the canonical JSONL materiality set, scores the real classifier against the human labels with a genuine confusion matrix, computes the escape-recall slice that matters, applies the fail-safe graduation rule, and emits a pre-filled decision-log draft. Advisory only — it measures the classifier the pipeline runs but never blocks a run.
nodes.languageNotes: Every `harness.*` import sits inside a function body, so the module imports on the standard library alone — its sheet parsing and metric helpers stay unit-testable without the judge and transport stack.

nodes.name: Row
nodes.summary: One labelled span from the gold sheet: its id, the human `material` verdict, the AI suggestion it may override, provenance fields (kind, section, in_ledger) and the classifier's later prediction.

nodes.name: find_gold
nodes.summary: Locates the labelled gold sheet by searching the candidate harness directories for known filenames, with an environment variable override taking precedence.

nodes.name: _rows_from_xlsx
nodes.summary: Parses the labelled XLSX sheet into raw row dictionaries, reading the header line and the TRUE/FALSE dropdown column.

nodes.name: read_sheet
nodes.summary: Dispatches on file extension to the XLSX or CSV reader and coerces each raw row into a validated Row, so the spreadsheet and its comma- or semicolon-separated twin are interchangeable.

nodes.name: escape_recall
nodes.summary: Computes the E3.1-specific escape-recall slice over the seeded rows — the share of out-of-ledger material claims the classifier actually catches, which is the recall that matters for fabrication detection.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Applies the fail-safe graduation rule: an undefined metric, an unreviewed label set or a judge repin all keep the classifier advisory; only clearing both the precision and escape-recall bars permits promotion to gating.

nodes.name: _to_examples
nodes.summary: Converts labelled rows into the canonical materiality-set example records the harness materiality module consumes.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Drives the whole calibration run end to end: finds and reads the sheet, enforces the review attestation and the non-drafter judge constraint, writes the materiality set, invokes the real classifier per row with pacing for rate-limited judges, scores precision and escape-recall, and writes the decision-log draft and provenance record.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Documents the E3 materiality calibration data and its two-anchor rule: positives are the engine's own claim-ledger enumeration and may legitimately be auto-labelled, while negatives are a human's call and are shipped unlabelled. Also states what becomes measurable at each stage of labelling.

nodes.name: msca_pf_default.json
nodes.summary: Default pre-evaluation profile for MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships, a single-researcher instrument: it binds the evaluator expectation registry, the option-tag grammar for the five MSCA variants, the three evaluation criteria and their section ids, and the MSCA-PF scorecard and rubric set.

nodes.name: ria_default.json
nodes.summary: Default pre-evaluation profile for the Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Action, a collaborative multi-partner instrument: the parallel form of the MSCA-PF profile, binding the same registry and three criteria to the RIA/IA evaluation form, scorecard and rubric set.
nodes.languageNotes: The RIA/IA evaluation form annotates no aspect as specific to either action type, so every aspect carries the tag 'RIA and IA' and the all-except prefix has no instance; it is declared anyway because the profile schema requires one.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Describes the E4 regression golden baselines — frozen per-section fingerprints covering the claim ledger, per-sub-section prose hashes and a formatting-invariant whole-artifact hash — what integrity drift the golden diff catches, and why the lane is merge-advisory and human-decided rather than run-blocking.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Minimal project file carrying pytest configuration only: the test path, repo-root import path, verbose output, and two custom markers registering the harness's advisory lanes — `harness_regression` for the E4 golden-set comparison and `harness_rubric` for the E5 rubric grid, both explicitly never run-blocking.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker for the DAG runner. Its docstring tracks the implementation status of the gate-predicate execution layer step by step and declares the package's constitutional subordination: it must not redefine gate logic, phase meanings, tier meanings or the authority hierarchy.

nodes.name: dependency_normalizer.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic, Claude-free preprocessor for Phase 4 scheduling: it reads the Phase 3 dependency map, the work-package temporal bounds from the seed and the project duration from the call binding, then classifies every dependency edge as strict (temporally enforceable) or non-strict (informational data input) into a normalized scheduling-constraints artifact.
nodes.languageNotes: A registered deterministic component: pure Python, no model invocation, no mutation of its inputs, and it fails closed on any input error. It follows the Step-0 call-slicer pattern but is bound into the node body through the agent runtime rather than the scheduler.

nodes.name: _read_json
nodes.summary: Loads a required JSON input and raises a labelled normalizer error on a missing file or malformed content, so every input failure surfaces with the artifact's name attached.

nodes.name: _build_wp_bounds
nodes.summary: Builds the per-work-package start and end month bounds from the work-package seed, the reference the edge classifier compares temporal overlap against.

nodes.name: _build_task_to_wp
nodes.summary: Indexes every task in the work-package structure back to its owning work package, so task-level dependency edges can be resolved to the WP layer.

nodes.name: _get_project_duration
nodes.summary: Extracts the project duration in months from the selected-call binding, the outer bound the normalized schedule must fit inside.

nodes.name: _classify_edge
nodes.summary: The core classification rule: a WP-level finish-to-start edge whose source WP ends after the target WP starts becomes non-strict (a logical data dependency, not full-WP sequencing), task-level finish-to-start edges stay strict, and data-input edges are always non-strict.

nodes.name: normalize_dependencies
nodes.summary: Public entry point for the component: resolves all three input artifacts for a run, classifies every dependency edge, and atomically writes the schema-tagged scheduling-constraints artifact to its canonical Phase 4 path.

nodes.name: persistence_policy.py
nodes.summary: Sole authority for what diagnostic data the runtime may write to disk, resolved from the deployment environment and a diagnostic-level variable. Development defaults to full prompt and response capture; production defaults to metadata only and rejects an explicit request for full content outright.
nodes.languageNotes: The module docstring carries the full policy matrix and a per-file table of what is written at each diagnostic level, making the module its own specification. Production mode fails loud — requesting full content raises at policy-resolution time rather than silently downgrading.

nodes.name: DiagnosticLevel
nodes.summary: Enumeration of the two diagnostic levels, full and metadata, that the whole persistence policy is keyed to.

nodes.name: resolve_diagnostic_level
nodes.summary: Resolves and caches the effective diagnostic level from the environment, defaulting production to metadata and raising rather than honouring a request for full content there.

nodes.name: allows_content_persistence
nodes.summary: Predicate the runtime calls before writing any prompt, response or parsed-output file: true only at the full diagnostic level.

nodes.name: allows_benchmark_persistence
nodes.summary: Predicate guarding the metadata-only artifacts — the invocation ledger, run manifest and transport diagnostics — which are permitted at every diagnostic level.

nodes.name: sanitize_error_message
nodes.summary: Truncates exception and error text before it reaches a metadata JSON file under production mode, closing the prompt-content leakage path that error echoing would otherwise open.

nodes.name: promote_graph_staging.py
nodes.summary: Implements the explicit half of the parallel-plus-explicit-promote design: the graph-to-docs compiler writes non-destructively into a staging tree, and a human runs this script with `--apply` to copy that output onto the canonical docs paths the runner consumes. Dry-run by default, guarded by a project-id match, with pre-promote backups and a promote record for reversibility.
nodes.languageNotes: Deterministic and model-free — a project-id-guarded byte copy with no domain reasoning, so the same staging always yields the same promotion. The project-id guard is what stops a stale second-instance staging from clobbering the real proposal docs.

nodes.name: _staging_project_id
nodes.summary: Reads the project id recorded in the staging tree's compile reports, the value the guard compares against the graph config before any copy is permitted.

nodes.name: promote
nodes.summary: Performs the guarded promotion: refuses on a project-id mismatch or a missing staging tree, backs up every canonical file it is about to overwrite, copies the staged output into place when applying, and writes the promote record.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line front end: parses the graph config path and the `--apply` flag, runs the promotion, and maps a fail-closed refusal to a non-zero exit code.

nodes.name: prose_detect.py
nodes.summary: Detection pass of the project's proposal prose profile: it measures human-facing text against the profile's mechanical rules — sentence length, em-dash count, clause-versus-list semicolons, paragraph length and a watch-word list — over every string value in a proposal-section JSON. It reports only and never edits; the edit pass is a separate, human-reviewed step.
nodes.languageNotes: A deliberately advisory tool: it reports enumeration exceptions and list punctuation rather than ruling on them, because the prose profile is an execution aid under the constitution's skill clause and a human makes the call.

nodes.name: split_sentences
nodes.summary: Splits text into sentences while protecting a fixed list of abbreviations from being mistaken for sentence ends.

nodes.name: iter_json_strings
nodes.summary: Walks a proposal-section JSON artifact and yields every string value, ignoring keys, so the linter measures prose wherever it is nested in the structure.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point: reads the target artifact, applies each mechanical rule to the extracted prose, and prints the per-rule findings and watch-word counts as a report.

layers.name: Constitution & Project Root
layers.description: The repository constitution (CLAUDE.md) — the highest interpretive authority above every prompt, skill, workflow and agent instruction — together with the project build and dependency metadata that defines the package.

layers.name: Workflow Specification Spine
layers.description: The declarative binding authority under .claude/workflows/system_orchestration: the compiled manifest that binds nodes to agents, skills, gate conditions and deterministic components, the agent and skill catalogues, the gate rules library, the eight per-phase node specs with their Phase-8 substeps, and the artifact schema specification with its 22 canonical artifact schemas.

layers.name: Orchestration Runtime Stack
layers.description: The three-layer execution stack with exactly one caller each — DAGScheduler dispatching nodes, run_agent() sequencing a node body, run_skill() invoking Claude — plus the CLI entry point, manifest and node resolution, run-context persistence, runtime result contracts, the Step-0 call slicer and the Phase-8 reuse, preseed and skip-binding resolvers.

layers.name: Gate Evaluation
layers.description: Gate machinery owned exclusively by the scheduler: the gate evaluator (the single code-level caller of evaluate_gate), the gate rule library, the gate result registry, and the ten modules of atomic predicates that decide coverage, criteria, cycles, files, schemas, source refs, timelines and upstream gate passes.

layers.name: Deterministic Components
layers.description: Claude-free, node-body-scoped passes that read declared artifacts and write canonical ones under a byte-equal-replay or pure-lookup guarantee — distinct in kind from skills, which are defined by invoking a model: the component binding substrate plus the section assembler, assumption applier, canonical-pack deriver, unit-cost budget deriver, budget request builder, dependency normaliser, consortium-composition evaluator, instrument profile resolver, checkpoint publisher and the DOCX and final-export writers.

layers.name: Model Transport
layers.description: The transport boundary to the language model: the shared claude_transport adapter driving the local claude CLI in TAPM and cli-prompt modes, alternative Bedrock and OpenAI-compatible backends, transport configuration and capability negotiation, the tool-executor and tool loop, and the non-repairing JSON response extractor.

layers.name: Graph Substrate
layers.description: The deliberately programme-agnostic knowledge-graph layer: the bidirectional Obsidian-vault to docs/ compiler and projector pair, the claim verifier and determinism-check auditors, the graph schema and config, the vault reader and scaffold, the dev_graph package that builds revisions, impact, packages and shadow snapshots over the repository own artifacts, and the agnosticism lint that proves no project vocabulary leaks in.

layers.name: Shared Foundation
layers.description: Low-level primitives every other layer rests on, led by atomic_write (33 importers) and paths (17): atomic artifact writing, canonical path resolution, version and upstream-input resolution, the diagnostic persistence policy, the shared working-assumptions reader, the four-value Confirmed/Inferred/Assumed/Unresolved status vocabulary, content fingerprinting for gate staleness, the Tier 3 source-index verifier and the anonymity leakage scan.

layers.name: Evaluation Harness
layers.description: The out-of-band QA track behind a strict one-way boundary — it reads engine artifacts and imports runner, and the engine never imports it, with zero runner-to-harness edges in the graph: verdict, provenance, routing and judge substrate, coverage, grounding, faithfulness and contradiction graders, the claim ledger, evidence packs, calibration and regression machinery, the blind pre-evaluation lane, CLI command drivers, and the per-instrument rubric, scorecard, profile and gold-set assets. Its results are advisory and never run-blocking.

layers.name: Operator Tooling
layers.description: Standalone operator scripts that import the engine but are never imported by it: dev-graph and Part B candidate builders, run phase-cost derivation, run-manifest preservation, a gate-result schema_id backfill, graph staging promotion and the prose detector.

tour.title: The Constitution
tour.description: Start here, and do not treat this file as a README. By its own Section 1, CLAUDE.md is the highest interpretive authority in the repository, ranking above every prompt, skill, workflow and agent instruction; it defines a ten-level authority hierarchy, a six-tier document model (Tier 1 normative framework through Tier 5 deliverables), the eight gated workflow phases, and twelve categories of constitutionally forbidden action. Its governing idea is that the system must prefer an explicit, honest gate failure over fabricated completion. Nothing else in the codebase makes sense before you have internalised that, because almost every design decision downstream exists to enforce a clause written here.
tour.languageLesson: Markdown as a governance artifact, not documentation: this file is the single highest-fan-out document in the graph (24 'documents' edges), meaning the analyzer found two dozen code and config files whose behaviour is directly traceable to clauses in it. When prose governs code, section numbers (§8.4, §17.5.3) become the stable identifiers that code comments and gate messages cite.

tour.title: The CLI Entry Point
tour.description: runner/__main__.py is where execution actually begins, invoked as `python -m runner`. It parses the run-scoping flags (--run-id, --phase, --node, --dry-run), loads the compiled manifest, and hands control to the scheduler — and that is deliberately all it does. Reading it tells you the engine's real interface is a scoped run over a declared graph of phases, not a script with a sequence of steps.

tour.title: The Scheduler and Node Dispatch
tour.description: The DAGScheduler is the top layer of the runtime stack and the largest module in the repository. It builds a read-only ManifestGraph from the compiled manifest and dispatches each node through a fixed five-step contract: set state to running, evaluate the entry gate, execute the node body, evaluate the exit gate, return a composite result. Study the contract alongside runtime_models.py, which holds the frozen dataclasses passed between layers, and run_context.py, which persists node state and HARD_BLOCK metadata to disk under .claude/runs/<run_id>/ — because the constitution requires that durable state, not agent memory, be the record of what happened.
tour.languageLesson: Python frozen dataclasses as inter-layer contracts: making SkillResult, AgentResult and NodeExecutionResult immutable means a lower layer cannot mutate a result after a higher layer has read it. The closed `failure_origin` enum ('entry_gate', 'agent_body', 'exit_gate') is what lets failures be classified exactly once rather than interpreted twice.

tour.title: The Agent Runtime
tour.description: run_agent() is the middle layer, and the thing to notice is what it is forbidden to do. It loads agent and prompt specifications, resolves canonical tier inputs, sequences skill invocations, and determines can_evaluate_exit_gate by inspecting actual files on disk — but it never calls the gate evaluator and never calls the scheduler. Each layer in this stack has exactly one caller; that is enforced architecture, not a stylistic convention, and the node_resolver supplies the canonical node identity the agent runtime works against.

tour.title: The Skill Runtime
tour.description: run_skill() is the bottom orchestration layer and the only place a skill specification becomes an actual model invocation. It loads a skill .md file, resolves declared inputs, assembles a prompt in one of two modes — TAPM, where Claude reads inputs from disk itself, or cli-prompt, where inputs are serialized — parses and validates the JSON response, then writes the artifact. Pair it with call_slicer.py, the deterministic Step-0 pass that shrinks a 338-794 KB work-programme file to a bounded ~5-10 KB call slice before any model is invoked at all.
tour.languageLesson: A critical design rule lives here: the runtime must never silently repair a malformed model response. A missing run_id or an incorrect schema_id is a validation failure, not an auto-correctable condition. This is why json_extract.py competes candidate JSON spans rather than trusting the first fenced block it sees.

tour.title: The Model Transport Boundary
tour.description: Every Claude invocation in the system funnels through claude_transport.py, which subprocesses the local `claude` CLI in print mode and reassembles the reply from a multi-turn streaming format. Isolating the model behind one adapter is what made the migration from API-key billing to a subscription CLI a transport-layer change with no effect on workflow logic, gates or schemas. The runner/transport/ package generalises this further with a tool loop for backends lacking native Read/Glob support, plus typed transport errors so a timeout is distinguishable from an unavailable CLI.

tour.title: Gates Are the Point
tour.description: This is the conceptual heart of the engine. gate_evaluator.py resolves a gate's predicates, runs each one deterministically, and writes the gate result — and it is called only by the scheduler, never by an agent or a skill. Note the inversion a newcomer always gets backwards: the manifest_reader exposes each gate's predicate_refs, and under 'Approach B' a predicate executes only if the manifest names it, so the predicate library is merely an implementation registry. A gate failure here is a correct and valuable output, not a bug to route around.

tour.title: The Predicate Modules
tour.description: Gates decompose into atomic, deterministic predicates spread across ten modules in runner/predicates/, covering file existence, schema conformance, coverage, criterion binding, timelines, source references and DAG cycles. Every one of them returns the same PredicateResult type with one of five canonical failure categories — the uniform shape is what lets the evaluator aggregate 149 declared predicates without knowing what any individual check means. The YAML library declares each predicate's id, evaluation function, args, prose condition and the operator-facing message shown when it fails.
tour.languageLesson: A barrel __init__.py re-exporting every predicate gives the evaluator one flat namespace to resolve names against, while keeping each predicate family in its own file. In Python this pattern trades a little import opacity for a stable public surface that a YAML registry can safely reference by bare name.

tour.title: The YAML Spine Governs the Python
tour.description: If you read only Python you will conclude the engine is self-describing. It is not. manifest.compile.yaml is the executable spine: a node_registry of 13 phase nodes binding each to its agents, skills, gate conditions and deterministic components, plus the gate_registry that decides which predicates run. It has zero import edges yet sources the largest cross-category relation in the whole graph (79 'configures' edges). The agent catalog declares each of the 20 agents' tier reads, writes and explicit must_not prohibitions; the artifact schema specification fixes the field-level shape of every Tier 4 and Tier 5 artifact the code is allowed to write.
tour.languageLesson: YAML as a binding manifest rather than a settings file. The 'compile' in manifest.compile.yaml signals a derived artifact: per-phase node specs under workflow_phases/ are the authored sources, and the compiled manifest is the single file the runtime reads. Edit the source, recompile — never patch the compiled spine directly.

tour.title: Skills vs Deterministic Components
tour.description: This distinction unlocks the whole design. A skill invokes Claude and performs domain reasoning; a deterministic component invokes no model, makes no inference, and is closed by a byte-equal-replay or pure-lookup guarantee. deterministic_components.py is the generic binding substrate dispatching 17 of them, and section_assembler.py shows the flavour: it array-appends per-sub-section drafts in spine order, carrying claims verbatim and deriving exactly two things — word counts and a de-duplicated union of source refs. Components are bound in the manifest just like skills, but they are not skills, and keeping that line sharp is what preserves the guarantee that only reasoning steps can introduce new content.

tour.title: The Budget Gate: Fail-Closed in Full
tour.description: Read these two phase specs as a pair — they are the sharpest illustration of the engine's philosophy. gate_09 categorically blocks every Phase 8 activity, including preparatory drafting, until a complete and structurally consistent budget exists; for lump-sum instruments that means a validated response from an external planner, because lump-sum figures carry judgment that cannot be replayed. unit_cost_budget.py is the instructive counter-case: it derives a unit-cost budget as fixed arithmetic on published constants (confirmed months x published rates x host coefficient), verified by byte-equal replay, which is precisely why determinism is permitted to substitute for the external-system guarantee. working_assumptions.py is the only sanctioned escape hatch — the mechanism by which a human operator, not an agent, converts an honest block into a declared assumption.
tour.languageLesson: The anti-fabrication argument is worth following precisely: externalisation and determinism are alternative guarantees against the same risk. Where a number requires judgment, push it outside the system; where it is pure arithmetic on published constants, prove it by replaying the computation and comparing bytes. Either way, no layer is ever allowed to estimate.

tour.title: The Graph Substrate
tour.description: runner/dev_graph/ is a rebuildable operational index over the repository's authoritative records — it owns nothing, and rebuilding from the same records is byte-identical. schema.py holds the closed vocabularies as data: the node types and the relationship set, each relationship declaring its permitted endpoint pairs. Alongside it, graph_compiler.py extracts Tier 3 inputs and Part B deliverables from an Obsidian vault into a staging tree (diffing rather than overwriting the hand-lift), graph_projector.py mirrors durable run state back into the vault, and graph_determinism_check.py proves the compiler is a pure function by compiling twice and comparing bytes.
tour.languageLesson: Content-addressed snapshots make 'has anything really changed?' a byte comparison instead of a judgement call. The pattern's one concession is a documented exclusion — a timestamp field like compiled_at is explicitly exempted from the byte-equality check, because otherwise determinism could never be demonstrated at all.

tour.title: The Out-of-Band Harness
tour.description: harness/ is a quality-assurance track, not part of the engine, and the boundary runs one way only: the harness may read engine artifacts and import runner modules, while the engine never imports the harness — the dependency graph contains zero such edges. HARNESS.md is its own specification, defining the substrate and its headline signals (status-aware faithfulness, rubric grading), and its verdicts are advisory and never run-blocking. verdict.py and judge.py are its most-imported internals, mirroring atomic_write's role on the engine side.
tour.languageLesson: A one-way import boundary is an architectural invariant you can actually test: assert that no module under runner/ imports harness/, and the rule stops depending on reviewer discipline. Declaring it in the package's __init__ docstring makes the intent discoverable at the point someone would be tempted to break it.

tour.title: The Shared Foundation
tour.description: Finish at the deepest sinks in the dependency graph, which are also the smallest modules. atomic_write.py has 33 importers: every deterministic component and exporter publishes canonical artifacts through its temp-file-plus-rename helpers, so a crashed run can never leave a half-written artifact that a gate would then read as complete. paths.py, with 17 importers, discovers the repository root by finding an ancestor holding both CLAUDE.md and .git/ — the constitution is literally the filesystem anchor. pyproject.toml closes the loop, carrying only pytest configuration plus the two markers that register the harness's lanes as explicitly non-blocking.
tour.languageLesson: Atomic writes via os.replace() on a same-filesystem temp file are the standard way to make a file update all-or-nothing on POSIX and Windows alike. In a gated system this is not a nicety: gate predicates decide pass or fail by inspecting files on disk, so a partially written artifact would be indistinguishable from a genuinely incomplete one.
